These examples express different design intentions. The first intentionally fades the whole surface. The second keeps the label fully opaque while allowing the surrounding background to contribute to the card’s appearance. They are not intended to produce matching pixels.

Reference: MDN: opacity and compositing.

Inspect the surface underneath

An alpha color does not have one final appearance independent of its backdrop. Compare the card over the actual light, dark or image surface where it will be used. Check the rendered text/background pair rather than calculating contrast against the uncomposited blue alone.

If a photograph is involved, review both bright and dark regions behind the label. A separate solid text surface or stronger overlay may produce a more dependable result than a subtle tint. Record the backdrop together with any approved color value.

Review what a faded element can still do

  • Check whether an opacity-zero control remains focusable or clickable.
  • Confirm disabled appearance is paired with the intended native behavior.
  • Inspect stacking when opacity is less than 1.
  • Test text and icons in hover, focus and selected states.

Opacity changes appearance; it is not a general interaction switch. If the card should become unavailable, choose the appropriate semantic behavior independently. For a token library, distinguish a translucent surface color from a component opacity value in the token names and usage notes. That prevents a designer’s “soft background” request from unexpectedly weakening every label and focus indicator inside it.
coverAlt: A group-faded card has muted text while a translucent background card retains dark opaque text; the two examples have different intended appearances.

title: Use CSS Hyphenation with the Correct Content Language
description: Improve narrow text columns with hyphens and accurate lang attributes. Check dictionary availability, editorial exceptions and long identifiers separately.
body:
Automatic hyphenation can help ordinary prose fit a narrow column without treating every word like a machine-generated string. The browser needs the text’s language to choose appropriate hyphenation rules. Start with accurate language markup, then review the result using real editorial copy.

Apply a language-aware prose rule

<article lang="en-US" class="narrow-notes">
  <p>Documentation should remain readable in a narrow reference panel.</p>
</article>
.narrow-notes {
  max-inline-size: 30ch;
  hyphens: auto;
}

The width is an illustrative test condition. Automatic break opportunities depend on the browser’s language resources and implementation, so the same paragraph may wrap differently on another system. A correct lang attribute also helps other language-sensitive features; do not choose it merely to force a preferred visual break.

Reference: MDN: hyphens.

Separate prose from exact identifiers

A URL, order identifier or code token has different reading requirements from an ordinary word. Hyphenation is not a universal overflow repair for those values. Use a deliberate wrapping policy for identifiers, and verify that copying the value preserves its original content.

.narrow-notes code { hyphens: none; }

For an exceptional editorial word, a soft hyphen can mark a preferred discretionary break. Use that sparingly: a document full of manually inserted opportunities becomes hard to maintain when wording or fonts change. Never rewrite the spelling simply to improve one screenshot.

Compare actual reading conditions

  • Test the final web font and its fallback.
  • Resize the text column across the intended range.
  • Review proper names and specialist vocabulary with an editor.
  • Check mixed-language passages using their own language attributes.

A narrow column may need a wider layout or different typography rather than increasingly aggressive breaks. Inspect repeated hyphenated endings across several consecutive lines and whether the words remain easy to scan. In the design handoff, state the content language, where automatic hyphenation is allowed, and which content types are exempt. Avoid promising identical line endings across browsers.
coverAlt: A narrow prose specimen illustrates a discretionary hyphenated line ending alongside an en-US language label and a browser-dictionary reminder.

title: Keep Fallback Text Legible with font-size-adjust
description: Evaluate a fallback font’s apparent size with font-size-adjust. Choose a deliberate metric, test wrapping and distinguish it from changing the declared font size.
body:
Two fonts at the same CSS font size can have noticeably different lowercase heights. font-size-adjust can help maintain an intended apparent text size when a fallback face is used. It does not make two typefaces identical, and it should be evaluated with the real font stack.

Build a controlled fallback specimen

.reading-sample {
  font-family: "Project Sans", Arial, sans-serif;
  font-size: 1rem;
  line-height: 1.6;
  font-size-adjust: .5;
}

Project Sans is a placeholder for your actual loaded font. The .5 value is an illustrative target ratio, not a measured recommendation for your brand. The ordinary numeric form uses the lowercase x-height metric relative to font size. Measure or evaluate the chosen typeface before selecting a production value.

Reference: MDN: font-size-adjust.

Compare the same paragraph twice

Create a short specimen containing lowercase letters, capitals, digits and punctuation. Use the same container width in both views. First inspect the intended web font, then deliberately select the fallback in DevTools. Record apparent lowercase size, line count and the position of the next component.

Test with adjustment enabled and disabled. Prefer the result that keeps the fallback readable without creating cramped lines or surprising wraps. The acceptance decision should include several paragraphs, not only a large “Aa” specimen that hides ordinary reading problems.

Keep the metric adjustment separate from other repairs

  • Verify the font request and the rendered face before tuning metrics.
  • Check a narrow card and the main reading column.
  • Review punctuation, accents and supported scripts.
  • Confirm enlarged text has enough line and component space.

If the chosen font never loads, fix that delivery problem independently. If a button has a fixed height, review the component constraint before attributing clipped text to the adjustment. Keep a small before-and-after specimen in the handoff, with the font names, declared size and chosen ratio. Report observed wrapping changes honestly; this property alone does not establish that layout shift has been eliminated.
coverAlt: Two illustrative lowercase specimens compare smaller and adjusted apparent letter height, without claiming measurements for a named font.

title: Preserve Line Breaks Without Forcing Horizontal Scrolling
description: Choose pre-wrap or pre-line for text with intentional newlines. Test spaces, tabs and long strings while keeping user-entered text out of unsafe HTML rendering.
keyword: white space pre wrap vs pre line
body:
Text copied from notes or logs often contains intentional line breaks. Normal whitespace handling collapses those breaks during rendering. white-space: pre-wrap preserves spaces and newlines while allowing wrapping; pre-line preserves line breaks but collapses sequences of spaces. Choose based on which formatting carries meaning.

Use a text specimen with deliberate formatting

<pre class="review-log">Header review
  Navigation: checked
  Footer: needs another pass</pre>
.review-log {
  white-space: pre-wrap;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
  tab-size: 2;
  font: 1rem/1.6 monospace;
}

This example preserves indentation while allowing long content to wrap. The additional overflow-wrap policy is for unexpected unbroken strings; it is separate from preserving whitespace. tab-size affects actual tab characters, not the two spaces written in this example.

Reference: MDN: white-space.

Choose whether indentation matters

For ordinary user notes where multiple spaces are accidental, pre-line may produce a cleaner display. For code or aligned logs, collapsing spaces can destroy useful relationships. If exact columns matter, consider a scrollable preformatted region instead of soft wrapping, and make that region accessible to keyboard users.

.plain-notes { white-space: pre-line; }

Do not use a preformatted layout to simulate a real data table when the rows and columns need semantic relationships. Whitespace alignment can fail as fonts, content lengths or screen sizes change.

Treat input as text, then review the result

  • Include empty lines, leading spaces and a long URL in the specimen.
  • Test a narrow screen and enlarged text.
  • Copy the displayed text back into a plain-text editor.
  • Check whether wrapped continuation lines are visually distinguishable from actual new lines.

When displaying untrusted notes, insert them as text through your framework’s normal escaping or textContent. Preserving whitespace is not a reason to inject the input as HTML. Document the chosen behavior with a small sample containing visible indentation and a long line, so the difference between formatting preservation and overflow handling is easy to verify.
coverAlt: A notes panel preserves newlines and indented status lines, with labels separating whitespace preservation from long-string wrapping.

title: Use ch Units for a Readable Text Measure
description: Set a flexible reading width with ch while understanding what the unit measures. Review real text, font changes and padding instead of assuming an exact character count.
body:
A ch-based maximum can make a reading column follow its typography more naturally than a fixed pixel width. However, 60ch does not mean every line will contain exactly sixty characters. The unit is based on the font’s zero glyph, and proportional letters have different widths.

Constrain the measure without fixing the viewport

.reading-column {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  inline-size: 100%;
  max-inline-size: 64ch;
  margin-inline: auto;
  padding-inline: 1rem;
}

This is a starting specimen, not a universal reading-width target. Border-box includes the horizontal padding inside the maximum, so the actual text area is narrower than 64ch. Decide whether your design token describes the outer container or the content measure.

Reference: MDN: font-relative length units.

Compare representative paragraphs

Use one paragraph of ordinary prose, one with technical terms and one containing links or inline code. Measure how comfortably the eye returns to the next line. Compare the same samples with the final web font and its fallback; changing the zero glyph’s width changes the unit’s physical size.

A monospace sample may look closer to an exact character count, but spaces, punctuation, writing direction and the chosen content still deserve review. Do not infer the measure of an entire design system from a single short sentence.

Check the container in its actual context

  • Place the column beside a sidebar as well as on its own.
  • Increase browser text size and inspect surrounding controls.
  • Test long headings independently from the paragraph measure.
  • Review the narrowest supported viewport for excess side padding.

If the layout uses a maximum page width as well, identify which constraint wins at each breakpoint. A small content column inside a large page shell can be deliberate. Keep the shell width and reading measure as different roles in the handoff. That allows a future font change to be reviewed as a typography decision without accidentally redefining the entire page grid.
coverAlt: A centered paragraph column is marked with a 64ch outer maximum and separate side padding, with a reminder that ch is not an exact character count.

title: Mark the Current Navigation Page with aria-current
description: Pair a visible active-link style with aria-current="page". Keep navigation semantics, route matching and keyboard focus separate from selected tab behavior.
body:
A navigation menu should identify the current page beyond a color change. aria-current="page" gives that relationship to assistive technology while ordinary link markup preserves navigation behavior. Use it for the page currently represented in the menu, and update it when the route changes.

Keep the current item a recognizable link

<nav aria-label="Project">
  <a href="/overview/">Overview</a>
  <a href="/files/" aria-current="page">Files</a>
  <a href="/settings/">Settings</a>
</nav>
nav a[aria-current="page"] {
  font-weight: 700;
  text-decoration: underline;
  text-underline-offset: .25em;
}

The paths are examples. A weight and underline cue makes the state visible without relying solely on color. Preserve a separate focus indicator; a link being current does not mean it currently has keyboard focus.

Reference: MDN: aria-current.

Define current within each navigation set

Usually one item in a related set is current. A page may contain separate navigation contexts, such as a main menu and breadcrumbs, each representing the same current location. Evaluate each set rather than removing every repeated current marker across the entire document.

A tab widget has its own selected-tab semantics and keyboard interaction. Do not replace aria-selected with aria-current simply because both designs use an active-looking underline. A multi-step process can use a different current value, such as step, when that is the relationship being conveyed.

Verify the route matching rule

  • Load the page directly rather than only following the menu.
  • Navigate between sibling pages and confirm the marker moves.
  • Check nested routes and trailing slashes.
  • Inspect the current-link announcement and visible focus independently.

Avoid a broad string match that marks both /files/ and /files/archive/ as separate current pages in the same set. Decide whether a parent section should be visually highlighted while the exact page is marked current, and express those as separate rules. Include direct-load and client-side navigation cases in the handoff so the marker does not become stale after a route transition.
coverAlt: A navigation row underlines the Files link and identifies it with aria-current page while the other links remain ordinary destinations.

title: disabled vs readonly: Choose the Right Form Behavior
description: Compare focus, editing and submission for unavailable form fields. Keep read-only values available when needed and verify what the server actually receives.
body:
Use readonly when a supported field should remain available for reading and copying but not editing. Use disabled when a control is unavailable. The difference affects focus and form submission, not just styling, so replacing one with the other can change the data the application receives.

Compare two labeled text fields

<form>
  <label for="reference">Reference code</label>
  <input id="reference" name="reference" value="SAMPLE-042" readonly>

  <label for="coupon">Coupon code — unavailable for this order</label>
  <input id="coupon" name="coupon" value="" disabled>
</form>

The reference is sample data. The read-only field can normally receive focus and its named value is included in form data. The disabled field is excluded. Test the actual form serialization rather than assuming both visible values are submitted.

Reference: MDN: readonly.

Reference: MDN: disabled.

Match the attribute to the control type

readonly applies to supported textual inputs and textarea, not to every form control. Adding it to a select or checkbox does not create a read-only version of that control. If someone only needs to see a final value, ordinary text may be a clearer representation than an inactive control.

Both attributes are Boolean: writing disabled="false" still leaves the attribute present and therefore active. Use the DOM property or remove the attribute to change the state. Review constraint validation as well; these states are not equivalent to an editable required field.

Test the intended task

  • Tab through the form and verify which fields can receive focus.
  • Try copying a reference value with the keyboard.
  • Inspect submitted FormData in a controlled test.
  • Enable an unavailable control and confirm its value and validation behavior.

Explain why an important control is unavailable using visible supporting text, especially when it cannot receive focus to reveal help. Neither attribute is an authorization boundary: submitted values can be altered outside the normal interface. The server must validate what it accepts. Document the display state, editability, focus behavior and submission rule together so the visual treatment does not conceal a data-flow change.
coverAlt: A read-only reference code remains available to focus and submit, while a disabled coupon field is shown unavailable and excluded from submission.

title: meter vs progress: Represent a Value or a Task
description: Choose native meter or progress markup by meaning. Label the indicator, distinguish indeterminate work and keep visible values synchronized with actual state.
body:
Use meter for a measured value within a known range, such as storage usage. Use progress for how much of a task has completed. Their bars may look similar, but the meaning differs. Choose the element from the information being communicated before styling its fill.

Show a measurement with context

<label for="storage">Sample storage usage: 6 of 10 GB</label>
<meter id="storage" min="0" max="10" value="6">6 of 10 GB</meter>

The values describe an illustrative measurement, not a running upload. Keep units in the visible label because the numeric attributes do not explain what the range measures. If you add low, high or optimum thresholds, define what those thresholds mean for the real product.

Reference: MDN: meter element.

Show task completion separately

<label for="upload">Example upload: 30%</label>
<progress id="upload" max="100" value="30">30%</progress>

For a task whose completion fraction is unknown, omit value to make progress indeterminate. Setting value to 0 represents a known zero-complete state, not unknown progress. Do not manufacture percentages merely to make an indicator feel active.

Reference: MDN: progress element.

Review labels, updates and outcomes

  • Check the accessible name and value for each indicator.
  • Keep the visible status text in sync with the attributes.
  • Test indeterminate, active, failed and completed task states.
  • Verify meaning remains understandable without the bar’s color.

A progress bar does not explain a failure or tell someone how to retry. Pair it with accurate task status and a recovery action where needed. If completion deserves an announcement, use a concise status update rather than announcing every percentage change as an urgent alert.

Inspect the native appearance in supported browsers before replacing it with complex custom visuals. A simple indicator with a clear label and accurate state is easier to verify than a decorative animation pretending to represent measured progress. Include the range, units, source of values and completion behavior in the component specification.
coverAlt: A storage meter is filled to six of ten gigabytes, while a separate task progress indicator is filled to thirty percent.

title: Give a Native Range Input a Clear Label and Value
description: Build a labeled range control with explicit bounds and a visible value. Review keyboard changes, step size and whether a slider is appropriate for precise entry.
keyword: html range input label output value
body:
A range input works well for adjusting a bounded value when sliding is a useful interaction. Give it a visible label, explicit bounds and a meaningful step. If the task requires exact typed values, consider a numeric entry field instead of expecting everyone to place a slider precisely.

Expose the chosen value

<label for="preview-scale">Preview scale</label>
<input id="preview-scale" type="range" min="50" max="150"
       step="10" value="100" aria-describedby="scale-value">
<span id="scale-value">100%</span>
const scale = document.querySelector("#preview-scale");
const value = document.querySelector("#scale-value");
scale.addEventListener("input", () => {
  value.textContent = `${scale.value}%`;
});

This specimen updates a visible value only; connect it to the actual preview behavior separately. The span avoids introducing another live region for every small movement. Test whether the described value gives useful context without repetitive announcements in your supported screen readers.

Reference: MDN: range input.

Choose bounds from the task

The sample permits values from 50 to 150 in increments of 10. Those values are illustrative. A coarse step may be fine for a preview but unsuitable for an exact measurement. Explain the unit and useful range near the control rather than relying on the thumb’s position.

Keep the native keyboard interaction unless there is a specific, tested reason to change it. Do not attach custom arrow-key handlers that accidentally double the increment or prevent ordinary navigation. If the displayed meaning is nonnumeric, evaluate aria-valuetext with the real assistive-technology behavior.

Review precision and input methods

  • Reach the control with Tab and adjust it with arrow keys.
  • Test the minimum and maximum values.
  • Use touch at the smallest supported viewport.
  • Check that changing the value does not unexpectedly move focus or navigate away.

A visible value is particularly useful when thumb position alone is ambiguous. Keep it synchronized from one state source rather than calculating a separate display value. Record the bounds, step, unit and timing of the effect in handoff notes, including whether the expensive preview update occurs during movement or after adjustment.
coverAlt: A preview-scale range control spans fifty to one hundred fifty percent with its thumb centered at one hundred percent and a visible value.

title: Add a Caption Track to an HTML Video
description: Connect a WebVTT caption file to a video, verify timing and labels, and review native player controls. Distinguish captions from subtitles and transcripts.
body:
A caption track can make spoken content and meaningful audio information available as synchronized text. For a native HTML video player, provide a WebVTT file through track. The markup connects the resource; accurate captions still require editing, timing review and a working player control.

Connect a labeled caption resource

<video controls preload="metadata" width="960" height="540">
  <source src="/media/review-demo.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <track kind="captions" src="/media/review-demo.en.vtt"
         srclang="en" label="English" default>
</video>

These are example paths and dimensions for assets you must supply. Use the actual video dimensions. Captions include relevant speech and non-speech audio, while a subtitle track serves a different language-support purpose. Select the track kind based on its actual contents.

Reference: MDN: track element.

Write a small WebVTT specimen

WEBVTT

00:00:01.000 --> 00:00:03.500
Open the spacing panel.

00:00:04.000 --> 00:00:06.000
[Notification sound]

These cues are illustrative, not a transcript of an existing recording. Begin the real file with the WebVTT header, use valid cue times and serve it as text/vtt. Check its network response; a successful video request does not establish that the caption file loaded.

Watch with audio muted

  • Turn the track on and off using the player’s controls.
  • Verify cue timing, spelling, speaker changes and meaningful sounds.
  • Check that text remains readable on a narrow screen.
  • Navigate player controls with the keyboard and inspect their labels.

Host the track with an appropriate same-origin or correctly configured cross-origin setup. A console or network error is more useful evidence than repeatedly changing the label. Test the deployed page, because local files may not reproduce the production delivery rules.

Captions do not automatically explain meaningful visual actions that are never spoken. Review whether the recording also needs audio description or an equivalent explanation, and offer a transcript when useful for scanning. Keep the caption file version aligned with the video: editing the recording can invalidate every later cue even when the old file still loads.
coverAlt: A native-style video preview shows an example caption below a simple panel demonstration, with the English caption track identified.

title: Find the Cause Behind a Layout Shift
description: Trace a moving element back to the content that displaced it. Reproduce late images, banners and font changes, then verify a targeted layout-stability repair.
body:
The element that moves during a layout shift is not always the element that caused it. A paragraph may jump because an image, banner or newly inserted panel above it changed size. Start from a repeatable recording and trace the space change before applying a fixed height to the moving text.

Record the moment and its context

  • Open the page with consistent viewport and network conditions.
  • Record a load or the interaction that reveals the movement.
  • Inspect the layout-shift entry and its affected elements in browser performance tools.
  • Compare the frames immediately before and after the shift.

Record whether the issue occurs on initial load, after scrolling or during an interaction. A single clean reload does not rule out a shift that happens later. Keep the affected region, triggering event and suspected size change together in your notes.

Reference: web.dev: optimize Cumulative Layout Shift.

Reserve the space you actually know

<img src="/images/sample-panel.webp"
     width="1200" height="630"
     alt="A sample panel with its spacing annotations">
.article-figure img {
  max-inline-size: 100%;
  block-size: auto;
}

The asset path is illustrative. Dimensions must match the real image’s ratio so the browser can reserve useful space. If a responsive source changes composition and ratio, review that selection separately. Adding arbitrary dimensions can create a different mismatch when the media arrives.

Follow the cause beyond images

For a late banner, decide whether space should be reserved or whether the information belongs in an existing region. For a font change, compare the real and fallback metrics. For expanding user content, review whether the transition is expected and whether it displaces the current reading position.

  • Repeat the same recording after the targeted repair.
  • Check long content and narrower viewports.
  • Review later interactions rather than only the initial load.
  • Compare field evidence when available with controlled lab observations.

Do not hide a moving paragraph or lock it to a height that clips content just to improve one recording. A useful fix preserves the content and removes an avoidable surprise. Report the measured result with its test conditions; a screenshot of a stable frame is not evidence that the entire page has no layout shifts.
coverAlt: Before and after page sketches show text moving down when an unreserved image appears, with an arrow identifying the inserted media as the cause.

title: Audit HTML Headings Without Changing the Design
description: Check heading levels, section relationships and reusable card titles. Repair the document outline while preserving the typography your design already uses.
body:
Audit headings by reading their text and levels in document order, then comparing that outline with the page’s actual sections. A large bold paragraph is not a semantic heading. Conversely, a real heading can use restrained typography without losing its role.

Write the outline before changing tags

For a fictional export settings page, the outline could be: Export settings, File format, Image options, and Color profile. The first is the page title; File format and Image options are sibling sections; Color profile belongs inside Image options. This gives the section relationships a concrete meaning before CSS enters the discussion.

<h1>Export settings</h1>
<h2>File format</h2>
<!-- Format controls -->
<h2>Image options</h2>
<h3>Color profile</h3>
<!-- Profile controls -->

Use browser inspection to list the actual h1–h6 elements. Look for a section that jumps from h2 to h4, a card title marked up as a paragraph, or repeated navigation text that appears as a heading for no structural reason. Returning from h3 to h2 simply closes a subsection; that is different from skipping a level while opening one.

Reference: W3C WAI guidance on heading ranks.

Separate heading rank from type size

.page-title { font-size: clamp(2rem, 5vw, 3.5rem); }
.section-title { font-size: 1.5rem; }
.card-title { font-size: 1.125rem; }

Choose the element from the content hierarchy and the class from the visual role. If a reusable card appears under an h2 on one page and an h3 on another, let its component accept the appropriate heading level. Do not hard-code h4 just because the card title looks small.

A single clear main h1 is a useful convention for this page. Do not treat counting h1 elements as a complete audit, or claim that changing the count alone will improve rankings. The labels and nesting need to describe the content.

Review the outline with real page states

  • Read only the heading text: does it explain the page without the surrounding paragraphs?
  • Open optional sections and check headings inserted by the application.
  • Inspect desktop and mobile layouts for duplicated hidden headings.
  • Navigate by headings with a screen reader and confirm the sequence is useful.

Record the old tag, proposed tag and section relationship in the review. Keep visual adjustments separate so a semantic fix does not accidentally redesign the interface. For long section titles, review heading wrapping after the hierarchy is correct.
coverAlt: A page outline shows one main heading, two sibling section headings and a nested subsection with increasing indentation.

title: Use HTML Landmarks and Name Multiple Navigation Regions
description: Organize a page with main, nav, header and footer. Give distinct navigation regions useful names and verify the resulting accessibility tree.
body:
Use native HTML landmarks to expose the major regions of a page, then give repeated regions distinct names when their purposes differ. A reader should be able to find the main content or a particular navigation group without stepping through every link.

Map the page’s major regions

<header>
  <a href="/">Example workspace</a>
  <nav aria-label="Primary">...</nav>
</header>
<nav aria-label="Project">...</nav>
<main id="main-content">
  <h1>Project overview</h1>
  <!-- The unique content for this page -->
</main>
<footer>...</footer>

In this example, Primary contains site-wide destinations while Project contains links for the selected project. Keep one visible main region for the page. A site-level header and footer provide different context from a header nested inside an article; the nested header is not automatically a site-wide banner landmark.

Reference: W3C WAI page regions tutorial.

Give names that describe the destination group

Prefer “Project” and “Primary” over “Navigation 1” and “Navigation 2.” Assistive technology can already announce the navigation role, so repeating that word in every name is usually unnecessary. If a visible heading names the region, connect it with aria-labelledby instead of maintaining a second label that can drift out of date.

<nav aria-labelledby="resources-title">
  <h2 id="resources-title">Resources</h2>
  <ul>
    <li><a href="/guides/">Guides</a></li>
    <li><a href="/support/">Support</a></li>
  </ul>
</nav>

Do not turn every card and decorative wrapper into a named region. A crowded landmark list makes the major boundaries harder to locate. For the example page, write down what a user would accomplish by jumping to each proposed landmark; remove regions that have no useful answer.

Inspect the result, not just the tags

  • Check the accessibility tree for the expected landmark roles and names.
  • Open the mobile menu and confirm hidden desktop navigation does not remain available unexpectedly.
  • Navigate by landmarks with a screen reader, then use the links inside each region.
  • Follow the skip link and verify it reaches the intended main content.

Landmarks, heading levels and the skip-link target should describe the same page organization. If they disagree, resolve the information structure before polishing spacing. This is a navigation aid, not a replacement for meaningful headings or clear link labels.
coverAlt: A page map labels Primary navigation, Project navigation, Main content and Footer as distinct regions.

title: Button or Link? Choose by What Activation Does
description: Choose an anchor for navigation and a button for actions. Inspect keyboard behavior, real URLs and component APIs without changing the visual design.
body:
Use an anchor with a real href when activation takes the reader to a destination. Use a button when activation performs an action in the current interface. The shape, color or prominence of the control does not determine its HTML element.

Classify the behavior before the style

<a class="primary-action" href="/exports/">View exports</a>
<button class="primary-action" type="button" id="preview">
  Refresh preview
</button>

The first example has a destination that can be copied or opened in another tab. The second asks the application to do work. A shared CSS class can make both look like the same design-system control while preserving their different semantics. The example button still needs an application handler; its label alone does not implement a refresh.

Reference: MDN anchor element reference.

A download link to an existing file can also be an anchor. A control that first generates a report may be an action button, followed by a link when the file becomes available. Describe those two steps in the component specification instead of choosing an element from the word “Download” alone.

Remove placeholder navigation

An anchor with href="#" is not a good substitute for a button. It exposes a navigation target even when the intended behavior is opening a menu or copying text. Removing href also removes the normal link behavior rather than turning the anchor into a native button.

For a client-side router, preserve a real destination href and review modified clicks, browser history and loading failures. JavaScript can enhance navigation without requiring every destination to become a click handler on a generic element. Avoid placing one interactive control inside another, such as a delete button inside a fully linked card.

Test the element’s expected interaction

  • Tab to the control and check its accessible name and role.
  • Activate links with Enter and test copying or opening their destinations.
  • Activate native buttons with Enter and Space, checking that the action runs once.
  • Confirm action buttons inside forms have an intentional type.
  • Check visible focus, long labels and any resulting focus movement.

During handoff, include a behavior column beside each control: destination URL or action, loading state, and result. Review button states separately once the underlying element is correct. A screenshot can show the visual hierarchy, but it cannot establish whether the control has the right browser behavior.
coverAlt: View exports is paired with a destination URL, while Refresh preview is paired with an action, despite matching button shapes.

title: Stop Helper Buttons from Submitting a Form
description: Trace accidental submissions to a button’s type and form owner. Separate helper actions from submit controls, and test Enter-key submission deliberately.
keyword: button type button prevents form submit
body:
If a preview, reveal-password or add-row button unexpectedly submits a form, inspect its type and associated form. For an ordinary form-associated button without special command behavior, omitting type can make it a submit button. Set type="button" explicitly for a helper action and type="submit" for the intended submission control.

Make each control’s job explicit

<form id="export-settings" action="/exports" method="post">
  <label for="export-name">Export name</label>
  <input id="export-name" name="name" required>
  <button type="button" id="preview-export">Preview</button>
  <button type="submit">Create export</button>
</form>

Preview requires your application’s click handler. Create export uses the form’s submission path. This example separates the roles without globally canceling every submit event. A blanket preventDefault can hide the bug while also breaking the action users actually need.

Reference: MDN button types and form association.

Follow the form owner, including outside controls

<button type="submit" form="export-settings">
  Create export
</button>

A button outside the form can still submit it through the form attribute. Inspect the rendered DOM rather than only a component file: wrappers, portals and component defaults may change the final relationship. In DevTools, compare the button’s type and form properties with the element you intended to control.

Reproduce the bug using a harmless local form or staging environment. Add a temporary submit listener that prevents navigation and records the event’s submitter. Remove that diagnostic code afterward. Do not test a destructive production action simply to identify the element that submitted it.

Check mouse and keyboard submission separately

  • Click every helper button and confirm it performs only its own action.
  • Press Enter in a single-line field and verify the intended submit path.
  • Use Space and Enter on the focused submit button.
  • Try invalid required fields and confirm errors remain usable.
  • Check a reusable button inside and outside a form.

Enter-key implicit submission is form behavior; fixing a helper button does not mean Enter should stop working everywhere. Likewise, type="reset" is not a synonym for cancel: it resets form values and deserves an explicit product decision. Document a component default and require an intentional submit type at form boundaries so later refactors do not reintroduce the problem.
coverAlt: A form sketch separates a Preview helper button with type button from a Create export control with type submit.

title: Inputmode vs. Input Type: Pick the Right Mobile Keyboard
description: Match virtual keyboards to field data without confusing keyboard hints with validation. Use text for identifiers and test entry, paste and autofill.
body:
The input type describes the control and influences its behavior. The inputmode attribute suggests a virtual keyboard. A numeric keyboard hint does not validate the value, and it does not make a textual identifier into a number.

Decide whether the value is a quantity

A quantity such as the number of copies can reasonably use a number control. A five-digit identifier may need its leading zero preserved and has no useful increment operation. Start with the data model, then choose the keyboard. Do not use type="number" merely because a field happens to contain digits.

<label for="code">Five-digit reference code</label>
<input id="code" name="code" type="text"
  inputmode="numeric" pattern="[0-9]{5}"
  maxlength="5" aria-describedby="code-help" required>
<p id="code-help">Enter all five digits, including any leading zero.</p>

This original example deliberately accepts only five ASCII digits. It is a reference-code field, not a universal postal-code template. The pattern and required attributes express browser validation separately from the keyboard hint. The server must also validate submitted values.

Reference: MDN inputmode reference.

Choose a hint that permits the required characters

Use email and telephone input types when those are the actual data being collected. For a decimal text field, inputmode="decimal" can request a decimal separator, but available keys vary across devices and locales. Numeric or decimal keyboards may omit a minus key, so a field that accepts negative values needs a real-device check.

Think beyond typing: people may paste a value, use autofill, dictate it or connect a hardware keyboard. Instructions should describe the accepted format, and errors should explain how to correct the value. A keyboard layout is a convenience, not an input-security boundary.

Review the complete entry path

  • Enter a leading-zero value and check the value sent to the server.
  • Paste an invalid value and verify a useful error message.
  • Try an empty submission and a value that is too long.
  • Check virtual keyboards on representative iOS and Android devices.
  • Test autofill and browser back navigation without silently losing the value.

Include the field’s type, inputmode, autocomplete purpose and validation rule in the handoff. Review autocomplete tokens independently: a keyboard hint does not tell the browser which saved personal detail belongs in a field.
coverAlt: A five-digit code beginning with zero is shown above a number-keyboard diagram, with separate keyboard hint and validation labels.

title: Keep Textareas Resizable Without Breaking the Layout
description: Let users enlarge a textarea vertically while preserving the form width. Check overflow, constraints and mobile behavior before removing the resize handle.
body:
For a textarea inside a narrow form, resize: vertical can let readers expand the editing area without dragging it wider than the layout. Give the control a useful starting height and keep its content reachable even where the browser does not offer a resize handle.

Start with a flexible field

<label for="review-notes">Review notes</label>
<textarea id="review-notes" name="notes" rows="6"></textarea>
textarea {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  width: 100%;
  min-height: 8rem;
  resize: vertical;
  overflow: auto;
  font: inherit;
}

The minimum height is an example design choice. The field can grow taller, while its width follows the containing form. Border-box includes padding and borders in that width. Avoid a fixed-height parent that clips the expanded control or covers the next action.

Reference: MDN resize property reference.

Inspect constraints when the handle seems ineffective

Check computed resize, overflow, min-height and max-height together. A maximum equal to the minimum leaves no room to resize. On generic blocks, resize does not apply with overflow: visible or clip; do not transfer a textarea rule to another element without reviewing its box and overflow behavior.

A global reset may set resize: none. Before overriding it, identify why the rule exists. If the goal was to prevent horizontal overflow, vertical resizing may meet that goal without taking away useful editing space. If JavaScript auto-expands the field, check whether it repeatedly overwrites a height the user chose.

Make the field usable without dragging

Resize-handle support and interaction differ by browser and device. A user should be able to compose and review a long note without discovering a tiny corner affordance. Keep scrolling available when the content exceeds the field. If manual resizing is essential to the task, consider an explicit expand control with a clear keyboard path.

  • Paste several paragraphs and move the caret to the final line.
  • Enlarge the field, then reach the next form control.
  • Zoom the page and inspect the form at a narrow viewport.
  • Check touch editing and the onscreen keyboard on a real device.
  • Confirm the field’s visible label and error remain associated.

For a clipped field, diagnose the overflow source before shrinking text or disabling resizing. The form should adapt to the writing task, including notes longer than the designer’s sample.
coverAlt: A note field grows vertically from a dashed starting boundary while keeping the same width, with the following action moving below it.

title: Use bdi for Names Inside Mixed-Direction Text
description: Isolate dynamic names from surrounding punctuation with HTML bdi. Test Arabic, Hebrew, Latin text and numbers without changing the stored strings.
body:
Wrap an inline name of unknown direction in bdi when it sits inside a sentence, status row or activity feed. Bidirectional isolation keeps that inserted text from unexpectedly rearranging nearby punctuation and numbers. It addresses text ordering, which is separate from the layout direction of the whole interface.

Isolate the unknown fragment

<p dir="ltr">
  Reviewer: <bdi>سارة</bdi> — 3 notes
</p>
<p dir="ltr">
  Reviewer: <bdi>Alex</bdi> — 12 notes
</p>

These are illustrative names and counts. Keep the colon, separator and count outside the isolated name because they belong to the surrounding sentence. Without an explicit dir attribute, bdi behaves with automatic direction detection. If the inserted fragment is known to require a particular direction, specify that direction deliberately.

Reference: MDN bidirectional isolate element reference.

Keep text isolation separate from layout and safety

Setting text-align changes alignment, not the Unicode ordering algorithm. Likewise, switching margin-left to margin-inline-start supports a bidirectional layout but does not isolate a dynamic name. Use logical layout properties for geometry and bdi for the inline boundary.

When generating the example dynamically, assign the name with textContent or your framework’s normal escaped interpolation. bdi is not an HTML sanitizer. Do not inject an untrusted name through innerHTML just because it is wrapped in an isolation element.

Avoid reversing the stored characters to make one screenshot look correct. That can corrupt copying, searching and later display in another context. Keep the original string and let markup express the intended relationship to the surrounding text.

Test the boundaries that tend to move

  • Try a right-to-left name followed by a colon, dash or numeric count.
  • Try a Latin name inside a right-to-left page.
  • Include mixed-script names, parentheses and digits.
  • Copy the full line and confirm the underlying text remains sensible.
  • Check long names that wrap onto another line.

Save the exact failing string, page direction and surrounding punctuation in a bug report. “RTL text looks wrong” is difficult to reproduce; a small sentence with a clear expected reading order gives the reviewer a usable test. Ask a reader familiar with the language to review a real multilingual interface rather than judging correctness only from visual symmetry.
coverAlt: A dynamic name is isolated inside a highlighted boundary between a fixed Reviewer label and a note count, illustrating the bdi boundary.

title: Mark Up Dates with HTML time and datetime
description: Separate readable date labels from machine-readable values. Choose date-only or timestamp formats and check that timezones, metadata and visible text agree.
body:
Use a time element with a valid datetime value when a visible date needs an unambiguous machine-readable representation. Keep a calendar date distinct from a timestamp: an article publication day and a meeting’s exact start time do not require the same information.

Represent the kind of date you actually have

<p>Published <time datetime="2026-11-14">November 14, 2026</time></p>
<p>Review starts <time datetime="2026-11-14T15:00:00-05:00">
  November 14 at 3:00 p.m. Eastern Standard Time
</time>.</p>

The first example is a date without an invented hour or timezone. The second is an illustrative timestamp with an explicit offset. Its human-readable label must describe the same instant. An offset records the relationship to UTC for that timestamp; it is not a complete rule for scheduling recurring events across daylight-saving changes.

Reference: MDN time element and accepted datetime formats.

Use one source of truth for visible and hidden values

A templating bug can show November 14 while leaving November 13 in datetime or structured data. Generate those representations from the same validated content field. If a page displays a localized time, format the label and timestamp from the same instant instead of splicing together unrelated strings.

Do not automatically convert a date-only publication value to local midnight in every visitor’s timezone. That transformation can shift the displayed calendar day. Define whether the field represents a calendar date or an instant before passing it through a date library.

The time element does not create a date picker, timezone selector or automatic calendar invitation. It also does not prove that an article was updated. Preserve an original publication date and expose a modified date only when there is a substantive update worth representing.

Inspect dates as content, not decoration

  • Compare visible text, datetime, structured data and any feed values.
  • Test an event near midnight in more than one timezone.
  • Check month and day ordering in the intended locale.
  • Include the year when an old entry could otherwise be ambiguous.
  • Verify that labels such as Published and Updated mean what the data says.

For a US-facing interface, a label such as “November 14, 2026” avoids the ambiguity of a numeric date. In a dense activity table, combine explicit labels with tabular numerals when appropriate. Typography can improve scanning, but the underlying time semantics still need to be correct.
coverAlt: A readable November 14, 2026 date maps to a date-only datetime value, with a separate timestamp example containing an explicit offset.

title: Why Table Border Spacing Disappears in CSS
description: Compare collapsed and separate table borders. Fix missing border-spacing, doubled grid lines and misleading cell-padding changes with a focused inspection.
body:
If border-spacing appears to do nothing, inspect border-collapse on the table. Collapsed borders share edges between adjacent cells. Separate borders keep each cell’s border independent and allow border-spacing to create gaps. Cell padding changes the space inside a cell, not the gap between cells.

Choose the model that matches the table

.data-grid {
  border-collapse: collapse;
}
.data-grid th, .data-grid td {
  border: 1px solid #b8c0cb;
  padding: .75rem;
}

.spaced-grid {
  border-collapse: separate;
  border-spacing: .5rem .75rem;
}

The first pattern suits a continuous grid. The second demonstrates different horizontal and vertical gaps. Keep the table’s real header and data-cell markup in either case. A border-model change should not turn the table into a collection of generic blocks.

Reference: MDN border-collapse reference.

Inspect the winning edge rules

Select the table and confirm its computed border model before adjusting individual cells. A reset may have established collapse globally. In the collapsed model, adjacent cell, row and table border declarations can compete at the same edge; increasing the width of one arbitrary border may not create the uniform result you expect.

For a clean separate-border grid without gaps, start with border-spacing: 0. If both adjacent cells draw a full border, their edges can appear doubled. Assign consistent sides, such as bottom and inline-end, then account for the outer boundary intentionally. Do not hide a double line by making the text or background nearly the same color.

Rounded table corners add another question: which box owns the outer edge and which box clips the content? Review that separately from cell spacing. Test actual browser painting rather than assuming a radius on each cell will round the entire table.

Compare a small fixture before changing the full table

  • Use a two-column, three-row example with visible borders.
  • Toggle collapse and separate while keeping other declarations unchanged.
  • Change spacing, then padding, and observe which areas grow.
  • Check highlighted rows and sticky cells for seams.
  • Inspect the table at a narrow width with long values.

Once the edge model is stable, apply the responsive table workflow. Gaps and borders affect the table’s width, so recheck overflow after the visual repair. Preserve readable data relationships instead of squeezing every cell to fit one screenshot.
coverAlt: A continuous two-by-two grid shows shared borders beside a separated grid with visible gaps between individual cells.

title: Align Inline Icons with Text Using vertical-align
description: Diagnose baseline gaps and icon positioning in a text line. Choose vertical-align for inline boxes and flex alignment for separate layout items.
body:
Use vertical-align to adjust an inline or inline-block icon within a line of text. It does not vertically center a normal block inside its parent. Before changing the value, confirm whether the icon participates in an inline line box, a table cell or a flex layout.

Inspect the baseline and the icon’s own box

.inline-icon {
  display: inline-block;
  width: 1em;
  height: 1em;
  vertical-align: -0.125em;
}

The negative offset is an illustrative optical adjustment, not a universal icon token. Test it with the font and icon you actually use. An inline image normally participates in baseline alignment, which can leave room below it for text descenders. That space is not necessarily a margin or unwanted padding.

Reference: MDN vertical-align reference.

The middle keyword aligns an inline box relative to the parent’s baseline and x-height; it does not promise that the artwork will look centered against every capital letter. Extra whitespace inside an SVG viewBox can also make a correctly aligned box look wrong. Inspect the SVG coordinate bounds before adding larger offsets.

Use a layout model for a separate icon-label pair

.icon-label {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  gap: .4em;
}
.icon-label svg {
  width: 1em;
  height: 1em;
  flex: none;
}

This alternative centers separate flex items. It is suitable for a compact control whose icon and label should move together, but it behaves differently from an icon embedded inside a wrapping sentence. Choose the relationship first; do not combine alignment properties until something happens to look right.

For a multi-line label, decide whether the icon should align to the first line or the whole text block. Centering beside three lines may be intentional for a card action and confusing for a list bullet. Include the long-label case in the component example.

Review beyond one font size

  • Compare lowercase text, capitals and letters with descenders.
  • Test the fallback font before the web font loads.
  • Inspect at normal and enlarged text sizes.
  • Try a two-line label and a right-to-left context.
  • Check that a decorative icon is hidden from assistive technology when the text already names the action.

Save the chosen alignment with the font, line-height and icon dimensions. An offset without that context is easy to misuse when another component adopts the same icon at a different size.
coverAlt: An inline blue icon sits beside a text label with a marked baseline, followed by a separate flex alignment example.

title: Use :where() for CSS Defaults That Are Easy to Override
description: Write low-specificity component defaults with :where(). Compare selectors, keep cascade layers in mind and verify overrides without adding important flags.
body:
Use :where() when a selector should match normally but contribute no specificity. It is useful for defaults that consumers should be able to override easily. The zero applies to the :where() expression and its arguments, not automatically to everything else in the selector.

Compare selectors that match the same element

:where(.article a) {
  color: #174fa0;
  text-underline-offset: .15em;
}
.article .quiet-link { color: #354052; }

The default selector contributes zero specificity, while the quiet-link rule has class specificity. Assuming equal origin, importance and cascade layer, the override can win without an ID selector or !important. This makes the default easier to reuse in a component library.

Reference: MDN :where() reference.

.article :where(a) { color: #174fa0; }
:where(.article a) { color: #174fa0; }

These two declarations illustrate a common trap. The first keeps the specificity of .article outside the function. The second puts the complete selector inside, so the whole selector contributes zero. Replacing :where() with :is() also changes specificity: :is() takes the highest specificity among its arguments.

Do not confuse specificity with the entire cascade

A low-specificity declaration can still win when a more important cascade stage favors it. Layers, origin and importance are considered before selector specificity. If an override fails, inspect the complete winning rule rather than concluding that :where() is broken.

For an existing stylesheet, convert one small default group first. Use a fixture containing a normal article link, a quiet variant and a link inside a nested component. Record which values should be inherited and which should be locally owned. This makes an accidental loss of styling visible before a broad reset change.

Keep defaults modest and behavior intact

  • Confirm the default still applies when no variant is present.
  • Check an override declared earlier as well as one declared later.
  • Inspect the computed winner and its cascade layer.
  • Retain visible focus and readable link distinctions.
  • Avoid adding !important just to compensate for an unclear selector contract.

Document the intended override point with the component. For broader rule conflicts, use the cascade debugging sequence. A low-specificity default is a maintenance choice, not a guarantee that every consumer rule should win.
coverAlt: A default selector inside where has zero specificity, while a component variant uses a class selector to provide a local override.

title: CSS initial, inherit, unset and revert: Choose the Reset
description: Choose a CSS reset by the value you want to restore. Compare specification defaults, parent values and browser styles with a small reproducible example.
keyword: css initial inherit unset revert difference
body:
Choose initial for the property’s specification-defined initial value, inherit for the parent’s computed value, unset for the property’s natural inherited-or-initial behavior, and revert to roll back the current style origin. These keywords answer different questions; none means “undo my last edit.”

Use display to expose the difference

/* Compare these one at a time on an ordinary div. */
.example { display: initial; }
.example { display: revert; }

The initial value of display is inline. An ordinary div typically receives display: block from the browser stylesheet, so an author-level revert can restore that browser behavior while initial does not. The result depends on the element and applicable styles; do not treat revert as a universal block reset.

Reference: MDN revert keyword reference.

Match the keyword to the source of the value

.sample-parent { color: #174fa0; padding: 2rem; }
.sample-child {
  color: inherit;
  padding: unset;
}

In this fixture, the child receives the parent’s color. Padding is not naturally inherited, so unset resets it to its initial value rather than copying the parent’s 2rem. On a naturally inherited property such as color, unset instead behaves like inherit.

Try each keyword in an isolated rule and inspect the computed value. For revert in author CSS, look for the user or browser rule that becomes relevant after author-origin styling is rolled back. For inherited properties, values flowing from an ancestor can still matter. Revert does not simply choose an earlier declaration from the same author stylesheet.

Avoid resetting more than the repair requires

A broad all: unset or all: initial can remove useful visual defaults from controls, including the cues that distinguish an input or button. It does not remove their native HTML behavior, so the page can end up with controls that still work but no longer look interactive. Prefer resetting the specific property that is wrong.

  • State the intended result: parent value, initial value or browser styling.
  • Inspect the parent and browser rules before applying a reset.
  • Check keyboard focus and disabled states after changing a control.
  • Test the rule in a second component to expose accidental inheritance.
  • Review separate cascade-layer behavior if the actual goal is to roll back a layer.

Keep a before-and-after computed value in the issue report. That provides better evidence than saying a reset “fixed the CSS,” and it helps the next developer preserve the reason for the change.
coverAlt: Four CSS reset keywords map to specification initial value, parent value, inherited-or-initial behavior and an earlier style origin.

title: Debug Circular CSS Custom Properties
description: Find token aliases that point back to themselves. Break circular dependencies with a literal base token and verify the consuming property in each theme.
body:
A circular dependency occurs when a CSS custom property refers to itself, directly or through other custom properties on the same element. For ordinary unregistered properties in that cycle, the values become invalid at computed-value time. Adding more fallback expressions without tracing the references can hide the symptom rather than repair the token graph.

Reduce the failure to a small alias chain

.notice {
  --notice-accent: var(--brand-accent);
  --brand-accent: var(--notice-accent);
  border: 2px solid var(--notice-accent, #64748b);
}

Both aliases point into the same loop. In this unregistered example, the border uses the supplied gray fallback instead of either intended alias. A token inspector may show both declarations present, so existence alone is not evidence that they resolve to a usable value.

Reference: CSS Custom Properties specification: dependency cycles.

Give the chain a real starting value

:root {
  --palette-blue-700: #174fa0;
  --brand-accent: var(--palette-blue-700);
}
.notice {
  --notice-accent: var(--brand-accent);
  border: 2px solid var(--notice-accent);
}

This original hierarchy flows from a literal palette value to a semantic brand role and then to the component. Write those arrows on paper when a larger theme fails. Stop when you reach a literal or a value whose source is understood; if you revisit a node, inspect that loop first.

References inside fallback arguments also participate in dependency analysis. A self-reference such as --gap: var(--gap, 1rem) does not define a safe local default. Define the default directly or use a differently named input token. Registered properties have additional type and initial-value behavior, so check registration before interpreting their result.

Trace scope as well as names

Custom-property values resolve before being inherited. Do not assume that similarly named declarations on different ancestors form the same cycle as two mutually dependent declarations on one element. Inspect the selected element, its local overrides and the values it inherits.

  • Temporarily replace one alias with a valid literal and observe the consumer.
  • Check every var() reference, including fallback branches.
  • Repeat the check in light, dark and locally overridden themes.
  • Remove the temporary literal only after the dependency path is clear.

Distinguish a cycle from a missing token or unsuitable substituted value. Those failures can produce similar colors on screen but require different repairs. Keep the documented alias direction stable so later token renaming does not recreate the loop.
coverAlt: Two aliases point to each other in a broken loop; below them a palette value flows through a brand role to a component token.

title: Color a Monochrome Icon with CSS mask-image
description: Use an SVG mask and currentColor for a single-color icon. Diagnose invisible masks, sizing and network failures while keeping a visible text label.
body:
A CSS mask can use an icon’s silhouette to reveal a solid background color. This is useful for a single-color decorative icon that should follow the surrounding text color. It is not a way to preserve a multicolor illustration; the mask controls visibility while the element supplies the paint.

Give the mask a size, a shape and paint

<button type="button">
  <span class="download-icon" aria-hidden="true"></span>
  Download report
</button>
.download-icon {
  display: inline-block;
  width: 1em;
  height: 1em;
  background-color: currentColor;
  mask-image: url("/icons/download.svg");
  mask-size: contain;
  mask-position: center;
  mask-repeat: no-repeat;
  mask-mode: alpha;
}

Supply the SVG at the illustrated path and wire the button to the actual application action. The visible label names the control even if the decoration fails. Alpha mode makes opacity determine which parts of the painted box remain visible.

Reference: MDN mask-image reference.

Debug an invisible icon in layers

First remove the mask temporarily. If no solid box appears, inspect dimensions, display, background-color and inherited color. If the box appears, restore the mask and check its request in the Network panel. Confirm the URL, status, file contents and applicable cross-origin restrictions.

Test through an HTTP server rather than opening a local file URL. A mask that fails to load can leave the painted element invisible. Inspect the SVG itself as well: transparent artwork, unexpected bounds or an incorrect mask reference can all produce a result that looks like a CSS color problem.

Choose a fallback for essential meaning

Keep a textual label when possible. For an icon-only control, supply an accessible name and review a visible fallback if the mask cannot render. Do not assume that a CSS background will remain visible under every forced-colors setting. Native controls and clear labels should carry the interaction.

  • Change the text color and confirm the icon follows it.
  • Inspect at several font sizes and pixel densities.
  • Block the icon request to see whether the control remains understandable.
  • Review forced-colors mode and keyboard focus.
  • Use an ordinary image or inline SVG when multiple colors are required.

For an inline SVG that only needs a shared fill or stroke color, currentColor directly in SVG may be simpler. Choose masking for a clear asset-delivery reason, not because every icon needs another rendering layer.
coverAlt: A blue painted square is transformed through a mask into a monochrome download arrow, with currentColor supplying the paint.

title: Drop-shadow vs. Box-shadow for Transparent Images
description: Choose a shadow that follows a transparent image’s silhouette. Compare filter syntax, blur behavior and clipping before reusing a card elevation token.
keyword: drop shadow vs box shadow transparent image
body:
Use filter: drop-shadow() when the shadow should follow the opaque parts of a transparent image. Use box-shadow when the shadow belongs to the element’s box, such as a card surface. A transparent PNG or SVG makes the difference easier to see than a rectangular photograph.

Compare the same asset with two shadow models

.asset-box {
  box-shadow: 0 8px 16px rgb(16 24 40 / 20%);
}
.asset-shape {
  filter: drop-shadow(0 8px 8px rgb(16 24 40 / 20%));
}

These are separate example starting values, not mathematically identical effects. Drop-shadow’s third length controls a blur standard deviation, while box-shadow uses a blur-radius parameter. Copying all the same numbers does not promise the same softness.

Reference: MDN drop-shadow() reference.

The filter follows the rendered alpha shape. If the source image contains an opaque white rectangle around the artwork, the shadow will follow that rectangle too. Open the asset against a contrasting background to verify transparency before trying to repair the effect with CSS.

Apply the filter to the intended content

A filter on a wrapper processes that element and its rendered contents as a group. If the wrapper includes a background and a text label, the shadow may describe more than the icon silhouette. Move the effect to the intended image when those other parts should remain unaffected.

Drop-shadow does not accept box-shadow’s spread length or inset keyword. Multiple drop-shadow functions are space-separated within filter, not comma-separated box-shadow layers. Filter order also matters, so inspect the complete filter declaration before replacing a single effect.

Check clipping and nearby elements

  • Compare the image with the filter disabled to reveal the original alpha edges.
  • Inspect ancestors for overflow clipping near the shadow.
  • Try the effect against both light and dark surfaces.
  • Review overlap with neighboring controls and any changed stacking behavior.
  • Check a smaller responsive image size before adopting the values as a token.

A non-none filter can establish a stacking context, which may explain an overlap change after a visual edit. Use the stacking-context inspection guide if z-index adjustments stop behaving as expected. For ordinary panel elevation, keep the box-shadow workflow; transparency-aware shadows solve a different task.
coverAlt: The same diamond artwork is shown with a rectangular box shadow and a silhouette-shaped shadow, illustrating different shadow boundaries.

title: Style List Bullets with ::marker
description: Adjust native list bullets and numbers without rebuilding them as decorative elements. Understand marker property limits and keep list meaning intact.
body:
Use ::marker to style the bullet or number generated for a list item. It lets a list keep its native marker while you adjust supported properties such as color and font styling. It is not a general-purpose box that accepts every layout or background property.

Start with a real list

<ol class="review-steps">
  <li>Choose a representative page.</li>
  <li>Inspect the computed values.</li>
  <li>Record the implementation decision.</li>
</ol>
.review-steps { padding-inline-start: 1.75rem; }
.review-steps li { padding-inline-start: .25rem; }
.review-steps li::marker {
  color: #174fa0;
  font-weight: 700;
}

This example preserves the ordered sequence while emphasizing its numbers. The list padding controls room for outside markers, and the list-item padding adds a small gap before the text. Tune those values using a multi-line item, not only three short labels.

Reference: MDN ::marker and its supported properties.

Recognize the marker box’s limits

If padding, border or background on ::marker appears to be ignored, inspect whether the property is supported for markers before increasing specificity. Changing the marker’s content is possible in supported implementations, but replacing every ordered number with the same symbol discards the visible sequence.

A heavily designed step badge may need an explicit layout rather than more marker styling. Keep an ordered list when order matters, and avoid maintaining two independently edited sets of numbers. For a checklist with real completion state, use controls and labels; a colored bullet alone does not communicate whether an item is checked.

Review wrapping, nesting and fallback

  • Include a two-line item and confirm the continuation aligns with the text.
  • Try double-digit item numbers without clipping the marker.
  • Check nested lists and a right-to-left layout.
  • Verify the list is still understandable if decorative styling is unsupported.
  • Inspect the accessibility tree and listen to the list structure with a screen reader.

Avoid removing native markers globally just to fix one component. That can alter how other lists look and, in some browser and assistive-technology combinations, how they are exposed. Keep the scope narrow and test the actual structure.

Use logical padding so the indentation follows writing direction. The goal is a readable sequence whose decorative treatment can change without making the content depend on CSS-generated meaning.
coverAlt: Three ordered review steps keep native-looking blue numbers beside dark text, with a marker rule underneath.

title: Use Hover and Pointer Queries Without Hiding Actions
description: Adapt optional hover styling to input capabilities. Keep controls available on touch, keyboard and hybrid devices instead of treating screen width as input type.
body:
Use hover and pointer media queries to adapt optional styling to the primary pointing input. Keep essential controls available without hover. A narrow viewport is not proof of touch input, and a wide viewport is not proof that a mouse is being used.

Build a complete baseline interaction

.action {
  min-height: 2.75rem;
  padding: .65rem 1rem;
}
.action:focus-visible {
  outline: 3px solid #174fa0;
  outline-offset: 3px;
}
@media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine) {
  .action:hover { background: #e7f0ff; }
}

The button remains visible and usable without the media query. The example height is a design choice, not a claim that one dimension alone establishes accessibility. Focus styling stays outside the hover condition so keyboard users do not depend on pointing-device detection.

Reference: MDN hover media feature.

Reference: MDN pointer media feature.

Understand primary input and hybrid devices

Hover asks whether the primary pointing mechanism can conveniently hover. Pointer describes the accuracy of the primary pointing mechanism. The any-hover and any-pointer variants describe capabilities among available pointing mechanisms, which may include more than one device.

A touchscreen laptop can have both touch and a mouse. Discovering that some device can hover does not mean the user is currently using it. Do not use any-hover to make an essential delete control available only when the pointer enters a card. Keep the action visible, or provide an explicit tap and keyboard path.

Test the task through each input path

  • Use keyboard-only navigation and confirm every action can be reached.
  • Tap the interface and verify the first tap performs a predictable action.
  • Move the pointer into and out of dropdowns without losing their content.
  • Check a hybrid device with more than one pointing mechanism.
  • Inspect enlarged text and long labels without shrinking targets.

For a disclosure, define an explicit trigger and state. A hover color may enhance the trigger, but hover should not be the only way to discover or operate its content. Forced states in DevTools help inspect CSS; they cannot establish that real touch or keyboard interaction works.

Record the input capability you tested instead of labeling screenshots “mobile” and “desktop” alone. Use the forced-state inspection workflow for styling, followed by real interaction checks for behavior.
coverAlt: Touch, keyboard and pointer paths each lead to an available action, while hover feedback is labeled as optional.

title: Highlight a Field Group with :focus-within
description: Use focus-within for group context while keeping focus-visible on the actual control. Check nested fields, pointer focus and movement between groups.
body:
Use :focus-within when a container should be highlighted while it or one of its descendants has focus. Keep the actual focused input or button visibly identifiable too. A group highlight gives context; it should not leave users guessing which control will receive their next keystroke.

Style context and control separately

<fieldset class="name-group">
  <legend>Reviewer name</legend>
  <label for="given">Given name</label>
  <input id="given" name="given">
  <label for="family">Family name</label>
  <input id="family" name="family">
</fieldset>
.name-group {
  border: 1px solid #a8b3c3;
  padding: 1rem;
}
.name-group:focus-within { background: #f1f6ff; }
.name-group input:focus-visible {
  outline: 3px solid #174fa0;
  outline-offset: 2px;
}

The background can stay highlighted as focus moves between these two fields. The outline follows the specific input. Native labels and the fieldset provide semantics independently of the CSS; the pseudo-class does not create an accessible group name.

Reference: MDN :focus-within reference.

Do not confuse focus-within with focus-visible

Focus-within responds to focus, including descendant focus in shadow trees. It is not restricted to the circumstances in which a browser chooses to show :focus-visible. Clicking an input may therefore highlight its group even when another control’s focus-visible treatment differs.

No tabindex is needed on the fieldset just to make the ancestor selector work. Adding a focus stop to every wrapper makes keyboard navigation longer without necessarily providing an action. Keep the normal focus path through the real controls.

Follow focus across the boundary

  • Tab from the preceding control into the first field.
  • Move between fields and check the individual focus indicator.
  • Tab out of the group and confirm its highlight clears.
  • Click a field, then repeat the sequence using Shift+Tab.
  • Check nested groups, error messages and forced-colors mode.

Avoid changing border width or padding on focus unless the space was already reserved. A moving field group can make the page feel unstable. An inset effect or background change can supply context without pushing adjacent content around.

If a group highlight appears stuck, inspect document.activeElement and whether a descendant still holds focus. Do not remove focus blindly to clear a visual style. For controls that need a shared question or label, use the fieldset and legend pattern first, then add the visual feedback.
coverAlt: A pale highlighted name group contains two inputs, with a strong blue outline only on the focused Given name field.

title: Clamp Card Summaries Without Hiding Essential Content
description: Limit an optional summary to a few lines while keeping a clear route to the full text. Check browser support, zoom, focusable content and repeated card labels.
body:
Use multi-line clamping for optional preview text when the reader has an obvious way to reach the full content. Avoid clamping instructions, validation errors or the only label that distinguishes one item from another. Equal card heights are a layout preference, not a reason to hide essential information.

Keep the destination and title outside the crop

<article class="guide-card">
  <h2><a href="/guides/review/">Review an export</a></h2>
  <p class="summary">An optional preview of the complete guide...</p>
</article>
.summary {
  display: -webkit-box;
  -webkit-box-orient: vertical;
  -webkit-line-clamp: 3;
  overflow: hidden;
}

This established prefixed combination depends on the box display mode and vertical orientation together. Unprefixed line-clamp support varies, so inspect your target browsers rather than assuming a lone line-clamp declaration works everywhere. Let an unsupported browser show more text instead of using a fixed height that silently clips it.

Reference: MDN line-clamp reference and legacy combination.

Design a usable route to the complete text

The linked title should clearly identify the destination. If several titles are identical and only the summary distinguishes them, shortening the summary can make the choices ambiguous. Improve the labels before adding truncation. A hover-only tooltip is not a reliable full-text route for touch and keyboard readers.

Keep links, buttons and other focusable elements out of the clamped paragraph. Visually clipped content can still create confusing accessibility behavior; CSS cropping is not equivalent to a semantic collapsed section.
