For displaying a date outside a form, use the time and datetime workflow. A date input collects a value; semantic date markup presents one.
coverAlt: A date field presents December 15, 2026 in a US-style display while its normalized value is 2026-12-15, with December bounds shown separately.

title: Clear Stale Errors in the Constraint Validation API
description: Use setCustomValidity for a real rule and clear it when the value changes. Distinguish validity checks from reporting and preserve server-side validation.
body:
A nonempty setCustomValidity message keeps a control invalid until you clear it. If a corrected field still refuses submission, inspect whether an earlier custom error remains set. Native validity rules and custom messages need a consistent update path.

Clear the old message before rechecking the rule

const code = document.querySelector("#reference-code");
function validateReference() {
  code.setCustomValidity("");
  if (code.value && !code.value.startsWith("REV-")) {
    code.setCustomValidity("Start the reference with REV-.");
  }
}
code.addEventListener("input", validateReference);

This example assumes a labeled text input and a real application rule requiring the prefix. Empty values are left to a required attribute if the field is mandatory. Clearing the message first prevents a previously invalid value from carrying a stale custom error into a corrected state.

Reference: MDN constraint validation guide.

Choose when to inspect and when to report

checkValidity() evaluates whether the control or form satisfies its constraints and returns a result. reportValidity() also asks the browser to report a problem to the user. Repeatedly reporting on every keystroke can be disruptive; choose a deliberate validation moment such as a relevant action or submission attempt.

Run your rule for every path that changes the value, including application code that sets a field programmatically. The input event handler only covers the events it actually receives. If a custom rule depends on another field, changing that dependency must also trigger revalidation.

Do not rely exclusively on a submit event handler to clear a stale custom error: native validation can prevent the submit event from firing. Keep custom state current before the browser reaches that submission check.

Review the full recovery sequence

  • Enter an invalid value and trigger the intended validation action.
  • Correct it and confirm the custom error is cleared.
  • Set the value through the application’s restore or autofill path.
  • Change any dependent field and recheck the result.
  • Test a server rejection while preserving the user’s other entries.

The browser’s validity state is not a substitute for server validation or persistent, accessible error text. Follow the form-error workflow for field associations and correction advice. Document both the rule and when it runs, so later UI changes do not leave a hidden stale validity state behind.
coverAlt: An invalid reference without the REV prefix is corrected, and the old custom validity message is explicitly cleared before the rule runs again.

title: Why a Textarea Character Counter Disagrees with maxlength
description: Compare UTF-16 limits with user-perceived characters before building a counter. Test emoji, accents and pasted text, then align browser and server rules.
body:
A textarea’s maxlength is measured in UTF-16 code units, which are not always the same as visible characters. A counter based on JavaScript string length follows code units too. Emoji and combining sequences can expose a mismatch between that technical limit and a product promise such as “200 characters.”

Define what the limit actually counts

const sample = "A\u{1F600}";
console.log(sample.length); // 3 UTF-16 code units
const segments = new Intl.Segmenter("en", {
  granularity: "grapheme"
});
console.log([...segments.segment(sample)].length); // 2 graphemes

The example uses an escaped emoji so the underlying string is unambiguous. A grapheme approximates a user-perceived character more closely than a code unit. It is still a deliberate counting policy that needs agreement across client and server.

Reference: MDN textarea maxlength reference.

Reference: MDN Intl.Segmenter reference.

Align the counter, control and submission rule

If the product intentionally uses the native code-unit limit, make the counter use the same basis and explain surprising behavior clearly. If the product requires a grapheme limit, do not combine it with the same numeric maxlength and assume they enforce equivalent rules. Design the validation and server implementation around the chosen policy.

A byte limit for storage or network payload is another measure. Do not label it as a character limit without a conversion policy. Also consider pasted line breaks and normalized text: transformations performed after entry can change the count being validated.

Keep the current count visible without making a screen reader announce every keystroke. Announce a meaningful threshold or validation result only when that helps the task. Preserve text when reporting an over-limit value rather than silently deleting content the user has composed.

Use a small multilingual test set

  • Plain ASCII text exactly at the limit.
  • An emoji represented by a surrogate pair.
  • A combining accent and a precomposed accented letter.
  • A multi-code-point emoji sequence.
  • Pasted multiline text and an existing saved value.

Check the count during entry, after application restoration and on the server response. Record the counting unit in the component specification, even if the interface uses friendlier wording. The error-message workflow should explain how to recover without pretending that every visible symbol has the same storage representation.
coverAlt: The example A plus code point U+1F600 counts as three UTF-16 code units but two graphemes, illustrating why counting policies must match.

title: Associate Complex Table Cells with the Right Headers
description: Use explicit header IDs when a table has multi-level relationships. Verify each data cell’s context and simplify the table when grouping becomes hard to follow.
keyword: html table multiple headers ids headers attribute
body:
For a complex table, identify which row and column headers give each data cell its meaning. When simple scope relationships are insufficient, assign unique IDs to header cells and reference them from the data cell’s headers attribute. A bold appearance or colspan alone does not express every relationship.

Write one complete relationship before scaling up

<table>
  <caption>Illustrative review counts</caption>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th id="team" rowspan="2">Team</th>
      <th id="nov" colspan="2">November</th>
    </tr>
    <tr>
      <th id="open">Open</th>
      <th id="closed">Closed</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody><tr>
    <th id="design" scope="row">Design</th>
    <td headers="design nov open">4</td>
    <td headers="design nov closed">7</td>
  </tr></tbody>
</table>

The counts are invented specimen data, not product results. The value 4 has the context Design, November and Open. Check that exact relationship before adding more months or row groups. IDs must remain unique across the whole document, including when two table components appear on one page.

Reference: W3C WAI multi-level table headers tutorial.

Do not confuse visual grouping with associations

Colspan and rowspan shape the grid. They do not by themselves explain every complex association to assistive technology. Conversely, a simple two-column table may be clearer with ordinary scope attributes rather than a dense web of IDs. Choose the least complex markup that expresses the actual data.

If headers repeat halfway through a long table, inspect the relationships for rows in every section. A template can produce valid-looking cells that reference the first group’s IDs accidentally. Sorting or filtering must preserve correct header references too.

Read representative cells in context

  • Check a first, middle and last data cell with a screen reader.
  • Confirm every headers token resolves to the intended header.
  • Test duplicated table instances for ID collisions.
  • Inspect responsive scrolling without hiding essential headers.
  • Ask whether splitting the table would make the comparisons easier.

A complex association scheme is not a reason to keep an unnecessarily complex presentation. If readers need only one month at a time, a simpler table may serve the task better. Combine semantic review with the responsive table workflow, preserving the meaning of the data as the visual layout adapts.
coverAlt: A sample table groups Open and Closed counts under November, with a Design row and an explicit header path for the value four.

title: Keep Accordion Buttons and Panels in Sync with aria-expanded
description: Implement a custom disclosure with a native button, explicit expanded state and matching panel visibility. Test keyboard operation and focus when content closes.
body:
For a custom accordion, put a native button inside an appropriate heading, expose its expanded state and keep that state synchronized with the associated panel. Use native details and summary instead when they already meet the requirement; custom markup means owning the additional behavior.

Connect one heading button to one panel

<h3>
  <button id="format-toggle" type="button"
    aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="format-panel">
    Export format notes
  </button>
</h3>
<div id="format-panel" hidden>
  <p>Choose the format required by the receiving tool.</p>
</div>
const toggle = document.querySelector("#format-toggle");
const panel = document.querySelector("#format-panel");
toggle.addEventListener("click", () => {
  const expanded = toggle.getAttribute("aria-expanded") === "true";
  toggle.setAttribute("aria-expanded", String(!expanded));
  panel.hidden = expanded;
});

This example allows the panel to open and close independently. The h3 level is only appropriate when it fits the containing page. Give each instance unique IDs, and ensure component CSS does not override hidden in a way that leaves a supposedly closed panel visible.

Reference: W3C ARIA Authoring Practices accordion pattern.

Separate expansion from other control states

Aria-expanded describes whether controlled content is expanded. Aria-pressed describes a toggle button’s pressed state and is not a substitute here. Keep the visible label meaningful in both states, and give the button a clear focus indicator.

For a multi-panel accordion, decide whether several sections can remain open. If another action closes a panel that contains keyboard focus, restore focus to a useful visible control. Do not collapse content silently while leaving focus in an unavailable descendant.

Review interaction and reading order

  • Tab to each heading button and activate it with Enter and Space.
  • Verify the exposed expanded value after every change.
  • Reach links and controls inside an open panel.
  • Close the panel and confirm its descendants leave the normal interaction path.
  • Test long headings, enlarged text and repeated component instances.

Arrow-key navigation between headers is an optional pattern choice; ordinary native buttons still need a working Tab sequence. Avoid making every small panel a named landmark when that would create excessive regions. Compare this implementation with the native disclosure guide and document why the custom behavior is needed.
coverAlt: An export-notes heading button has aria-expanded true and points through aria-controls to its visible panel.

title: Review Tooltips for Hover, Focus and Dismissal
description: Test whether temporary help can be reached, read and dismissed without losing context. Distinguish a brief tooltip from interactive content that needs another pattern.
body:
Review a tooltip as a temporary interaction, not just a small floating label. A useful check asks how it opens, whether the pointer can reach it, how long it stays available and how it can be dismissed. Keyboard users need a way to discover the same supporting information.

Write a reproducible interaction sequence

1. Tab to the help trigger.
2. Read the additional explanation.
3. Dismiss it without moving focus.
4. Open it with the pointer.
5. Move the pointer from the trigger onto the help.
6. Leave the relevant area and verify the closing behavior.

Use an actual label from the interface, such as “Export quality,” and record what should happen at each step. A forced hover state in DevTools can help inspect colors but cannot prove that the pointer can cross a gap without closing the content.

Reference: W3C guidance on content appearing on hover or focus.

Keep the additional content operable and predictable

For author-created hover/focus content, review dismissibility, hoverability and persistence under the criterion’s conditions and exceptions. Escape is a common dismissal mechanism. Dismissal should not require a user to move focus away merely to uncover something beneath the tooltip.

Do not hide essential instructions only in a tooltip. A user may never trigger it, and its short-lived format is a poor home for long explanations. If the content contains links, buttons or a task to complete, choose an appropriate interactive popover or dialog instead of styling it as a tooltip and ignoring focus behavior.

The HTML title attribute is not a complete custom-tooltip implementation. Browser-managed title presentation and timing are not controlled in the same way, and it should not be the only naming or instruction strategy for a control.

Stress the placement and timing

  • Test keyboard focus and pointer hover independently.
  • Move slowly across the boundary between trigger and content.
  • Dismiss while leaving the pointer and focus in place.
  • Check viewport edges, scrolling ancestors and enlarged text.
  • Try touch input and confirm essential help remains available.

Record the closing rules and whether dismissal remains respected until the next intentional trigger. Reappearing immediately after Escape can make a technically present dismissal key ineffective in practice. Use the help-panel workflow when the information needs a deliberate open action or richer interaction.
coverAlt: A help trigger and its floating explanation have a connected pointer path, with keyboard focus, hover and Escape dismissal listed as separate checks.

title: Find Keyboard Focus Hidden Behind Sticky Headers
description: Test focus beneath sticky headers, footers and banners. Fix overlapping page chrome and verify forward and backward navigation at enlarged sizes.
body:
A visible focus style is not enough if a sticky header or floating banner covers the focused control. Review keyboard navigation through the complete page, especially near the viewport edges. The user needs to see where their next action will occur.

Reproduce the overlap with real focus

Open the page with its normal header, cookie notice and any persistent action bar. Tab through controls until one approaches an edge, then reverse with Shift+Tab. Repeat at a smaller viewport and with enlarged text. A click on the control may scroll differently from sequential keyboard navigation, so test both deliberately.

Reference: W3C Focus Not Obscured (Minimum) explanation.

The Level AA minimum concerns a focused component being entirely hidden by author-created content. Aim for the whole control to remain visible where practical; partial visibility is a minimum boundary, not an ideal design target. Review the criterion’s notes when user-positioned or user-opened content is involved.

Repair the overlap at its source

html { scroll-padding-block-start: 5rem; }
.section-target { scroll-margin-block-start: 5rem; }

These illustrative offsets can help some scrolling and target-alignment paths, but they are not a universal keyboard-focus fix. Verify the actual browser behavior and header size. A header that wraps to two lines can outgrow a fixed offset, and a nested scrolling panel may need its own treatment.

Consider reducing sticky content, allowing it to leave the viewport at high zoom or reserving enough usable space. A permanent footer plus a large header can leave very little working area even when neither one is individually excessive. Do not solve an overlap by removing the focus indicator.

Check the paths after a repair

  • Tab forward and backward near both viewport edges.
  • Activate skip links and error-summary links.
  • Open and close persistent notices and nonmodal panels.
  • Increase text size until header labels wrap.
  • Inspect controls inside nested scroll containers.

In the issue report, name the focused element, covering element, viewport and exact navigation sequence. “Focus is missing” can mean several different defects; a screenshot showing the overlap plus the active element narrows the diagnosis. Use the anchor-spacing workflow for fragment alignment, then separately verify keyboard focus visibility.
coverAlt: A sticky header covers part of a focused action in one viewport sketch, while a second sketch leaves the entire action visible below the header.

title: Test a Page with User Text-Spacing Overrides
description: Review text after line, paragraph, letter and word spacing increase together. Find clipping and lost controls without redesigning the site around one preset.
body:
Test text-spacing adaptability by applying the relevant spacing changes together and checking that content and controls remain usable. This is an override test, not a requirement that the site’s default typography use those values. Preserve the page’s ordinary font size and other styles during the focused check.

Use the four spacing relationships

Line height: at least 1.5 × font size
Space after paragraphs: at least 2 × font size
Letter spacing: at least 0.12 × font size
Word spacing: at least 0.16 × font size

These are the relationships used by WCAG’s text-spacing criterion for applicable markup and scripts. Apply them through a review stylesheet or an appropriate testing tool, taking care not to reduce a value that is already larger. The language/script exception matters when a spacing property is not used by that writing system.

Reference: W3C Text Spacing explanation.

Inspect the components most likely to lose content

Start with short fixed-height controls, navigation labels, notification banners and dense cards. Increased spacing can make a label wrap into a height that the original specimen never required. Look for text clipped by overflow, buttons whose second line is covered and content colliding with an icon.

Read an entire paragraph, not only its first line. Check the boundary between paragraphs and the next component. A fixed card height can preserve a neat grid while silently losing the end of the text. A multiline clamp may also need review when the shortened preview stops conveying useful information.

When you find a failure, disable the particular height or clipping constraint in DevTools to identify the cause. Do not “repair” the test by overriding the user’s spacing back to your preferred values. The goal is an adaptable component.

Save evidence and restore the normal page

  • Record the override values and the affected content.
  • Test links, form submission and disclosure controls after wrapping changes.
  • Repeat with long labels and realistic paragraph lengths.
  • Verify any intentional truncation still has a usable route to the full content.
  • Remove the diagnostic override before reviewing the normal visual design.

This focused check does not establish complete accessibility conformance. It gives a reproducible way to find one class of layout failure. Keep the defect report tied to lost content or functionality and review the line-height inheritance guide if nested text behaves inconsistently.
coverAlt: A spacing review checklist lists line height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2em, letter spacing 0.12em and word spacing 0.16em as minimum override relationships.

title: Review Reflow at High Browser Zoom
description: Check whether content remains readable and operable at a narrow equivalent viewport. Test page zoom, two-dimensional exceptions and sticky interfaces deliberately.
body:
A reflow review checks whether content adapts to the available reading area without losing information or functionality. Browser zoom is useful because it exposes layouts that only work at the designer’s original text and viewport scale. Inspect the tasks on the page, not just whether the first screen looks tidy.

Set a known starting viewport

For vertically scrolling content, WCAG’s reflow criterion uses an equivalent width of 320 CSS pixels. A starting viewport 1280 CSS pixels wide at 400% zoom is one way to reach that relationship. Measure the page viewport, not the outer browser window including its frame and side panels.

Reference: W3C Reflow explanation.

({ width: window.innerWidth, height: window.innerHeight })

Record the baseline viewport, browser zoom and resulting width. A narrow responsive preview is also useful, but do not describe it as a real zoom test if you only dragged a viewport handle. Native controls, fixed layers and browser behavior deserve checks under actual zoom.

Read and operate the whole page

Follow a paragraph to its end, use navigation, fill a form, open a disclosure and reach the final action. Look for horizontal page scrolling needed to read ordinary text, hidden controls, overlapping sticky regions and content cut by fixed heights. Check errors and empty states as well as the initial view.

Some content needs two-dimensional layout for meaning or use, such as certain data tables and maps. That exception should not make the entire surrounding page scroll sideways. Keep ordinary headings, explanations and controls responsive around the exceptional content, and review the criterion’s details for the specific case.

Diagnose overflow instead of hiding it

  • Identify the element wider than the available area.
  • Check fixed widths, long unbroken strings and minimum sizes.
  • Inspect nested grid or flex constraints.
  • Review sticky headers and footers that consume the remaining viewport.
  • Test the repaired task again at normal and high zoom.

Do not use overflow-x: hidden on the whole page merely to remove a scrollbar while content remains unreachable. Use the overflow debugging workflow to fix the cause. Save the viewport, zoom, trigger and affected element so the review can be repeated after a layout refactor.
coverAlt: A wide 1280-CSS-pixel viewport at 400 percent zoom is compared with a narrow 320-CSS-pixel equivalent reading area.

title: Test Missing Resources with Chrome Request Conditions
description: Block one image, font or request to review a page’s fallback behavior. Keep patterns narrow, verify the blocked request and restore normal loading afterward.
keyword: chrome devtools block requests test fallback
body:
Use Chrome DevTools’ request-blocking controls to test how your own page behaves when a resource fails to load. Block one known image, font or request at a time so the resulting fallback has an explainable cause. A simulated failure is useful evidence when it is labeled and reproducible.

Block a specific request and confirm the simulation

  • Open Network and reload to locate the resource.
  • Use the request’s context menu to block it, or add a narrow pattern in Request conditions.
  • Keep blocking enabled and reload the relevant page state.
  • Check the request status to confirm DevTools actually blocked it.

Reference: Chrome DevTools Request conditions documentation.

Chrome’s current documentation calls the drawer Request conditions; older installations may use request-blocking wording. A status such as blocked:devtools distinguishes the simulation from a real server failure. Record the exact pattern rather than reporting that “the image server is down.”

Review the fallback against the user’s task

For an image, check alternative text, reserved layout space and whether an essential action remains understandable. For a web font, inspect fallback text, wrapping and button sizes. For a data request, verify that a useful error or retry path appears instead of a permanent spinner.

Blocking an entire domain can also block unrelated assets and authentication flows, making the result harder to interpret. Start with the smallest resource that answers the question. If caching or a service worker means the resource is not requested again, inspect the actual loading path before claiming the test passed.

Do this in a safe review context with representative data. A failed-request test should not require submitting a destructive production action. Keep the simulated condition separate from ordinary browsing and from any real incident report.

Restore and compare

  • Disable the pattern and reload to confirm the normal state returns.
  • Check that the fallback did not erase useful user input.
  • Repeat with another resource only after recording the first result.
  • Verify that images, fonts and data requests need different recovery strategies.
  • Remove or disable diagnostic patterns when the review ends.

DevTools can retain saved patterns even after a session ends, so explicitly inspect them during later debugging. Use the font-loading guide or the alternative-text workflow for the corresponding repair. A good fallback keeps the task understandable, not merely free of console errors.
coverAlt: A selected image request is marked blocked by DevTools while the page fallback retains a text label and reserved image space.

title: Set the Page Language and Mark Language Changes in HTML
description: Use a valid lang value for the document and meaningful language changes. Keep language separate from direction, translation and font selection.
keyword: html lang attribute language of parts
body:
Set the document’s primary language with lang on the html element, then mark passages in another language when appropriate. This gives browsers and assistive technologies language information they can use. It does not translate the text or automatically choose the correct page direction.

Start with the language of the actual content

<html lang="en-US">
  <!-- An English document intended for US readers -->
</html>
<p>The Spanish interface uses the label
  <span lang="es">Guardar cambios</span>.
</p>

The first example identifies US English. The second identifies a Spanish phrase within English text. Use a valid language tag that matches the content; do not derive the language solely from the user’s location or the domain suffix. A page can serve US readers while containing passages in other languages.

Reference: MDN lang global attribute reference.

Separate language from neighboring concerns

Lang describes language. Dir describes text direction, and CSS logical properties help the layout follow that direction. An Arabic passage can need both language and direction information; setting one does not automatically express every aspect of the other.

Language can also affect text processing such as hyphenation. If a paragraph uses the wrong dictionary or pronunciation, inspect the inherited language before changing spacing or replacing the font. A correctly identified language still needs a font with the required glyph coverage.

Avoid indiscriminately adding language changes to every proper name or borrowed term. Review whether the passage genuinely changes language in a way that needs marking. Keep content authors involved so the markup follows meaning rather than a guess based on unfamiliar characters.

Review dynamic and localized content

  • Inspect the language on the rendered html element.
  • Check embedded passages and inherited values on their ancestors.
  • Switch the application locale and confirm content and language metadata change together.
  • Listen to representative passages with supported assistive technology.
  • Test hyphenation and spelling-related behavior where it matters.

For a component that receives multilingual content, specify who supplies language metadata. Do not silently label every incoming string as English. Use the bidirectional isolation guide for unknown-direction inline names and the hyphenation guide when language-aware line breaking is part of the design.
coverAlt: An English document marked en-US contains a Spanish phrase marked es, keeping passage language separate from the page default.

title: Use Small Caps Without Confusing Them with Uppercase
description: Inspect real small-cap glyphs, font support and synthesis before styling a text role. Compare small-caps with uppercase transformation at the sizes you ship.
keyword: css font variant caps small caps
body:
Small caps are a typographic treatment using capital-shaped glyphs designed for a smaller height. They are not simply the same as turning every letter into an ordinary uppercase character. Use font-variant-caps when the text role calls for the font’s capitalization features, and inspect what the selected face actually supplies.

Compare the treatments on one specimen

.small-cap-label { font-variant-caps: small-caps; }
.all-small-cap-label { font-variant-caps: all-small-caps; }
.uppercase-label { text-transform: uppercase; }

Use the same family, size and weight for an original specimen such as “Design Review.” Small-caps typically treats lowercase letters as small capitals while retaining ordinary capitals; all-small-caps requests small-cap treatment for both cases. Uppercase transformation serves a different purpose.

Reference: MDN font-variant-caps reference.

Verify the font feature instead of trusting the property name

A face may lack the necessary small-cap glyphs, and the browser can synthesize a substitute. Synthetic small caps can have different stroke weight and proportions from designed glyphs. Check the font’s documentation and rendered output before making the treatment part of a brand text style.

Compare a version where synthesis is disabled if your browser and font workflow support it. That can help identify whether the appearance depends on generated forms. Do not assume a CSS declaration proves that the intended OpenType feature was present in the downloaded file.

Keep the specimen realistic. A short decorative heading can look balanced while a dense navigation label becomes difficult to scan. Review lowercase, capitals, numerals and punctuation, and compare localized strings rather than applying a Latin typography choice automatically to every script.

Document a complete text role

  • Confirm the actual loaded face and its supported features.
  • Compare normal, small-cap and uppercase specimens at the same size.
  • Inspect stroke weight and spacing at small sizes.
  • Check fallback rendering before the web font loads.
  • Review long labels and line wrapping in the component.

Store the font file, feature setting, size, weight and tracking together in the handoff. If the font lacks suitable glyphs, an ordinary case treatment may be clearer than a fragile imitation. The font-synthesis guide explains how generated styles can differ from real supplied designs, while the tracking guide helps review spacing separately.
coverAlt: A typography review compares a font-feature small-cap request with uppercase transformation, emphasizing verification of the actual font glyphs.

title: Number Section Headings with CSS Counters
description: Scope a CSS counter to one article and increment it deliberately. Test nested components and hidden headings, and keep essential numbering in semantic content.
body:
CSS counters can generate section numbers from document structure. Use a scoped counter when numbering is a visual aid that should follow the sections automatically. If a number is essential to navigation, cross-references or an exported document, represent that meaning in the content model rather than relying only on generated CSS text.

Scope the counter to the intended article

.numbered-guide { counter-reset: section; }
.numbered-guide > section { counter-increment: section; }
.numbered-guide > section > h2::before {
  content: counter(section) ". ";
  color: #174fa0;
}

This example assumes direct child sections, each with a direct h2. The narrow selectors keep an unrelated nested component from incrementing the same sequence. Counter-reset creates the starting counter scope, counter-increment advances it, and counter() inserts the displayed value.

Reference: MDN CSS counters guide.

Review structural changes, not just the first render

Add, remove and reorder a section in a local fixture. Then insert a nested example containing another heading. A broad selector such as every h2 inside the article may accidentally count that example as a top-level section. The CSS should follow the intended information structure, not merely all tags of a certain size.

Hidden and conditionally rendered sections also need testing. An element removed from rendering with display: none does not behave like a visible numbered section for counters. Decide whether the numbering should follow visible sections or stable content identifiers before choosing the implementation.

Do not hard-code prose such as “see section 4” when the visible sequence is dynamically generated and can change. Use descriptive links to stable section IDs. If a legal, procedural or reference number must remain stable, store it explicitly and keep it consistent across HTML and exports.

Check alternate ways of reading the document

  • Disable the counter styling and confirm the headings still make sense.
  • Inspect screen-reader output for generated prefixes and unwanted repetition.
  • Copy text and review a print or export version.
  • Test multiple article instances on the same page.
  • Confirm heading levels remain semantic rather than chosen for their numbering.

For ordered steps, begin with a real ordered list and style its markers when appropriate. A heading counter does not create list semantics. Use the heading audit to establish the structure first, then add numbering as an intentional presentation layer.
coverAlt: An article scope numbers three section headings in order, with a separate reminder that stable references need meaningful content identifiers.

title: Write a Design Bug Report a Developer Can Reproduce
description: Turn a visual mismatch into a useful report with a trigger, environment and expected behavior. Separate observed evidence from a proposed CSS fix.
keyword: design bug report reproducible css issue
body:
A useful design bug report lets another person reproduce the same mismatch without guessing the page state or viewport. Start with the task that fails, then provide the smallest set of conditions that makes the defect appear. A screenshot supports that record but rarely replaces it.

Describe the trigger and the result

Page: /review/example
State: export panel open; long file name selected
Viewport: 360 × 800 CSS pixels
Browser and zoom: record the tested version and setting
Steps: open panel, select sample, Tab to the final action
Observed: the action label is clipped on its second line
Expected: the complete label remains visible and operable

This is a hypothetical report template, not a claim about Penta AI. Replace every field with what you observed. Include the content string that triggers wrapping, using safe specimen data instead of private account details.

Attach evidence that explains ownership

Capture the full affected component and enough surrounding layout to show the relationship. If the child seems too wide, inspect its parent’s layout and box model. Note the element that owns the relevant height, overflow or spacing rule, rather than attaching a large unsorted dump of CSS.

Reference: Chrome DevTools CSS inspection reference.

Separate observation from a proposed repair. “The second line is clipped when this panel is 360px wide” is evidence. “Remove height: 40px” is a hypothesis until you test long labels, neighboring elements and alternate states. A developer may find a better fix once the underlying constraint is clear.

If the issue appears only after loading, record the timing and request conditions. If a pseudo-class was forced in DevTools, say so. Include browser zoom and the screenshot capture conditions so an exported image’s dimensions do not become an accidental layout specification.

Give the repair a verifiable finish line

  • Specify the affected task and the expected usable result.
  • Include one failing fixture and one ordinary case that must still work.
  • List important states such as error, loading, focus and long content.
  • Record whether the problem occurs on real hardware or in emulation.
  • Retest the original sequence after the proposed fix.

Keep unrelated visual opinions in separate issues so one repair has a clear purpose. A concise report with a reproducible trigger is more actionable than a gallery of unlabeled screenshots. Use the handoff checklist for the broader specification, and use this report to isolate a particular failure against it.
coverAlt: A concise design bug report lists the trigger, viewport, observed clipping and expected complete action label as separate evidence fields.

title: Connect Controls Outside a Form with the form Attribute
description: Associate detached inputs and submit buttons with the correct HTML form. Check ownership, field names and submission before rearranging a form layout.
keyword: html form attribute external input button
body:
A save button can sit outside a form in the document and still submit it. Give the form a unique id, then use that value in the control’s form attribute. This is useful when a page toolbar and the editable fields occupy separate layout regions.

Make ownership explicit

<form id="profile" action="/profile" method="post">
  <label for="display-name">Display name</label>
  <input id="display-name" name="displayName">
</form>
<label for="team">Team</label>
<input id="team" name="team" form="profile">
<button type="submit" form="profile">Save profile</button>

The route is illustrative; implement its server handler before using this as a working submission. Both named inputs belong to the same form even though the team field is outside it. The label’s for connects a label to a control; the control’s form connects that control to its form owner. These are separate relationships.

Reference: MDN form attribute.

Inspect the rendered relationship

Select the detached input in DevTools and inspect its form property. It should reference the intended form element. Check the form’s elements collection and a local new FormData(form) snapshot as well. A matching visual panel or shared component name does not establish ownership.

The attribute does not inherit down a subtree. Putting form="profile" on an external fieldset does not automatically associate its nested inputs; assign ownership to those controls individually. Keep IDs unique when a component appears twice. Do not nest forms to repair a toolbar layout.

Review the complete save interaction

  • Activate Save with keyboard and pointer input.
  • Submit with an invalid required field and check where focus moves.
  • Confirm the server receives each expected named field.
  • Check which form owns each button when multiple forms share the page.

External controls still need a sensible reading and focus order. A distant Save button may be technically associated yet hard to discover. Document the relationship alongside the button’s explicit type so a later layout refactor does not silently change which form submits.
coverAlt: A form named profile contains the display name, while a separate team field and Save button explicitly point to the same form owner.

title: Why Unchecked Checkboxes Are Missing from FormData
description: Inspect checkbox submissions without losing repeated values. Understand unchecked fields, explicit values and the data contract your server must enforce.
body:
An unchecked checkbox contributes no name/value entry to a normal form submission. It does not automatically submit false or an empty string. Start by deciding what an absent entry means in your application, then inspect the actual payload instead of inferring it from the visible checkmark.

Keep the value and checked state separate

<form id="preferences">
  <label><input type="checkbox" name="format" value="svg"> SVG</label>
  <label><input type="checkbox" name="format" value="png"> PNG</label>
</form>
const form = document.querySelector('#preferences');
const data = new FormData(form);
console.log(data.getAll('format'));

With neither option selected, the array is empty. With both selected, it contains svg and png. The value is the submitted token, while checked determines whether that checkbox contributes an entry. A checkbox without an explicit value uses on when checked.

Reference: MDN checkbox submission behavior.

Preserve repeated keys

Use getAll() when the same name can legitimately occur more than once. A convenient conversion such as Object.fromEntries(data) keeps only one value per object key and can erase a multi-selection. Inspect the network payload as well as any JavaScript representation before blaming the server.

Reference: MDN FormData.getAll.

For a single preference, the server can map an absent checkbox key to false if the endpoint’s contract defines that meaning. For a partial update, absence might instead mean “leave unchanged.” Decide explicitly. A hidden field with the same name creates repeated entries when the checkbox is checked; parser behavior must be agreed rather than assumed.

Test the payload matrix

  • Submit with zero, one and every option selected.
  • Remove the name in a fixture and observe the missing entry.
  • Disable a checked option and compare the payload.
  • Verify that unknown or unauthorized values are rejected server-side.

Use specimen preferences during inspection so logs do not capture personal data. Keep the disabled-field behavior in the same handoff: an omitted value can come from either an unchecked box or an unavailable control, and those states may have different product meanings.
coverAlt: A checked SVG option contributes format equals svg to a payload, while an unchecked PNG option contributes no entry.

title: Reset a Form to Its Defaults, Not Necessarily to Empty
description: Debug form reset behavior by comparing current and default values. Keep error messages and application state consistent when restoring a form’s defaults.
keyword: html form reset defaultvalue not empty
body:
A native form reset restores default control values. It is not a universal “clear everything” operation, and it does not undo a server-side save. When a reset appears broken, compare the current value with the default value before adding code that empties every field.

Observe the two values

<form id="draft">
  <label for="title">Title</label>
  <input id="title" name="title" value="Untitled review">
  <button type="reset">Restore defaults</button>
</form>
const form = document.querySelector('#draft');
const field = document.querySelector('#title');
field.value = 'My edited review';
console.log(field.value, field.defaultValue);
form.reset();
console.log(field.value); // Untitled review

This example deliberately starts with a nonempty default. Editing the current value does not make it the new default. If application code changes the value attribute or defaultValue, the next reset can restore that newer default instead. Check both properties in the same debugging session.

Reference: MDN form reset method.

Reference: MDN input defaultValue.

Restore surrounding state deliberately

Resetting controls does not automatically remove an application’s error summary, clear custom validity messages, restore a disabled attribute or discard uploaded server data. Decide which state belongs to the reset operation. Controlled form components also need their framework state reconciled, or the next render can put the edited values back.

A reset event handler runs as part of the reset operation; avoid assuming that reading controls immediately inside it gives the final restored values. For an explicit JavaScript reset workflow, call form.reset() and then synchronize the dependent display. Do not name a control reset, which can mask the form method.

Name the action according to its consequence

“Restore defaults,” “Clear filters” and “Discard edits” describe different promises. For a filter form, the default might be “All teams,” not an empty field. For saved settings, discarding edits may require reloading the last saved model instead of using the markup’s initial values.

  • Change text, checkboxes and select values before testing.
  • Confirm the reset preserves the intended default selection.
  • Retest validation after restoring defaults.
  • Keep a destructive reset away from the primary save action.

If error feedback survives after its field has been restored, use the custom-validity checklist to identify which state your application still needs to clear.
coverAlt: An edited title returns to the nonempty default Untitled review after reset, showing that reset does not necessarily clear the field.

title: Show Partial Selection with an Indeterminate Checkbox
description: Build a native select-all checkbox that reflects none, some or all choices. Derive the mixed state from the items and keep submission behavior separate.
body:
A select-all checkbox needs to distinguish a partial selection from both zero and complete selection. On a native checkbox, set the JavaScript indeterminate property for that mixed presentation. Derive it from the child choices so the summary cannot drift out of sync.

Compute the summary from the items

<label><input id="all-formats" type="checkbox"> All formats</label>
<fieldset id="formats">
  <legend>Export formats</legend>
  <label><input type="checkbox" name="format" value="svg"> SVG</label>
  <label><input type="checkbox" name="format" value="png"> PNG</label>
</fieldset>
const all = document.querySelector('#all-formats');
const items = [...document.querySelectorAll('#formats input')];
function sync() {
  const count = items.filter(item => item.checked).length;
  all.checked = items.length > 0 && count === items.length;
  all.indeterminate = count > 0 && count < items.length;
}
items.forEach(item => item.addEventListener('change', sync));
all.addEventListener('change', () => {
  items.forEach(item => { item.checked = all.checked; });
  sync();
});
sync();

The parent has no name because it summarizes the options rather than adding another export format. This minimal example assumes every child is enabled and the list is static. Recompute the collection when rows are added or removed; define whether disabled choices participate before extending it.

Reference: MDN indeterminate checkboxes.

Keep appearance separate from submitted data

Indeterminate is a property, not an HTML attribute you can make work by writing indeterminate="true". It does not create a third submitted value. The ordinary checked state still governs whether a named checkbox contributes data. Read the checkbox payload guide when wiring the selection to a form.

Test transitions rather than a single screenshot

  • Start with neither item selected: the summary is unchecked.
  • Select one item: the summary becomes mixed.
  • Select both: the summary becomes checked.
  • Activate the summary with Space and verify both child states.
  • Uncheck a child and confirm the mixed state returns.

Listen to the actual accessible state in a supported browser and screen reader. Keep native labels and fieldset semantics, and avoid replacing the checkbox with a drawn dash that has no input behavior. If the interface remembers a previous partial selection, document that additional interaction separately; this simple example only switches the whole set on or off.
coverAlt: Three checkbox summary states show none selected, some selected with a dash, and all selected with a check mark.

title: Use datalist for Suggestions, Not a Restricted Choice List
description: Choose between datalist and select by whether custom input is allowed. Connect native suggestions to a labeled field and review accessibility fallbacks.
keyword: html datalist vs select custom value
body:
A text input connected to datalist can offer suggestions while still allowing other values. Use it when the suggestions help typing but do not define the only valid answers. If users must choose from an allowed set, a native select is often the clearer starting point.

Connect the list without replacing the label

<label for="workspace-tag">Workspace tag</label>
<input id="workspace-tag" name="tag" list="tag-suggestions"
       aria-describedby="tag-help">
<datalist id="tag-suggestions">
  <option value="Typography"></option>
  <option value="Color"></option>
  <option value="Layout"></option>
</datalist>
<p id="tag-help">Choose a suggestion or enter your own tag.</p>

The input’s list value references the datalist ID. Its name remains on the input because that is the form control. The help text explicitly permits a custom value, making the product rule visible instead of leaving the user to discover it through rejection.

Reference: MDN datalist element.

Separate suggestions from validation

Typing “Motion” into this example does not become invalid merely because Motion is absent from the suggestions. If the server maintains an allowed taxonomy, either validate against it with a clear error or use a selection interface that communicates the restriction. Do not treat the suggestion menu as a security boundary.

Option labels and displayed values can differ across browsers. Use simple values that make sense when typed, selected and submitted. Test duplicate and case-variant entries with the real server normalization rules, rather than silently changing a user’s label in the browser.

Review the native popup on target devices

A datalist popup is controlled by the browser and has styling and accessibility limitations. Review keyboard selection, screen-reader announcement, enlarged text and contrast on the combinations you support. Verify the ordinary text field remains usable if suggestions are unavailable; avoid putting indispensable instructions only in the popup.

  • Type a partial match, then choose a suggestion.
  • Enter a value absent from the list.
  • Clear the field and check required-field behavior if applicable.
  • Submit a long custom tag and inspect its display elsewhere.

For a short fixed set, compare this flow with a native select and grouped options. For a complex searchable picker, budget for a full keyboard and accessibility implementation rather than assuming a datalist can be styled into one.
coverAlt: A text field accepts Motion even though its suggested tags are Typography, Color and Layout, illustrating that suggestions are not a restricted set.

title: Validate Multiple Email Entries Without Claiming Delivery
description: Use native email fields for one address or a comma-separated list. Distinguish syntax validation from mailbox verification and explain the expected format.
body:
An input type="email" can check the browser’s email-address syntax rules. With multiple, it accepts a comma-separated list instead of one address. Neither setting proves that an address exists, receives mail or belongs to the person entering it.

Explain the list format next to the field

<label for="reviewers">Reviewer email addresses</label>
<input id="reviewers" name="reviewers" type="email" multiple
       aria-describedby="reviewers-help">
<p id="reviewers-help">Separate addresses with commas. Optional.</p>

This example is intentionally optional. Test it with a blank value, one specimen address and two comma-separated addresses such as alex@example.com, sam@example.org. Also try a semicolon-separated list and a display-name format. Do not promise that formats accepted by a mail application will satisfy the browser’s input rules.

Reference: HTML Standard email input rules and required-field constraint.

Distinguish syntax from the product requirement

Use validity.typeMismatch to investigate a syntax failure and validity.valueMissing to investigate a required field left empty. Add required and update the visible instructions if at least one address is mandatory. Define additional minimum or maximum recipient counts separately and test the empty, single-address and multiple-address cases in supported browsers.

Avoid adding a short improvised regex that rejects ordinary valid addresses. If an organization limits invitations to a domain or a maximum recipient count, explain that rule and enforce it on the server. Native validation helps the interaction but cannot authorize recipients, stop a forged request or establish mailbox ownership.

Make rejection recoverable

  • Keep the original entry available for editing after an error.
  • Describe whether commas, a single address or a particular domain is expected.
  • Check paste behavior and the keyboard on an actual mobile device.
  • Confirm server parsing and browser feedback agree on representative cases.

Show a delivery or verification status only when the corresponding backend operation supports it. “Address format accepted” and “Invitation delivered” are different observations. For custom rules, follow the validity-state clearing workflow so an old message does not keep a corrected field blocked.
coverAlt: A comma-separated list of example email addresses passes through separate syntax and mailbox checks; accepting syntax does not establish delivery.

title: Why a Flex Item Ignores Its Declared Width
description: Trace a flex item’s starting size through flex-basis, width, growth and shrinkage. Use a controlled layout to distinguish a basis from the final width.
keyword: css flex basis vs width ignored
body:
In a horizontal flex row, a definite flex-basis supplies the starting main size in preference to width. That starting size is still subject to growth, shrinkage and minimum-size constraints. Comparing only the width declaration with the final box skips the algorithm that runs between them.

Start with a case that cannot grow or shrink

.row { display: flex; gap: 1rem; }
.sample {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  width: 18rem;
  flex: 0 0 12rem;
}

In a sufficiently wide row with no conflicting minimum or maximum, the sample starts and stays at a 12rem border-box width. Switch its basis to auto and the declared 18rem width becomes relevant to the starting size. Change one property at a time and measure the item’s border box in DevTools.

Reference: MDN flex-basis.

Reintroduce the constraints deliberately

Now set flex: 1 1 12rem. Extra room can enlarge the item and insufficient room can shrink it. The 12rem basis is no longer a promised final width. Add a second item and compare short content with an unbroken identifier; an automatic minimum can prevent the shrinkage you expected.

Check the main axis as well. With column direction, flex-basis participates in height sizing rather than serving as another width control. Percentage bases also need a definite main size to resolve as expected; an indefinite container can produce content-based behavior. Record the container’s sizing context before copying a percentage between layouts.

Write down the intended sizing contract

  • For an inflexible item, specify its basis and whether overflow is acceptable.
  • For a flexible item, decide how surplus and deficit space should be shared.
  • Inspect minimums and maximums before adding important declarations.
  • Verify padding and borders under the chosen box-sizing model.

If the purpose is equal flexible cards, test unequal content instead of using three identical placeholders. If one control must remain legible beside shrinking text, use the button shrinkage guide to assign the constraint to the correct item. The useful handoff states which part may change size, not merely the width observed in one screenshot.
coverAlt: A flex sizing diagram starts from a 12rem basis and then applies growth, shrinkage and minimum constraints before reaching a final size.

title: Align Flex Items Within Lines and Lines Within a Container
description: Distinguish align-items from align-content in a wrapped flex layout. Create spare cross-axis space and inspect line boundaries before changing alignment.
keyword: flex align items vs align content
body:
In flexbox, align-items aligns items within each flex line. align-content distributes the lines within the container’s cross-axis space. A change to align-content can appear ineffective when the container does not have spare space or is configured as a single-line flex container.

Make the line boundaries visible

.tray {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: 1rem;
  width: 22rem;
  min-height: 20rem;
  align-items: flex-start;
  align-content: space-between;
}
.tray > .card { flex: 0 0 9rem; }
.tray > .card:nth-child(2) { min-height: 8rem; }

Use four short sample cards and give one extra content. At this width they form two lines. The tallest item helps determine its line’s size; align-items places its shorter neighbor within that line. Align-content positions the lines in the available height. The values are a debugging fixture, not a recommended fixed-size production component.

Reference: MDN align-items.

Reference: MDN align-content.

Change one alignment level at a time

Switch align-items to center and watch the short card within its line. Then switch align-content to center and watch the group of lines. Remove the minimum height and compare again. If the content uses all the available height, there may be no surplus for line distribution to make visible.

With flex-wrap: nowrap, align-content has no effect in flexbox even if the container is tall. Do not generalize that rule to every layout mode: grid and block alignment have their own behavior. An individual flex item can also override the group’s align-items value through align-self.

Follow the axes, not the screenshot

For a row in horizontal writing, the cross axis is vertical. Change flex-direction or writing mode and that visual shortcut no longer holds. Inspect the container’s direction and wrapping before treating “center” as a vertical alignment instruction.

  • Test one card, two lines and an uneven final line.
  • Use long text so items have different heights.
  • Remove temporary dimensions before shipping.
  • Retest the layout at narrow widths and enlarged text.

Use the layout comparison if the actual requirement is shared row and column tracks. Alignment properties can distribute available space, but they cannot give a flex layout the same track structure as a grid.
coverAlt: Two flex lines sit in a tall container; blue shorter items align within their line while green outlines show the two line regions being distributed.

title: Keep Padding and Backgrounds on Wrapped Inline Labels
description: Compare slice and clone for a highlighted phrase that wraps across lines. Review box-decoration-break fallbacks, line spacing and real text selection.
keyword: css box decoration break clone wrapped text
body:
A highlighted inline phrase can break into several line fragments. With box-decoration-break: clone, each fragment gets its own decoration instead of looking like a slice through one continuous box. This is useful for a marker-style background behind a heading phrase that must wrap naturally.

Keep the phrase inline

.heading {
  max-width: 18ch;
  line-height: 1.5;
}
.heading > .highlight {
  padding: .05em .25em;
  border-radius: .2em;
  background: #d9f2e5;
  color: #163327;
  -webkit-box-decoration-break: clone;
  box-decoration-break: clone;
}

Put ordinary text inside a span with the highlight class, and keep that span inline. Turning it into inline-block creates one atomic inline box, which changes the wrapping problem rather than solving the decoration of fragments. Use a phrase long enough to wrap into two or three lines at the test width.

Reference: MDN box-decoration-break.

Compare the two fragment models

Temporarily set the property to slice. Inspect the beginning and end of each line: cloned decorations can repeat padding, border treatment and background painting for each fragment. The effect is especially clear with rounded ends. Choose the behavior that matches the design rather than treating either value as universally correct.

Support varies across browsers and fragmentation contexts, so review the browsers you ship to. The prefixed declaration provides a compatibility path in engines that require it for this treatment. The text must stay readable when the decorative enhancement is ignored; do not encode necessary state solely through a perfect capsule shape.

Check wrapping, spacing and selection together

  • Resize until a single word moves between lines.
  • Increase font size and verify adjacent highlights do not collide.
  • Select and copy the phrase to confirm it remains real text.
  • Check the foreground against the actual highlight color.

Vertical padding on an inline element can paint beyond the line’s normal metrics. Give the heading enough line height and inspect collisions instead of adding a fixed height to contain them. Keep the full phrase available; replacing it with an image makes responsive wrapping and text selection harder.
coverAlt: A two-line highlighted phrase has separate rounded backgrounds and padding on each line, illustrating cloned inline decorations.

title: Use an Outline Without Changing the Element’s Layout Size
description: Compare outlines and borders when a focus or selection treatment shifts nearby content. Inspect clipping and contrast without hiding the focus indicator.
keyword: css outline vs border layout size
body:
A border participates in the CSS box model. An outline is painted around the element without reserving layout space. When adding a state indicator makes nearby content jump, compare those mechanisms before compensating with negative margins.

Create a state that keeps its dimensions

.sample-action {
  padding: .65rem 1rem;
  border: 1px solid #66756c;
  border-radius: .5rem;
  background: white;
  color: #183126;
}
.sample-action:focus-visible {
  outline: 3px solid #174fa0;
  outline-offset: 3px;
}

Measure the button before and after keyboard focus. Its border remains the same width; the outline adds a visible ring without increasing the layout box. These colors and dimensions are a specimen to test against your surfaces, not a completed accessibility assessment.

Reference: MDN outline property.

Choose where the state should be drawn

A selection border may be part of a component’s design even when focus uses an outline. Reserve its maximum thickness in the base state, then change color, if the border should not change size. With border-box sizing and a fixed width, thicker borders can reduce the content area instead of enlarging the outside box; text can still reflow.

Outline-offset controls the space between the outline and the border edge. Positive offsets can collide with neighboring controls or be clipped by an ancestor. Inspect the painted result inside scroll panels, rounded containers and dialogs. An unchanged bounding box does not prove the indicator is visible.

Verify both the visual and keyboard states

  • Tab into and out of the component without forcing pseudo-classes.
  • Compare box dimensions and nearby text wrapping.
  • Check every adjacent background and selected state.
  • Review forced-colors mode and clipping ancestors.

Do not remove the browser outline unless an effective focus treatment replaces it. A box-shadow can be decorative, but its behavior under forced colors differs from an outline or border. Use the forced-colors review to evaluate the actual result. Record focus and selection independently in the component state inventory so a selected item does not accidentally lose its keyboard indicator.
coverAlt: An outline surrounds a button outside its border while a nearby button remains in place, showing a painted ring that does not reserve layout space.

title: Stabilize Table Columns with table-layout: fixed
description: Use fixed table layout with an explicit table width and intentional column sizes. Test long cell content without hiding values or losing table semantics.
keyword: css table layout fixed column width
body:
Fixed table layout calculates horizontal structure from the table width and column constraints rather than continually sizing columns around every cell’s content. It can make a predictable table easier to scan, but it does not make long values disappear safely or guarantee that every table fits a phone.

Give the algorithm an explicit width

<table class="assets">
  <caption>Example asset inventory</caption>
  <colgroup><col class="asset-name"><col></colgroup>
  <thead><tr><th scope="col">Name</th><th scope="col">Notes</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody><tr><td>navigation.svg</td><td>Primary navigation icon</td></tr></tbody>
</table>
.assets { width: 100%; table-layout: fixed; }
.assets .asset-name { width: 35%; }
.assets th, .assets td {
  padding: .75rem;
  text-align: start;
  vertical-align: top;
  overflow-wrap: anywhere;
}

The first column takes the specified share and the other receives remaining space in this two-column example. With an automatic table width, requesting fixed layout does not produce the same fixed-width behavior. Inspect the computed table width before changing cell declarations.

Reference: MDN table-layout.

Test values that challenge the column contract

Replace the short asset name with a long identifier, add a multiline note and insert more rows. The goal is stable column boundaries with understandable content. A wrapping policy can increase row height; that is often preferable to concealing information. Avoid assuming that fixed layout is also a truncation rule.

If the design requires ellipsis, provide an accessible way to reach the complete value. A tooltip that appears only on mouse hover is not enough. For a comparison table that genuinely needs more width, retain the table and use a deliberate scrolling region rather than squeezing each column into unreadable fragments.

Preserve relationships while changing geometry

  • Keep a caption and correctly associated headers.
  • Test a narrow container and enlarged text.
  • Check the longest identifier and translated column headings.
  • Verify copied and exported data retains complete values.

Use the responsive table guide for the surrounding overflow strategy. Use fixed layout when the column plan is known and useful; keep automatic layout when content-driven column sizing better serves the data. The choice should follow the reading task, not merely the first row’s appearance.
coverAlt: A two-column asset table uses a 35 percent name column and a remaining notes column, with a long name wrapping inside stable boundaries.

title: Count the Right Siblings with nth-child and nth-of-type
description: Debug structural selectors in mixed HTML. Compare sibling position, element type and filtered nth-child queries before using positional component styles.
keyword: css nth child vs nth of type
body:
The difference between :nth-child() and :nth-of-type() is the set being counted. The first counts element siblings; the second counts siblings with the same element type. A class before either pseudo-class filters the match but does not automatically change that counting set.

Use a mixed sibling fixture

<section class="results">
  <h2>Saved samples</h2>
  <article class="card">First sample</article>
  <aside>Review note</aside>
  <article class="card">Second sample</article>
</section>
.results > .card:nth-child(2) { border-color: blue; }
.results > .card:nth-of-type(2) { background: #e7f3ec; }

The first rule matches the first article because it is the second element child. The second rule matches the second article because it is the second article sibling. Text nodes and whitespace do not increment these element positions. Inspect the matched elements instead of guessing from how many cards you see.

Reference: MDN nth-child.

Reference: MDN nth-of-type.

Filter the counting set when that is the intent

For the second sibling carrying a class, :nth-child(2 of .card) expresses a filtered counting set. Check target-browser support before depending on that selector. It differs from .card:nth-child(2), which asks whether the second element child happens to have the class.

Hiding an element with CSS does not remove it from structural counting. A hidden row can therefore disturb alternating stripes. Where supported, a filtered selector can explicitly exclude the hidden rows. A framework that removes the node entirely creates a different DOM, so test both visibility and rendering conditions.

Avoid tying meaning to an accidental position

  • Insert a heading or notice before the cards.
  • Hide one item, then remove it in a separate test.
  • Mix element types that share the same component class.
  • Check which selectors actually match in DevTools.

If the second card is special because it is “recommended,” give it an explicit state class or attribute. Use structural selectors for structure, such as alternating presentation, rather than encoding product meaning that breaks when content is reordered. For a matching rule that still loses, continue with the cascade debugging guide.
coverAlt: A sibling list contains a heading, first article, note and second article; labels identify the first article as child two and the second as article two.

title: Contain a Floated Image with display: flow-root
description: Keep a floated illustration inside its section without using overflow as a layout fix. Compare float containment, clipping and deliberate text wrapping.
body:
A section containing a floated image can appear shorter than the image when its normal-flow text ends early. Use display: flow-root on the section to establish a block formatting context that contains its floats, while preserving text wrapping around the image.

Reproduce the short-text case

.editorial-note {
  display: flow-root;
  padding: 1rem;
  border: 1px solid #ccd5ce;
}
.editorial-note img {
  float: inline-start;
  width: 8rem;
  height: auto;
  margin-inline-end: 1rem;
  margin-block-end: .5rem;
}

Place an image and one short paragraph inside the section. Temporarily remove flow-root and inspect whether the border encloses the float. Then restore it and compare with a much longer paragraph. The container should behave sensibly in both fixtures, rather than relying on enough text to push its bottom edge down.

Reference: MDN block formatting contexts.

Separate containment from clipping

Overflow rules can create a block formatting context too, but they also carry scrolling or clipping consequences. Using overflow hidden merely to contain a float may cut off a shadow, a focus indicator or an overlapping decoration. Flow-root makes the containment purpose explicit without asking for clipping.

This does not make arbitrary absolutely positioned children contribute to the section’s height. It addresses float behavior within the new formatting context. It can also affect margin collapsing at the boundary, so review the first and last text margins rather than assuming every spacing relationship stays identical.

Confirm that a float is still the right layout

Floats are useful when prose should wrap beside an illustration and later continue beneath it. If the requirement is a rigid image-and-text pair with independent columns, grid or flexbox is usually easier to specify. Choose based on the flow of content, not on which property first makes a screenshot resemble a mockup.

  • Test a short paragraph and several long paragraphs.
  • Check narrow widths where the illustration dominates the line.
  • Inspect outlines and shadows near the section’s edges.
  • Check the margin boundary after enabling flow-root.

For overflow changes, review hidden versus clip separately. The final handoff should say whether the illustration floats within prose, sits in a separate track or intentionally overlaps the section; these are different layout contracts.
coverAlt: A section boundary encloses a floated image and a short paragraph, demonstrating float containment without clipping the content.

title: Continue or Reverse an Ordered List with Native HTML
description: Set ordered-list numbering with start, reversed and item values. Keep the document’s reading order meaningful instead of using CSS to fake a sequence.
keyword: html ordered list start reversed value
body:
Use an ordered list when the sequence of items matters. HTML can continue a sequence with start, count downward with reversed, and set a particular item’s ordinal with value. Those attributes change numbering without asking CSS to reorder the content.

Continue a sequence after an interruption

<ol start="4">
  <li>Review the responsive layout.</li>
  <li>Check the keyboard path.</li>
  <li>Record unresolved issues.</li>
</ol>

The start value is an integer even when the marker style is alphabetic or Roman. This example begins at the fourth step because earlier steps would exist elsewhere in the same document. Do not start at four simply to make a decorative label look interesting; readers should understand the continued sequence.

Reference: MDN ordered list attributes.

Distinguish countdown numbering from DOM reversal

<ol reversed start="3">
  <li>Third-place example</li>
  <li>Second-place example</li>
  <li>First-place example</li>
</ol>

This illustrative ranking is already written in the intended reading order. Reversed makes its numbering descend; it does not reverse the elements themselves. Without an explicit start, a reversed list begins from its number of list items. Adding or removing an item can therefore change the starting number.

An integer value on a list item establishes that item’s ordinal and affects the numbering that follows. Use it for a real interruption or special numbering requirement, and test dynamic insertions. For a normal uninterrupted list, letting the browser calculate the sequence is simpler than manually maintaining every value.

Keep visible numbers and content meaning aligned

  • Read the items in DOM order without CSS.
  • Add and remove a middle item and inspect the sequence.
  • Check copy, print and screen-reader behavior for your supported environment.
  • Avoid duplicating typed numbers beside native markers.

Use marker styling for visual treatment and CSS counters for appropriate generated section labels. A list’s ordinal is not always a sufficient stable identifier: if another document needs to refer permanently to a requirement, give that requirement a durable ID in the content model.
coverAlt: One ordered list continues at four, five and six; a second counts down three, two and one while preserving the written item order.

title: Use Superscripts and Subscripts for Meaningful Notation
description: Mark up exponents and chemical subscripts with HTML while keeping line spacing readable. Avoid using semantic notation elements for decorative badges.
keyword: html sup sub superscript subscript line height
body:
Use sup and sub when raised or lowered notation belongs to the content, such as a simple exponent or chemical formula. Do not choose them merely because a promotional badge needs to sit higher beside a heading; decorative placement should be handled with CSS.

Start with semantic notation

<p>The square has an area of 25 m<sup>2</sup>.</p>
<p>The label describes H<sub>2</sub>O.</p>

Read the surrounding sentence as well as the small characters. The superscript 2 describes a square unit; the subscript 2 contributes to the formula. Keep ordinary text intact and let the HTML express that relationship rather than embedding a picture of the notation.

Reference: MDN superscript element.

Reference: MDN subscript element.

Review line metrics before applying a reset

Superscripts and subscripts can affect the line box. Compare a paragraph with notation against one without it using the actual typeface, font size and line height. A cramped line can collide with a neighboring line even if the characters look well aligned in an isolated word.

If the design requires a compact treatment, evaluate it locally instead of applying a global line-height zero rule to every sup and sub. A zero line height can keep notation from expanding the line box while leaving the painted glyphs able to overlap adjacent content. Test high and low glyphs, consecutive lines and enlarged text before accepting that tradeoff.

Use a richer representation for richer content

Simple HTML notation is not a complete mathematical typesetting system. For structured equations, consider MathML and review the accessibility of the actual output. A footnote marker also needs a link and a usable return path when navigation is intended; a raised digit alone does not provide either interaction.

  • Copy the notation and inspect the resulting plain text.
  • Read the sentence with the screen readers you support.
  • Review narrow paragraphs and increased text spacing.
  • Check that small glyphs remain legible rather than shrinking them to preserve a rigid line.

Use the line-height guide to understand inherited spacing and the inline alignment guide for decorative icon placement. Separating meaning from positioning makes both the content and its styling easier to maintain.
coverAlt: A square-meter expression uses a raised two while a water formula uses a lowered two, separating meaningful notation from decorative placement.

title: Choose Whether a Background Follows the Box or Its Content
description: Compare local, scroll and fixed background attachment inside a scrolling panel. Test panel and page movement separately before copying a visual effect.
keyword: css background attachment local vs scroll
body:
Inside a scrolling panel, a background can stay attached to the panel’s box or move with its content. background-attachment: scroll uses the box; local follows the scrollable contents. The names are easy to misread unless you test the panel’s scrolling separately from the whole page.

Build a panel with an obvious visual landmark

.notes-panel {
  max-height: 14rem;
  overflow: auto;
  padding: 1rem;
  background-image: linear-gradient(#dcebe3 0 4rem, white 4rem);
  background-repeat: no-repeat;
  background-attachment: local;
}

Fill the panel with enough text to scroll. The colored band provides a simple landmark without needing an external image. Scroll only the panel and observe the band, then change local to scroll and repeat. Keep the same content and panel dimensions so the attachment is the only variable.

Reference: MDN background-attachment.

Test the outer page independently

With scroll, the background stays with the element as the page moves, but does not travel with the element’s internally scrolling contents. With fixed, the background is attached to the viewport. Scroll the page while the panel remains partly visible to distinguish that viewport attachment from the other cases.

For multiple backgrounds, attachment values correspond to image layers. Inspect the full image and attachment lists together; a gradient used for a scroll cue may intentionally behave differently from a decorative texture. Also review background-origin and clipping rather than assuming attachment alone defines the painted region.

Keep the effect optional

Mobile browsers, compositing and surrounding transforms can complicate a fixed-background design. Test the actual device and component context. Do not claim a screenshot proves the scrolling behavior, and do not hide an essential boundary or instruction inside a decorative background effect.
