  • Scroll the panel while holding the page position constant.
  • Scroll the page without changing the panel’s scroll position.
  • Review text contrast at every part of the background.
  • Check performance and motion comfort on target devices.

Use a plain readable surface as the fallback. If the effect creates apparent motion behind content, include it in the motion review. For misplaced painting boundaries, continue with background origin and clip instead of compensating with unexplained padding.
coverAlt: A scrollable box separates its outer boundary from its content, with local attached to the moving content and scroll attached to the box.

title: Compare Optical Sizing with the Actual Font File
description: Review font-optical-sizing at reading and display sizes. Verify the font’s opsz support and isolate axis overrides before attributing a mismatch to CSS.
keyword: css font optical sizing auto none opsz
body:
Optical sizing lets a supporting typeface adapt its forms to the size at which it is rendered. The difference can be subtle: it is not simply another font-size setting. Before comparing auto and none, confirm that the loaded face actually supports optical sizing.

Create a controlled specimen

.specimen {
  font-family: "Your Optical Font", serif;
  font-weight: 400;
  letter-spacing: normal;
}
.specimen--auto { font-optical-sizing: auto; }
.specimen--none { font-optical-sizing: none; }
.specimen--reading { font-size: 1rem; }
.specimen--display { font-size: 3rem; }

Replace the placeholder family with a licensed font you have loaded and verified. Show the same sentence in all four combinations of size and optical setting. Keep width, weight, spacing and browser zoom consistent. If one specimen wraps differently, inspect that outcome rather than silently changing its tracking to force a match.

Reference: MDN font-optical-sizing.

Check the axis and the winning declaration

Variable fonts commonly expose the optical-size axis as opsz. Inspect the file’s documented axes and the actual rendered face, including fallback. A CSS declaration can compute successfully even when the selected font has no optical-size behavior to apply.

Look for a low-level font-variation-settings declaration that explicitly sets opsz. An axis override can change the behavior you expected from the higher-level property. Isolate that declaration in your specimen instead of removing every variation setting from the live component, where weight or custom axes may be intentional.

Record an observable design decision

  • Capture the font file and version used for the comparison.
  • Review small labels, body text and large headings.
  • Inspect punctuation, narrow counters and dense letter combinations.
  • Compare the result at the intended size, not only in an enlarged screenshot.

Do not infer that auto always produces a dramatic difference or that none represents the designer’s intended appearance. The choice depends on the face and the layout. Record which setting you reviewed and any explicit axis values so the typography can be reproduced. Use the variable-font axis guide for the broader file-to-CSS mapping and font loading checks if both specimens are unexpectedly identical.
coverAlt: A typography review matrix compares auto and none at reading and display sizes, with a reminder to verify optical-axis support in the loaded font.

title: Inspect Ligatures Without Changing the Underlying Text
description: Diagnose joined glyphs with font-variant-ligatures and a controlled specimen. Keep characters intact while checking font features, fallback and readability.
keyword: css font variant ligatures disable joined letters
body:
A ligature can render a sequence of characters as a combined glyph. If two letters look joined, inspect the font’s features before inserting spaces or changing the source text. Glyph substitution and the characters people copy are different layers of the typography.

Compare the same text with one feature changed

.sample {
  font-family: "Your Text Font", serif;
  font-size: 2rem;
  letter-spacing: normal;
}
.sample--common { font-variant-ligatures: common-ligatures; }
.sample--without { font-variant-ligatures: no-common-ligatures; }

Use a verified loaded font and a phrase containing candidate pairs such as “office file.” Not every font includes the same substitutions, so no visible change is a valid observation. Compare the same characters, weight and width; changing the text between samples makes it impossible to isolate the feature.

Reference: MDN font-variant-ligatures.

Inspect the right category of feature

Common, discretionary and historical ligatures are different feature categories. Contextual alternates are related but separately controllable. The broad value none disables the feature categories covered by this property; no-common-ligatures targets the common ligature category. Choose the narrow control that expresses the design requirement.

Check low-level font-feature-settings rules and inherited typography styles if the result differs from the local specimen. Confirm the rendered font too: a fallback can have entirely different glyphs. A tighter pair without a changed shape may be kerning rather than a ligature, so compare the outlines as well as the space between them.

Preserve the content contract

  • Copy and paste the sample into a plain text field.
  • Search for the original word in the page.
  • Review long reading passages rather than isolated pairs only.
  • Test any code font separately using real operators and identifiers.

For code, disabling optional substitutions can make individual characters easier to inspect, but it does not change what the code contains. For connected scripts, avoid indiscriminately disabling typographic behavior just to resemble a Latin specimen. Test the actual language and font rather than treating every join as a defect.

Record the requested feature setting alongside the font source. Use the kerning comparison when spacing is the issue and tracking guidance when the entire run is too loose or tight. Do not use invisible characters or extra spaces as a visual repair.
coverAlt: A font feature comparison keeps the source phrase office file identical in both samples, distinguishing glyph behavior from underlying characters.

title: Indent a Paragraph’s First Line Without Padding Every Line
description: Use text-indent for a first-line paragraph treatment. Compare it with padding, inspect inheritance and test narrow widths before applying an editorial style.
keyword: css text indent first line vs padding
body:
Use text-indent when the first line should start inward while later lines return to the normal text edge. Padding moves the content edge for every line. They can look similar in a one-line paragraph, so compare them using text that wraps.

Apply the treatment to a deliberate paragraph sequence

.essay {
  max-inline-size: 65ch;
  line-height: 1.6;
}
.essay p { margin-block: 0; }
.essay p + p { text-indent: 1.25em; }

This original editorial pattern indents a paragraph only when another paragraph immediately precedes it. A paragraph after a heading is not indented by that selector. Decide whether that is the intended reading rhythm; do not apply it to form help, status messages or card descriptions just because they also use paragraph elements.

Reference: MDN text-indent.

Inspect units and inheritance

An em value scales with the text size. A percentage is relative to the containing block’s width, so the indent can change substantially as the reading column grows. Inspect the computed declaration and the containing block instead of interpreting a percentage as a share of the first word.

Text-indent is inherited. If the rule is placed high in a component tree, nested blocks may receive an unexpected indent. Keep the selector scoped and reset the value on intentionally different nested text where necessary. Negative indents can push text outside its box; they need a clear layout reason and overflow review.

Compare the real reading experience

  • Use several multiline paragraphs with different opening words.
  • Resize the text column and increase the font size.
  • Insert a heading, a quote and a list between paragraphs.
  • Review right-to-left content in its correct direction and language.

Avoid stacking a large indent, large paragraph gaps and narrow columns without evaluating the resulting rhythm. Each treatment signals a break; combining them can make short copy feel fragmented. For a hanging label or a numbered instruction, semantic lists or a small grid may express the structure better than an unusual indent.

Use the reading-width guide to set the column context, then compare indentation with paragraph spacing in the actual typeface. Capture the selector rule in the handoff so the style follows content structure rather than being manually added to selected paragraphs.
coverAlt: A paragraph’s first line starts inward while subsequent lines return to the normal edge, distinguishing text indentation from padding every line.

title: Use CSS Columns for Flowing Text, Not Card Row Layout
description: Create readable multi-column text with a preferred column width and gap. Inspect the reading path, fragmentation and narrow-screen fallback before shipping.
keyword: css columns column width reading order
body:
CSS multi-column layout flows content down one column and then into the next. It is useful for some editorial and print layouts, but it is not a row-by-row card grid. Choose it only when that reading path matches the task and stays practical on the available screen.

Start with a preferred column width

.reference-copy {
  column-width: 20rem;
  column-gap: 2rem;
  column-rule: 1px solid #cdd6d0;
}
.reference-copy h2 { break-after: avoid; }
.reference-copy .short-note { break-inside: avoid; }

Fill the container with real headings and paragraphs. The column width is a preferred size used with the available space; it is not a promise that every column always measures exactly 20rem. Resize the parent and inspect the number and width of columns instead of forcing a fixed count at every viewport.

Reference: MDN multi-column layout concepts.

Review fragmentation as part of the content

A paragraph can continue in another column. Break-avoid requests help keep a short note or heading relationship together, but they are not an unlimited guarantee when the content cannot fit. Do not apply break-inside avoid to every large section and then expect the browser to balance arbitrarily long blocks perfectly.

Without a constrained height, a long article can produce tall columns that require readers to scroll down and then return upward for the next column. With a fixed height, content may produce additional columns that overflow horizontally. Test both the length of the document and the container’s height before deciding the pattern is appropriate.

Follow the actual reading and keyboard path

  • Read from the beginning of the first column to the next.
  • Tab through any links in the same content order.
  • Test headings near a column boundary and a long unbroken value.
  • Check enlarged text and a single-column narrow layout.

The DOM remains the content’s sequence; a visual arrangement that suggests reading across rows can conflict with it. Use grid or flexbox when items need that row-based relationship. For print, evaluate the columns in the print stylesheet separately, because page fragmentation adds another boundary. Keep an ordinary single-column view when it better supports reading.
coverAlt: Two text columns are numbered in reading order: down the first column, then down the second, rather than across matching rows.

title: Set Component Styling Boundaries with CSS @scope
description: Use CSS scope roots and limits to target a component subtree. Inspect inherited values, fallback styles and competing rules before relying on isolation.
body:
Use @scope to restrict where a group of selectors can match. A scope root identifies the component region; an optional limit excludes a nested region. This can keep local styling readable without continually extending selectors to mirror every wrapper in the DOM.

Define a root and a nested limit

@scope (.review-card) to (.embedded-preview) {
  .title { margin-block: 0 .75rem; }
  .action { border-color: #286b4a; }
}

Place a title and action inside a review card, then add an embedded preview with its own title and action. The rules target the card’s eligible descendants, excluding the limit element and its subtree. Use the same class names in both areas to make the boundary observable, rather than testing only unrelated names.

Reference: MDN scope roots, limits and cascade behavior.

Check inheritance separately from matching

A scope limit is not an inheritance barrier. If a scoped rule changes color on an ancestor, descendants beyond the limit can still inherit that color. Inspect whether an unexpected value comes from a matched rule on the element or an inherited value from its parent.

The selector that identifies the root does not simply get prepended to every scoped selector for specificity. Scoping proximity also participates in cascade resolution after specificity. If a rule loses, inspect the complete cascade rather than assuming the nearest component always wins over importance, layers or a more specific selector.

Keep an understandable fallback

  • Test a component alone and nested inside another instance.
  • Add an embedded widget using the same class names.
  • Inspect inherited color and font separately from box properties.
  • Check the actual browser versions in your support policy.

Older browsers can ignore an unsupported at-rule, so retain essential readable base styles outside the enhancement when needed. This is not the same boundary as Shadow DOM. Record what the scope selects, what it excludes and which inherited defaults remain intentional. That gives a later maintainer a concrete contract when markup changes.
coverAlt: A review card scope contains a title and action, with an embedded preview marked as an excluded subtree; inheritance is shown as a separate consideration.

title: Read Native CSS Nesting Without Miscounting Specificity
description: Use the nesting selector to distinguish component states from descendants. Check selector-list specificity and browser-parsed CSS when refactoring styles.
body:
In native CSS nesting, & refers to the parent selector. It helps distinguish a state of the component itself from a descendant inside it. Read the resulting relationship before treating nested syntax as a shorter spelling of every preprocessor pattern.

Separate component states from child selectors

.sample-card {
  padding: 1rem;
  &.is-selected { border-color: #286b4a; }
  & .title { margin-block-start: 0; }
  &:focus-within { background: #edf6f0; }
}

The first nested rule targets a card that also has the selected class. The second targets a title inside a card. The third targets the card when focus is within it. Adding a space before the selected class would change the first relationship to a descendant match.

Reference: MDN native CSS nesting.

Inspect selector lists before refactoring

The nesting selector uses the highest specificity in its associated selector list, similar to :is(). Mixing an ID selector and a class selector in that list can therefore make a nested rule harder to override than a separately written class-only descendant rule.

#featured, .sample-card {
  & .title { color: #174fa0; }
}

Do not assume the class-matching branch contributes only class-level specificity here. Keep unrelated ID and class selectors separate when that stronger weight is accidental. Compare the winning rule before and after a refactor with a real component fixture.

Reference: MDN nesting specificity.

Verify the CSS the browser receives

  • Test selected and unselected cards.
  • Move focus between two controls inside the card.
  • Inspect a title inside a nested card instance.
  • Check whether a build tool rewrites the source before delivery.

Native nesting is parsed by the browser; a preprocessor can have different syntax and compilation rules. Avoid assuming a concatenation pattern such as a component suffix works identically. Use the cascade inspection workflow on the delivered stylesheet, and preserve the behavior rather than just the source indentation.
coverAlt: Two nested CSS relationships contrast a selected state on the same card with a title descendant inside the card.

title: Submit a Form from JavaScript Without Skipping Validation
description: Compare requestSubmit with submit when JavaScript starts a form action. Preserve native validation, submit events and the intended submit button’s behavior.
body:
Use requestSubmit() when JavaScript should initiate the normal form-submission path, including validation and a submit event. Calling submit() directly bypasses those two steps. That difference explains why the same form can reject an empty field with a button but send it through a script.

Name the intended submit button

<form id="review">
  <label for="review-title">Review title</label>
  <input id="review-title" name="title" required>
  <button id="save-review" type="submit" name="action" value="save">
    Save review
  </button>
</form>
const form = document.querySelector('#review');
const save = document.querySelector('#save-review');
// Call in response to the intended application action:
form.requestSubmit(save);

Run this in a controlled fixture before connecting a real endpoint. Leave the title empty, then fill it and repeat. A supplied submitter must be a submit button associated with that form. Passing a different element or a button belonging to another form is not a valid shortcut.

Reference: MDN requestSubmit.

Preserve the event contract

A submit handler can prevent navigation and implement an asynchronous request, but it should not call requestSubmit again unconditionally: that can re-enter its own event path. Decide where the application transitions from native validation to custom transport, and keep that transition explicit.

Direct submit does not fire the submit event and does not perform constraint validation. It is therefore unsuitable when your logic depends on that handler or on the browser checking required fields. A control named submit can also mask the form’s submit method, making a seemingly ordinary method call fail.

Reference: MDN submit method differences.

Test each initiation path

  • Activate the native button with pointer and keyboard.
  • Initiate the programmatic path with invalid and valid values.
  • Confirm the expected submitter and action value.
  • Verify the server independently validates the request.

Use the submitter guide when the form has more than one action. Native client validation improves interaction; it does not replace server validation or authorization.
coverAlt: A requestSubmit flow goes through validation and the submit event before transport; a direct submit path is distinguished as bypassing those steps.

title: Identify Which Button Submitted a Multi-Action Form
description: Use SubmitEvent.submitter for forms with multiple actions. Preserve button name and value data, handle missing submitters and test Enter-key submission.
keyword: submit event submitter multiple buttons formdata
body:
A form can have multiple submit buttons with different action values. Read event.submitter in the form’s submit handler to identify the initiating control. Checking only the last button clicked is fragile because submission can also begin through a keyboard or programmatic path.

Give actions explicit data values

<form id="review-actions">
  <label for="review-name">Name</label>
  <input id="review-name" name="name" required>
  <button type="submit" name="intent" value="save">Save</button>
  <button type="submit" name="intent" value="preview">Preview</button>
</form>
const form = document.querySelector('#review-actions');
form.addEventListener('submit', event => {
  event.preventDefault(); // Local diagnostic fixture only.
  const submitter = event.submitter;
  const data = submitter
    ? new FormData(form, submitter)
    : new FormData(form);
  console.log(data.get('intent'));
});

Both actions in this fixture use normal validation. The two-argument FormData constructor includes the named submitter’s entry. Building FormData from the form alone does not preserve that clicked button’s name/value pair. Use specimen values for diagnostics rather than logging private form data.

Reference: MDN SubmitEvent.submitter.

Keep server actions and UI actions aligned

A button can override submission attributes such as the destination with formaction. Decide whether the native form transport or a JavaScript handler owns that routing. A custom fetch handler must deliberately preserve the intended behavior; it does not automatically honor every attribute merely because the DOM contains it.

Reference: MDN button submission attributes.

Handle a missing submitter explicitly according to the product contract. Do not guess that preview or publish was intended. The server should allow only recognized action values and independently check permissions before acting.

Test beyond clicking both buttons

  • Press Enter from the text field and inspect the resulting intent.
  • Call requestSubmit with a specific submit button.
  • Try invalid input before each action.
  • Confirm duplicate activation cannot accidentally perform an action twice.

If a helper action should never submit, use type="button" instead. Keep this pattern for actions that genuinely share the form’s submission and validation lifecycle.
coverAlt: Save and Preview submit buttons carry separate intent values, and an event inspector records which button initiated the form submission.

title: Fix a Number Field That Rejects an In-Range Decimal
description: Debug stepMismatch separately from minimum and maximum errors. Choose a numeric step and base that match the permitted increments, then explain them clearly.
keyword: html input number step mismatch decimal min
body:
A number can be between min and max yet still fail a number field’s step constraint. The accepted values follow increments from a step base; they are not simply every number inside the range. Inspect validity.stepMismatch before changing unrelated range limits.

Define a deliberate sequence

<label for="spacing">Spacing increment</label>
<input id="spacing" name="spacing" type="number"
       min="0.5" max="4.5" step="0.5"
       aria-describedby="spacing-help">
<p id="spacing-help">Use 0.5 to 4.5, in increments of 0.5.</p>

In this example, 0.5, 1 and 1.5 fit the sequence; 0.75 does not. The minimum supplies the step base here. Without an applicable minimum, the value attribute can provide a base; otherwise number inputs generally use zero. An omitted step defaults to 1, which can surprise a design that visibly invites decimals.

Reference: MDN number input constraints.

Inspect the specific failure

const input = document.querySelector('#spacing');
console.table({
  value: input.value,
  stepMismatch: input.validity.stepMismatch,
  underflow: input.validity.rangeUnderflow,
  overflow: input.validity.rangeOverflow
});

Test one allowed value, one off-step value and values just outside each boundary. Keep the numeric model consistent on the server. Floating-point arithmetic and unit conversions need deliberate handling; a browser accepting the input does not prove downstream calculations preserve the intended precision.

Use step="any" when arbitrary numeric increments are permitted. It removes the step restriction, not the minimum, maximum or other validation rules. Do not set any just to silence an error if the product actually accepts half-unit increments only.

Separate quantities from identifiers

  • Try typing and pasting a decimal rather than only using spinner buttons.
  • Check the field in the supported locale and browser combinations.
  • Keep the allowed increment visible before validation fails.
  • Retain a correction path without silently rounding meaningful values.

For a postal code or an identifier with leading zeros, reconsider number input entirely. The inputmode comparison explains how to request a numeric keyboard while retaining a text value when arithmetic is not the task.
coverAlt: A number input allows half-unit increments from 0.5 to 4.5; the example 0.75 falls between valid steps despite being within the range.

title: Write HTML Patterns That Match the Whole Field Value
description: Use pattern for an explicit input format, with visible guidance and separate required handling. Test full-value matching, invalid patterns and server validation.
keyword: html pattern whole string required validation
body:
The HTML pattern attribute validates the entire nonempty value of a supported input. It is not a search for a matching fragment somewhere in the string. Begin with the allowed format and a few accepted and rejected examples before writing the expression.

Give the format a visible explanation

<label for="review-code">Review code</label>
<input id="review-code" name="code" type="text"
       pattern="[A-Z]{2}[0-9]{4}" required
       aria-describedby="review-code-help">
<p id="review-code-help">Two uppercase letters followed by four digits, such as AB0123.</p>

AB0123 matches this illustrative format. xAB0123y does not, because matching covers the whole value. An empty value fails the separate required rule. Do not wrap the pattern in JavaScript slash delimiters, and do not rely on a title-only tooltip to communicate the format.

Reference: MDN pattern attribute.

Separate missing, mismatched and malformed cases

Inspect validity.patternMismatch for a nonempty mismatch and validity.valueMissing for an empty required field. If a malformed expression causes the pattern constraint to be ignored, an apparently accepted value is not evidence that the expression works. Keep representative rejected fixtures in the review.

Modern HTML patterns use Unicode-aware v-mode semantics, including specific escaping rules within character classes. Copying a regular expression from another runtime can change its meaning or make it invalid. Prefer a simple expression for a simple rule, and check the documentation when the format includes punctuation or Unicode sets.

Match the application’s actual rules

  • Test the shortest and longest permitted values.
  • Try leading and trailing whitespace.
  • Include lowercase and non-ASCII input in the review.
  • Confirm pasted values receive the same feedback as typed values.

This sample intentionally accepts only ASCII uppercase letters and digits; it would be inappropriate for a person’s name. Do not impose a convenient regular expression on content whose legitimate forms are broader than the design sample. Decide whether normalization occurs, show the result clearly and enforce the same contract on the server.

If the rule depends on another field or asynchronous data, use the custom validity workflow with a useful correction message. Native pattern matching is one local format check, not a complete data-validation system.
coverAlt: The code AB0123 matches two uppercase letters and four digits; xAB0123y is rejected because the pattern checks the whole value.

title: Label Password Fields with the Correct Autocomplete Purpose
description: Use current-password and new-password for their intended tasks. Keep labels, paste and password-manager behavior usable across sign-in and password changes.
keyword: autocomplete current password new password fields
body:
Password fields need both a human-readable label and an accurate autocomplete purpose. Use current-password when requesting the existing credential, and new-password when creating or replacing one. The distinction helps browsers and password managers understand the task without guessing from visual position.

Describe a password-change form accurately

<label for="existing-password">Current password</label>
<input id="existing-password" name="currentPassword"
       type="password" autocomplete="current-password">
<label for="replacement-password">New password</label>
<input id="replacement-password" name="newPassword"
       type="password" autocomplete="new-password">
<label for="repeat-password">Confirm new password</label>
<input id="repeat-password" name="confirmPassword"
       type="password" autocomplete="new-password">

Add the application’s required and validation rules deliberately. A confirmation field also requests the new password; there is no separate confirm-password autocomplete token. In a sign-in form, identify the account field with autocomplete="username", even when that account identifier is an email address.

Reference: MDN autocomplete field purposes.

Review assistance instead of fighting it

Autocomplete tokens provide guidance; the browser or password manager decides how to offer suggestions and filling. Do not claim the attributes guarantee an identical popup in every environment. Test saved credentials and generated-password behavior in the combinations the product supports.

Keep paste available. Avoid clearing a field merely because its value appeared without the exact keystrokes your handler expected. A reveal-password control should be a clearly named button with type="button" so checking the value does not submit the form unexpectedly.

Test the complete task with specimen credentials

  • Fill the existing credential from a password manager.
  • Generate a new password and confirm it.
  • Paste a long value and inspect wrapping of instructions and errors.
  • Check focus, reveal controls and validation without logging passwords.

Use a test account or isolated fixture, and never print credential values into a diagnostic report. The frontend should describe actual server requirements rather than inventing a strength guarantee from a decorative meter. For the basic field relationship, keep persistent labels visible even after autofill; autocomplete is metadata, not a replacement for instructions.
coverAlt: Current password, new password and confirmation fields are mapped to current-password, new-password and new-password autocomplete purposes.

title: Apply Required Rules Correctly to Radios and Checkboxes
description: Distinguish one required radio choice from individually required checkboxes. Test group validity and visible instructions before adding a minimum-selection rule.
keyword: required radio group vs checkbox group
body:
Required behaves differently for same-named radio buttons and for checkboxes. A required radio group needs one checked choice. A required checkbox requires that particular checkbox to be checked. Marking every checkbox required does not express “choose at least one.”

Model a single required choice with radios

<fieldset>
  <legend>Review format (required)</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="format" value="brief" required> Brief</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="format" value="full" required> Full</label>
</fieldset>

One required member makes a same-named radio group require a selection; repeating the attribute consistently can make the group easier to maintain. The example’s name unites the choices for both selection and submission. Separate groups need separate names even if their labels happen to be similar.

Reference: MDN required radio and checkbox behavior.

Express a checkbox minimum separately

If users may select several export formats but must choose at least one, use checkboxes and implement the group-count rule explicitly. Put clear instructions near the group, choose a stable enabled control to carry any custom validity message, and clear that message as soon as the rule is satisfied.

Do not add required to all items as a shortcut: that makes every one mandatory. For a consent checkbox that genuinely must be checked individually, required can represent that local constraint. Group rules and individual obligations need different visible wording.

Inspect the state transitions

  • Submit a radio group with no selection, then each alternative.
  • For a checkbox minimum, test zero, one and several selections.
  • Disable or remove an option and recompute the allowed set.
  • Check that the error directs focus to a usable control and explains the correction.

A fieldset and legend communicate the group’s purpose but do not themselves implement a minimum count. Keep the native grouping structure and the validation logic aligned. If a summary checkbox shows partial selection, its indeterminate state still does not establish the group’s validity.

Validate the selection again on the server, including allowed values and any authorization rules. Client-side required checks provide timely feedback; they do not make a forged or stale request trustworthy.
coverAlt: A radio group requires one selection, while required on individual checkboxes applies separately to each checkbox; an at-least-one checkbox rule needs its own validation.

title: Inspect an Image’s Selected Source and Natural Size
description: Read currentSrc and naturalWidth alongside the rendered image box. Distinguish responsive source selection, loading success and density-corrected dimensions.
body:
An image has more than one useful size: the selected resource, its intrinsic density-corrected dimensions and the box painted by CSS. Read these separately when a responsive image looks soft or unexpectedly cropped. The src attribute alone may not identify the resource the browser selected.

Capture a complete inspection record

const img = document.querySelector('.reference-image');
await img.decode();
const box = img.getBoundingClientRect();
console.table({
  selectedURL: img.currentSrc,
  naturalWidth: img.naturalWidth,
  naturalHeight: img.naturalHeight,
  renderedWidth: box.width,
  renderedHeight: box.height
});

Use this with an actual image element and handle a rejected decode promise when loading fails. Record the viewport and device pixel ratio with the values. If the image is lazy-loaded, bring it into the intended loading conditions before interpreting a zero natural size.

Reference: MDN selected image source.

Reference: MDN naturalWidth.

Avoid comparing different units as if they were identical

Natural width is expressed in CSS pixels after density correction, so it is not always the raw pixel width of the downloaded file. A 2x candidate can have twice the resource pixels while describing the same intrinsic CSS width. Inspect the resource itself when the file dimensions are the question.

CurrentSrc tells you which URL was selected; it does not prove the resource successfully loaded. Conversely, a rendered box can exist even when the image has failed because CSS or HTML dimensions reserve space. Check the network result and decoding state before blaming object-fit.

Compare the conditions that trigger the mismatch

  • Capture the selected URL at a narrow and a wide viewport.
  • Record device pixel ratio and any emulation setting.
  • Compare CSS box dimensions with object-fit and object-position.
  • Test an uncached load when investigating responsive candidate selection.

Use the srcset and sizes workflow to correct slot assumptions. Use the image fitting guide when the resource is correct but the box crops it. Keep those diagnoses separate so a layout fix does not unnecessarily increase download size.
coverAlt: An image inspection card records the selected URL, intrinsic density-corrected size and rendered CSS box as three separate measurements.

title: Fit a Decorative Background Without Accidental Tiling
description: Compare cover and contain for CSS backgrounds, including positioning and repeat. Keep essential imagery in semantic markup and test different box shapes.
keyword: css background size cover contain repeat
body:
For a CSS background, cover fills the positioning area while preserving the image’s proportions, so some content may be cropped. Contain fits the whole image inside that area and can leave uncovered space. Set repeat deliberately when comparing them, or tiling can disguise the result.

Use the same image and box for the comparison

.decorative-panel {
  min-height: 18rem;
  background-color: #edf3ef;
  background-image: url("/images/sample-texture.webp");
  background-position: center;
  background-repeat: no-repeat;
  background-size: cover;
}

Replace the specimen URL with your own decorative asset. Switch cover to contain without changing the box, then compare a wide container and a tall one. The background color provides an intentional surface where contain leaves space. Default repeating behavior is a separate decision from sizing.

Reference: MDN background-size.

Inspect the positioning area and focal content

Background-origin determines the positioning box, while background-clip controls painting boundaries. Padding can therefore change the apparent fit in ways that are not explained by cover alone. Inspect all three properties before adjusting an image asset to compensate for a box-model difference.

A percentage background-position is not simply a fixed pixel offset. Review the crop across the component’s actual aspect ratios, especially when a decorative subject sits near an edge. For multiple layers, sizes, positions and repeats must correspond to the intended image layer.

Choose the right place for meaningful imagery

  • Test the narrowest and widest supported component shape.
  • Remove the image temporarily and check text readability.
  • Review contrast over the lightest and darkest visible areas.
  • Verify the intended fallback color and resource-loading result.

A CSS background has no alt attribute. When an image conveys information that needs a text alternative, use semantic image markup rather than hiding meaning in decoration. The object-fit guide covers fitting an actual image element inside its box. For a layered overlay, continue with background layer order and verify the text stays readable after every crop.
coverAlt: A decorative background comparison shows cover filling a box with a cropped subject and contain leaving intentional space around the complete subject.

title: Lay Out Vertical Text with writing-mode and text-orientation
description: Use writing-mode for vertical text flow and text-orientation for glyph direction. Review logical sizing, language and reading order before rotating labels.
keyword: css vertical writing mode text orientation
body:
Writing-mode changes how text lines flow through a box. Text-orientation controls the glyph orientation within vertical text. They solve a different problem from rotating an already laid-out horizontal box with transform, which leaves its original layout space behind.

Compare flow before changing individual glyphs

.rail-label {
  writing-mode: vertical-rl;
  text-orientation: mixed;
  padding-block: .75rem;
  padding-inline: 1rem;
}

Use a short real label in a component rail, then test a longer label and mixed-script text. Vertical-rl stacks lines from right to left; vertical-lr changes that progression. Mixed allows character orientation appropriate to the script, while upright requests upright characters. Do not assume those choices produce equally readable English labels.

Reference: MDN writing-mode.

Reference: MDN text-orientation.

Inspect logical dimensions and language together

In vertical writing, the inline dimension runs along the vertical text flow. A max-inline-size therefore constrains a different physical direction than it does in horizontal English text. Use logical properties deliberately and inspect the computed box instead of carrying over a width assumption from a horizontal specimen.

Language metadata remains important for the content itself. Vertical layout does not tell the browser which language the words use, and it is not a reason to alter the document’s semantic order. Keep the visible label in real text so it remains selectable and available to assistive technology.

Review the component as an interaction

  • Tab through nearby controls in document order.
  • Increase text size and test the longest label.
  • Review a narrow viewport where the rail may need a horizontal fallback.
  • Check mixed Latin and non-Latin characters in the actual font.

If the design merely asks for a short decorative sideways word, compare the layout consequences of rotation before choosing it. For functional navigation, prioritize legibility and predictable controls over the shape of the rail. The logical-properties guide helps record which dimensions follow text flow and which intentionally stay physical.
coverAlt: A vertical text-flow diagram separates the inline direction from the progression of successive lines, reminding the reviewer that writing mode changes logical dimensions.

title: Change Text Case Without Rewriting the Content
description: Inspect text-transform with language-aware casing and realistic labels. Distinguish uppercase styling from editorial title case, stored data and accessible names.
keyword: css text transform uppercase capitalize language
body:
Text-transform changes the rendered case treatment of text. It does not provide an editorial title-case algorithm or define the canonical value stored by the application. Keep the content meaningful in its original form, then apply a scoped visual treatment where the design calls for it.

Start with a short label specimen

<p class="eyebrow">Design review</p>
<p class="turkish-sample" lang="tr">istanbul</p>
.eyebrow {
  text-transform: uppercase;
  letter-spacing: .05em;
}
.turkish-sample { text-transform: uppercase; }

The language-marked sample illustrates why casing cannot always be treated as an English-only mapping. Review it in the browsers and fonts you support. Use the label as a specimen; do not change the page language merely to force one letter shape.

Reference: MDN text-transform and language-specific casing.

Separate capitalization from writing rules

Capitalize is not the same as an editor deciding which small words remain lowercase in a heading. It also does not reliably repair incorrectly cased source content. If a product needs title case as stored content, implement and review that editorial rule explicitly rather than relying on a paint-time CSS transformation.

Long passages in uppercase can become harder to scan. Check the real label length, punctuation and font weight instead of choosing tracking from a short mockup. Keep identifiers, code and case-sensitive values visually faithful when changing their presentation could confuse copying or comparison.

Test the content outside its styled view

  • Disable the case rule and read the original text.
  • Copy and paste the label in target browsers.
  • Inspect the control’s accessible name when the text labels an action.
  • Review translations, abbreviations and mixed-script phrases.

Copying and accessibility exposure need to be checked in the supported environment; do not assume a visual change rewrites every representation of the string. Keep server comparisons and stored identifiers independent of CSS. If the requirement is true small-cap glyphs rather than capital letters, use the small-caps feature comparison. For spacing after a deliberate uppercase treatment, review letter spacing with the actual font.
coverAlt: The source text Design review is styled as DESIGN REVIEW, with separate checks for language, copying and accessible naming.

title: Match Native Controls to a Theme with color-scheme
description: Use color-scheme to declare supported native UI appearances. Keep custom tokens, selected theme and browser-managed controls consistent across light and dark.
keyword: css color scheme native inputs dark mode
body:
Color-scheme tells the browser which color schemes an element can support. It can influence browser-managed controls and scrollbars, but it does not recolor every custom component. A page with dark backgrounds and bright native inputs often needs this declaration aligned with its actual theme.

Declare the scheme the selected theme supports

:root {
  color-scheme: light;
  --page: #f7f9f7;
  --text: #17251d;
}
:root[data-theme="dark"] {
  color-scheme: dark;
  --page: #142019;
  --text: #edf5ef;
}
body { background: var(--page); color: var(--text); }

This example assumes application code deliberately sets the theme attribute. It does not implement a theme picker or persistence. Compare a native text input, select and date field in both states, alongside a custom card using the same page tokens.

Reference: MDN color-scheme.

Keep preference detection separate from support

Prefers-color-scheme detects the user’s preference; color-scheme declares the schemes the element supports. Declaring light dark allows browser selection among supported schemes. It should not be used as a claim that a fixed light-only custom interface has already been designed for dark mode.

A deliberately light embedded section on a dark page may need its own light color scheme and matching custom foreground and background colors. Test that section’s descendants instead of changing the entire document to repair one field. Native styling still varies by browser and operating system.

Review the full control inventory

  • Check editable, disabled, focused and invalid fields.
  • Open native pickers and menus where supported.
  • Inspect custom icons and placeholder text against their actual surfaces.
  • Test user preference changes and an explicit application override.

Accent-color controls certain native control accents and is not interchangeable with color-scheme. Forced-colors mode is another separate review. Use the semantic theme-token guide for authored components and native accent styling for checkboxes and related controls. The resulting theme should be judged from the rendered task, not merely from the presence of a dark-mode declaration.
coverAlt: Light and dark panels each pair a custom surface with a native field, showing that supported color scheme and authored theme colors should agree.

title: Measure the Clickable Target, Not Just the Icon
description: Review pointer target dimensions and spacing using WCAG 2.2 guidance. Inspect the real hit area, neighboring controls and exceptions in the interface context.
keyword: wcag target size minimum 24 css pixels
body:
A small icon can sit inside a comfortably sized button, and a large visual decoration can still have a tiny click target. Measure the element that actually receives the pointer action. Start with a compact toolbar where neighboring controls are easy to activate accidentally.

Separate the drawing from the hit area

.icon-action {
  display: inline-flex;
  align-items: center;
  justify-content: center;
  min-inline-size: 2.25rem;
  min-block-size: 2.25rem;
  padding: .5rem;
}
.icon-action svg { width: 1rem; height: 1rem; }

This specimen makes room around a small icon; the values are a design starting point. Use a native button with an accessible name, and check the computed size rather than assuming a rem value always equals a fixed number of CSS pixels. Test whether the padded area really activates the control.

Apply the criterion in context

WCAG 2.2 success criterion 2.5.8, at Level AA, sets a 24 by 24 CSS pixel target-size requirement with exceptions. These include specified spacing conditions, an equivalent conforming control, inline targets, unmodified user-agent controls and essential presentation. Read the exact exception before recording a pass.

For the spacing exception, the criterion uses a 24 CSS pixel diameter circle centered on each undersized target’s bounding box. Those circles must not intersect another target or the circle for another undersized target. It is not a blanket rule that every small icon merely needs a particular gap.

Reference: W3C understanding of target size minimum.

Record a reproducible measurement

  • Identify the hit-area element in DevTools.
  • Measure its bounding box in CSS pixels.
  • Inspect nearby targets and any overlap.
  • Record the exception relied on, if one applies.
  • Test the toolbar on a real touch device as well as with a mouse.

A minimum-size review is one check, not a complete accessibility verdict or a promise of comfortable use for every person. Larger practical targets may suit the task. Keep keyboard focus and control states in the same review so improving pointer activation does not hide the focused action or introduce overlapping buttons.
coverAlt: A small arrow icon sits within a larger button hit area, with dimension markers referring to the target boundary rather than the visible icon.

title: Choose tabindex Zero or Minus One for the Intended Focus Path
description: Distinguish sequential keyboard focus from programmatic focus. Use native controls first and avoid positive tabindex values that create a separate ordering system.
body:
Tabindex zero generally adds an element to sequential keyboard navigation in document order. A negative value lets a focusable target receive programmatic focus without becoming an ordinary Tab stop. Choose based on the interaction, rather than adding tabindex to every visible wrapper.

Give a programmatic destination a narrow purpose

<h2 id="review-summary" tabindex="-1">Review summary</h2>
<button type="button" id="show-summary">Go to review summary</button>
document.querySelector('#show-summary').addEventListener('click', () => {
  document.querySelector('#review-summary').focus();
});

The heading can receive focus when the user activates the dedicated action. It does not become an extra stop during ordinary Tab navigation. Verify the resulting focus indicator and viewport position in the complete page, not only by reading the attribute.

Reference: MDN tabindex.

Preserve native interaction semantics

A button or link already has keyboard behavior appropriate to its element. Adding tabindex to a generic div does not supply button activation, an accessible role or disabled behavior. Use the native element unless the application has a specific reason and a complete custom interaction implementation.

Positive tabindex values introduce priority ordering before ordinary zero and native focus stops. This can diverge from reading order as content changes. Fix document structure instead of assigning increasing numbers to reproduce a visual layout. A negative tabindex is also not a way to disable an action or hide it from assistive technology.

Walk both paths

  • Tab forward and backward through the component.
  • Activate the action that moves focus programmatically.
  • Confirm the active element and visible focus treatment.
  • Repeat after conditional content is inserted or removed.

Keep focus movement connected to an understandable user task. A noninteractive heading does not need focusability simply because it is visually prominent. For a route change, modal or composite widget, follow the interaction pattern’s complete focus requirements rather than applying this small example universally.

Use the visual-order review when the tab sequence feels wrong. Use focus without automatic scrolling only when the destination’s visibility is already handled deliberately.
coverAlt: Two focus paths distinguish a tabindex zero element in sequential Tab order from a tabindex minus one destination reached through an explicit focus action.

title: Move Keyboard Focus Without an Unexpected Scroll Jump
description: Use focus with preventScroll when the destination is already visible. Verify activeElement, focus visibility and nested scrolling instead of suppressing movement blindly.
body:
Calling focus can scroll the page to expose the focused element. The preventScroll option suppresses that automatic movement. It is useful when another part of the interaction has already positioned the destination, but it can hide focus offscreen if used without checking visibility.

Use the option for a visible destination

const summary = document.querySelector('#review-summary');
// The interaction has already made this focusable target visible.
summary.focus({ preventScroll: true });
console.log(document.activeElement === summary);

The target must be focusable, for example a heading with tabindex="-1" or a native control. This code does not make a hidden or inert destination usable. Check the target’s state before assuming a successful method call means the user can see and interact with it.

Reference: MDN focus options.

Inspect focus and scrolling as separate outcomes

Record document.activeElement before and after the operation. Also inspect scrollTop on the page and any surrounding scroll container. A nested panel may move independently of the outer document; comparing only the page’s scroll position can miss the jump that the user experienced.

PreventScroll does not promise a visible focus indicator. Retain a suitable focus style and test the actual keyboard sequence. It also does not neutralize a later layout change, sticky overlay or script that scrolls the page again. Diagnose the timing instead of applying the option to every focus call.

Give offscreen targets an explicit visibility plan

  • Test with the destination fully visible, partially visible and offscreen.
  • Check a sticky header and a nested scrolling panel.
  • Verify focus after content expands or loads asynchronously.
  • Test at enlarged text sizes where the same destination can move.

If the destination is offscreen, reveal it deliberately before suppressing automatic scrolling, or allow normal focus scrolling when that better serves the task. Smooth motion is not always appropriate; respect the motion policy for the interface. The scroll alignment guide explains a separate visibility operation.

Keep this behavior tied to a specific interaction such as an explicit summary jump. Do not move focus merely because background data refreshed. A stable viewport is helpful only when keyboard users still understand where focus went and can continue their task.
coverAlt: A visible summary receives focus inside an unchanged viewport, illustrating preventScroll with a reminder to keep the focused target visible.

title: Reveal an Element with Deliberate Scroll Alignment
description: Choose start, center or nearest alignment for scrollIntoView. Review nested scroll containers, sticky headers and motion without confusing scrolling with focus.
keyword: scrollintoview block nearest start sticky header
body:
ScrollIntoView asks ancestor containers to reveal an element. Its alignment options control where that element should land; they do not move keyboard focus by themselves. Use a visible task, such as revealing a selected row, to decide whether minimal movement or a consistent landing position is appropriate.

Start with minimal alignment movement

const row = document.querySelector('[data-selected-row]');
row.scrollIntoView({
  behavior: 'instant',
  block: 'nearest',
  inline: 'nearest'
});

This fixture avoids animated scrolling and asks for the nearest alignment along both axes. Test it when the row is above, below and already inside the visible region. Compare block start or center if the task requires a specific reading position rather than the smallest useful adjustment.

Reference: MDN scrollIntoView options.

Inspect every scrolling ancestor

A row inside a scrolling panel can affect both that panel and the page. Record which containers move and verify that a surrounding heading or toolbar does not disappear unexpectedly. Do not assume the method only changes the nearest scroll container without explicitly checking the supported API options and behavior.

A sticky header can cover the landing position. Apply an appropriate scroll margin to the target and test the actual header height at the relevant breakpoint. A fixed offset copied from desktop may be wrong when navigation wraps on a smaller screen.

.review-row { scroll-margin-block-start: 5rem; }

Keep motion and focus intentional

  • Reveal a target near each edge of the scroll area.
  • Test a target taller than the available viewport.
  • Review nested scrolling and enlarged text.
  • Confirm keyboard focus remains where the task expects it.

If you choose smooth behavior, provide a reduced-motion path and avoid repeated animation as state updates. If the user also needs focus moved, make that a separate decision with a focusable destination; scrolling alone is not an accessible focus-management strategy.

Use the scroll-margin guide to handle landing offsets and the focus guide to coordinate an already-visible destination. Record the reason for the alignment so a later animation change does not obscure the original task.
coverAlt: A scroll panel shows a selected row near its lower boundary and an arrow indicating the minimal movement used to reveal the row.

title: Observe Component Size Changes with ResizeObserver
description: Measure a component when its own layout changes, not only when the window resizes. Choose a box, clean up observers and avoid resize feedback loops.
body:
ResizeObserver reports element-size changes even when the browser window stays the same size. That makes it useful for a preview panel affected by a sidebar or content update. Choose the box you need to observe before comparing the result with another measurement API.

Observe the relevant component box

const panel = document.querySelector('.preview-panel');
const observer = new ResizeObserver(entries => {
  for (const entry of entries) {
    const size = entry.borderBoxSize[0];
    console.log({
      inlineSize: size.inlineSize,
      blockSize: size.blockSize
    });
  }
});
observer.observe(panel, { box: 'border-box' });
// When this component is removed:
// observer.disconnect();

This example assumes a modern implementation with borderBoxSize support and a simple unfragmented box. Add a deliberate compatibility path if your support policy needs one. The logical inline and block dimensions follow writing mode; they are not universally interchangeable with physical width and height.

Reference: MDN ResizeObserver.

Avoid measuring one box and fixing another

A content-box measurement excludes padding and borders. A border-box observation includes them. A transformed visual rectangle from getBoundingClientRect answers another question again. Write down which size drives the behavior so an apparent disagreement does not lead to extra compensating pixels.

If the observer callback changes the observed element’s size, it can cause further observations and a feedback loop. Compare the intended value before writing it, separate the measurement from unrelated layout work, and investigate loop warnings rather than hiding them. Deferring work alone does not make a logically circular update correct.

Test component changes directly

  • Open and close a neighboring sidebar without resizing the window.
  • Change content length and inspect wrapping.
  • Add padding and compare the chosen box measurements.
  • Remove the component and confirm observer cleanup.

Use CSS container queries when the goal is purely responsive styling of a component. Reach for observation when JavaScript actually needs the dimensions, such as coordinating a rendering surface. The container-query guide provides the CSS alternative, while the measurement comparison helps separate layout dimensions from transformed visual bounds.
coverAlt: A sidebar changes a preview panel’s available width while the outer viewport stays fixed, illustrating why component observation differs from window resize handling.

title: Choose the Reference Box for an SVG Transform
description: Compare fill-box and view-box when an SVG shape rotates around the wrong center. Inspect transparent coordinate space, stroke width and transform origin together.
keyword: svg transform box fill box view box origin
body:
An SVG shape can rotate around the center of its artwork or around a larger SVG coordinate region. Transform-box selects the reference box used by transform calculations. If the pivot looks far from the shape, inspect that box before changing the origin percentages repeatedly.

Use an off-center shape to expose the difference

<svg viewBox="0 0 200 100" width="400" height="200"
     aria-hidden="true">
  <rect class="sample-shape" x="20" y="30" width="40" height="40"
        fill="#0f7fff" />
</svg>
.sample-shape {
  transform-box: fill-box;
  transform-origin: center;
  transform: rotate(20deg);
}

The rectangle is intentionally away from the center of the viewBox. With fill-box, its object bounding box supplies the reference. Switch to view-box and compare the pivot against the SVG viewport’s coordinate region. Use the same origin and angle so the reference box is the only changed variable.

Reference: MDN transform-box.

Inspect strokes and unused coordinate space

Fill-box and stroke-box account for different bounds: a thick stroke can extend beyond the fill geometry. A viewBox can also include generous empty space around a small mark. Both can make a percentage origin look unexpected if you judged the center from visible pixels alone.

Confirm whether the transform is applied to an inner SVG graphic or an outer HTML wrapper. The relevant box can differ. Keep layout size and visual transformation separate: rotating a shape does not automatically reserve additional space for the resulting rotated bounds.

Verify a useful range of states

  • Compare zero rotation with positive and negative angles.
  • Add a thick stroke and inspect whether the chosen reference still fits.
  • Resize the outer SVG while keeping the viewBox fixed.
  • Check clipping near the viewport boundary.

This is a static diagnostic example, not an animation prescription. If the component later animates, review its motion and focus behavior independently. Use the viewBox scaling guide for the outer coordinate mapping and the transform-origin guide for the pivot itself. Record the box and origin together in the handoff so the effect survives an asset replacement.
coverAlt: A small SVG rectangle sits away from the viewBox center, with separate markers for the artwork center and the coordinate region center.

title: Add a Gradient Border with an Explicit Fallback
description: Use border-image with a gradient source and slice value. Keep a normal border fallback and check rounded corners, dimensions and forced-colors behavior.
keyword: css border image gradient slice border radius
body:
Border-image can paint a gradient or image around an element’s border region. It requires a deliberate border setup and slicing behavior; a background gradient alone does not become a border. Start with a simple square-corner panel before adding more decorative constraints.

Define the normal border first

.gradient-panel {
  border: 4px solid #286b4a;
  border-image-source: linear-gradient(120deg, #2878dd, #53a97c);
  border-image-slice: 1;
  padding: 1.25rem;
}

The ordinary solid border provides a fallback and establishes thickness. The gradient is the image source, and the slice value supplies the slicing needed for this simple gradient treatment. Change the panel’s width and height to confirm the border remains intentional at each shape.

Reference: MDN border-image.

Inspect the limitations before copying the effect

Border-radius does not round the border image in the same way it rounds an ordinary border. If the design needs a rounded gradient ring, choose a technique designed for that result, such as layered backgrounds with a transparent border, and test its clipping separately. Do not assume increasing the radius will repair a square image border.

The border-image shorthand can reset several longhands at once. Inspect source, slice, width, outset and repeat when a later rule changes the appearance. Outset can paint beyond the border box, which needs review near neighboring content and clipping ancestors.

Keep decoration separate from state meaning

  • Disable the image source and inspect the fallback.
  • Test a short panel and one with long text.
  • Review the border against every adjacent theme surface.
  • Check forced-colors mode and keyboard focus if the panel contains controls.

A decorative border should not become the only indication that an item is selected or invalid. Add meaningful text or control state as appropriate, and retain a distinct focus treatment. This example’s palette is illustrative; inspect the real rendered colors instead of treating it as a contrast-certified component.

Use the gradient inspection guide for the color transition and the forced-colors review for alternate rendering. A documented fallback makes the component easier to maintain than a visually impressive ring whose failure state is invisible.
coverAlt: A panel with a blue-to-green decorative border is paired with a plain solid-border fallback, showing that the component remains visible without the image source.

title: Put Vendor CSS in a Layer Before Writing Overrides
description: Control vendor styles with explicit cascade layers. Check unlayered rules and reversed important precedence before trying to win with stronger selectors.
keyword: css cascade layer vendor overrides important
body:
Cascade layers let you establish precedence between groups of author styles before comparing selector specificity within those groups. They are useful when vendor CSS is deliberately placed in an earlier layer and application overrides live later. The vendor stylesheet must actually belong to a layer for that plan to work.

Establish the order before the rules

@layer vendor, components, overrides;
@import url("/styles/vendor.css") layer(vendor);

@layer overrides {
  .sample-button { background-color: #286b4a; }
}

Replace the illustrative URL with the stylesheet your project uses. Keep import placement valid: a layer-order statement can precede the import, but ordinary style rules should not. Inspect the delivered CSS if a bundler rewrites imports; the source file’s appearance does not prove the browser received the same layer structure.

Reference: MDN import layers.

Account for unlayered and important rules

Within the author origin, normal unlayered declarations outrank normal declarations in named layers. Moving only your override into a layer while leaving vendor rules unlayered can therefore weaken the override. Check the layer shown for the actual winning declaration.

Important declarations reverse layer precedence: earlier layers outrank later ones, and layered important declarations outrank unlayered important declarations. Do not extend the normal “later wins” rule to an important conflict. Treat an important vendor rule as a separate issue rather than escalating every application selector.

Reference: MDN layer precedence.

Test the contract with a small fixture

  • Compare a vendor rule and an override targeting the same property.
  • Add an unlayered normal rule and observe the change.
  • Test an important conflict separately.
  • Verify hover, focus and disabled variants still have their intended appearance.

Avoid reorganizing the entire stylesheet to fix one unexplained declaration. First use the cascade debugging workflow to identify origin, importance, layer and specificity. Document the layer order once so future components follow the same override contract instead of creating new local exceptions.
coverAlt: Three author layers are ordered vendor, components and overrides; opposing arrows distinguish normal precedence from reversed important precedence.

title: Size the Extra Rows Created by CSS Grid
description: Use grid-auto-rows for tracks created beyond the explicit grid. Test added items, long content and placement rules without forcing every row to a fixed height.
keyword: css grid auto rows implicit tracks
body:
A grid can create additional rows when content exceeds the explicitly defined tracks. Grid-auto-rows controls the sizing of those implicit rows. If the first row looks right but later rows behave differently, inspect which tracks came from the template and which were created automatically.

Add more items than the template describes

.sample-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr));
  grid-template-rows: 6rem;
  grid-auto-rows: minmax(6rem, auto);
  gap: 1rem;
}

Use six cards in this original fixture. The template explicitly sizes the first row; the remaining rows use the automatic track rule. A longer card in a later row can make that row grow. The fixed first row is intentional here to expose the distinction, not a recommendation for unknown production content.

Reference: MDN implicit row sizing.

Inspect placement before changing height

An item placed beyond the explicit grid can create implicit tracks even when the number of items is small. Inspect grid-row, grid-column and named-area assignments on the item that seems to create a gap. A mistaken placement cannot always be repaired by shrinking auto rows.

Grid-auto-flow controls auto-placement, not track height. Dense packing can fill earlier holes, but it can also produce a visual sequence that differs from DOM order. Do not enable dense solely to make a dashboard look compact without checking reading and keyboard order.

Reference: MDN grid auto-placement.

Review growth and empty space

  • Add one item at a time and inspect the created tracks.
  • Put the longest content in an implicit row.
  • Remove any fixed container height during diagnosis.
  • Check spanning items and explicit placement declarations.

If all rows are content-driven, consider omitting the fixed template row and using a consistent automatic policy. If cards need alignment with a parent’s shared tracks, review subgrid instead. Record which rows are explicit, which can grow and whether a change in item count should create a new row.
coverAlt: A two-column grid contains one explicitly sized first row and two additional rows sized through grid-auto-rows.

title: Check Whether Stale CSS Comes from the Browser Cache
description: Compare cached and uncached loads in Chrome without clearing unrelated site data. Inspect actual response content and service-worker involvement before changing CSS.
keyword: chrome devtools stale css disable cache
body:
When a deployed CSS change seems absent, first confirm which stylesheet the page actually loaded. Disabling the browser cache is a useful diagnostic comparison, but it does not prove that the server, CDN or service worker is serving the version you expected.

Compare two controlled loads

  • Open Network and reload the affected page with ordinary caching.
  • Record the stylesheet URL, transfer indication and a recognizable declaration in its response.
  • Enable Disable cache while DevTools remains open and reload.
  • Compare the same resource and declaration again.

Keep the page route, account state and viewport unchanged. A new stylesheet filename or a different page build can explain the result independently of caching. Record a real difference in the response rather than assuming the design should have changed because a deployment command completed.

Reference: Chrome Network reference.

Identify another layer when the response stays old

An HTTP cache bypass does not clear all application storage or establish that a service worker is uninvolved. Inspect the Application panel’s service-worker state if the site uses one. Bypass for network provides a separate diagnostic comparison; restore it afterward so normal behavior is tested too.

Reference: Chrome service-worker diagnostics.

If the uncached response itself lacks the expected declaration, check the deployment artifact and resource URL. If the declaration is present but loses, the problem may be the cascade, an inactive media condition or a component rendering a different class. Those are different failures with different owners.

Capture evidence before clearing state

Route and page state:
Stylesheet URL:
Expected declaration:
Observed response declaration:
Cache enabled result:
Cache disabled result:
Service-worker involvement:

Avoid clearing all site data as the first experiment; it can change login and stored preferences, removing the original conditions. Use specimen data when sharing evidence. A useful bug report identifies the response that was served and the state that reproduced the mismatch, then separates that observation from the proposed cache or CSS repair.
coverAlt: A stylesheet diagnostic compares ordinary caching, a cache-disabled load and service-worker involvement as separate checks.

title: Trace the Request That Loaded an Unexpected Asset
description: Use Chrome’s Initiator information to find why an image, font or stylesheet loaded. Separate dependency evidence from assumptions about performance or ownership.
keyword: chrome network initiator asset request chain
body:
The Network Initiator information helps explain what triggered a resource request. Use it when an unexpected image, font or stylesheet appears in the request list, rather than deleting every reference with a similar filename. The trigger and the visible component using the asset may not be the same file.

Start from one exact request

  • Open Network before reproducing the page state.
  • Filter to the asset type and select the exact request URL.
  • Inspect the Initiator column and the request’s Initiator details.
  • Follow an available source link or dependency chain back toward its trigger.

A script-initiated request may provide a call stack, while parser-driven loading can point toward markup. Record what DevTools actually exposes; not every request has a convenient application-level stack. If navigation clears the evidence, enable Preserve log for that controlled reproduction.

Reference: Chrome request initiators and dependency details.

Distinguish the trigger from the diagnosis

A font request triggered by a stylesheet is not automatically unnecessary: the page may need a glyph or weight from that face. An image selected from srcset may be legitimate at the current device pixel ratio. Compare the requested resource with the rendered content before deciding it is redundant.

Likewise, an early request is not proof that a preload helped, and a late request is not proof that JavaScript is at fault. Keep initiator evidence separate from timing, transfer size and user-visible impact. Inspect redirects and the final URL if the name in the markup differs from the request you selected.

Write a small dependency record

Observed asset URL:
Trigger shown by DevTools:
Relevant route or component:
State that caused the request:
Visible use or confirmed lack of use:
Next experiment:

Repeat the action once with ordinary conditions after any temporary blocking or cache change. For responsive images, pair the record with currentSrc and natural dimensions. For font optimization, use the preload measurement workflow before changing priorities. The result should identify a testable dependency, not merely a suspicious filename.
coverAlt: An illustrative dependency chain connects a page to a stylesheet and then an image, with a reminder to verify the actual request initiator.

title: Pause the Script That Changes an Element’s Class
description: Use a DOM attribute breakpoint to catch an unexpected class or inline-style change. Reproduce the smallest interaction and inspect the call stack that caused it.
keyword: chrome dom breakpoint attribute class changes
body:
If a class or inline style keeps changing after you edit it, pause the code that performs the change. A DOM attribute-modification breakpoint on the affected element can reveal the writer instead of making you search every event handler in the application.

Choose the element and mutation type

  • Inspect the element in the Elements panel.
  • Open its context menu and choose Break on, then Attribute modifications.
  • Repeat the specific interaction that changes its class or style attribute.
  • When execution pauses, inspect the call stack and the relevant source location.

Set the breakpoint on the element whose attribute changes. A subtree-modification breakpoint answers a different question, such as a child being added or removed; it does not simply mean “pause on every possible change anywhere below here.” Choose Node removal when the target itself disappears.

Reference: Chrome DOM change breakpoints.

Reduce the noise before interpreting the pause

A framework can update several attributes during a render. Resume past unrelated changes until you catch the one tied to the visual defect, and record the before-and-after value. The first paused library function may only be infrastructure; use the stack to locate the application state or callback responsible.

A CSS rule becoming active without any DOM mutation will not necessarily trigger this breakpoint. Hover, a media condition or a stylesheet change can alter appearance while the class remains identical. Compare the element’s attributes and computed property to decide which debugging path fits the evidence.

Turn the pause into a reproducible report

Trigger: open the sample panel
Observed mutation: class changes from ... to ...
Paused source and call stack:
State value associated with the change:
Expected component state:

Use actual observations in place of this template. Remove or disable the breakpoint after the investigation so it does not interrupt later tests. If the markup is stable but the wrong declaration wins, return to the cascade workflow. If a state update is responsible, fix the state contract rather than repeatedly overriding the resulting inline style.
coverAlt: An element changes from class closed to class open, and an attribute breakpoint pauses the script so its call stack can be inspected.

title: Find a Design Token Across Loaded Resources in Chrome
description: Search loaded resources for a custom property or class, then verify the winning declaration. Distinguish browser evidence from a complete repository search.
keyword: chrome devtools search all loaded resources css variable
body:
Chrome’s Search panel can locate a custom-property name or class across loaded resources. It is useful when you can inspect the deployed page but do not yet know which stylesheet owns a token. A text match is a lead, not proof that the declaration controls the selected element.

Search for an exact, distinctive string

  • Open DevTools, then More tools and Search.
  • Enter the full custom-property name, such as --surface-card.
  • Start with a literal search; enable regular expressions only when needed.
  • Open a result to inspect its surrounding source.

Keep punctuation in the query when it helps distinguish a declaration from ordinary copy. Case sensitivity matters for custom-property names. Searching only for a common hex value can return unrelated borders, backgrounds and examples that happen to share the same color.

Reference: Chrome Search panel.

Connect the match to the rendered element

Return to Elements and inspect the property that consumes the token. Trace its variable chain and the scope supplying each value. A token definition in an unloaded theme or inactive condition may be present in source without affecting the current component.

The Search panel searches loaded resources, not every file in the repository or every route that could load later. Network headers and responses have a separate Network search workflow. Generated bundles and source maps can also change which filenames and source text you see; record the deployed file when source mapping is unavailable.

Capture ownership rather than a list of matches

Token name: --surface-card
Consuming component and property:
Winning definition and scope:
Loaded source URL:
Theme or media condition:
Repository owner, if confirmed:
