Navigate through the relevant theme or lazy-loaded state and repeat only when it adds missing evidence. Do not call a token unused merely because the initial page search found no match. Use variable fallback debugging for invalid values, and preserve observations in a design brief with clear source and scope information. This keeps a copied color from becoming an undocumented global rule.
coverAlt: A search for the surface-card custom property produces source matches, followed by a separate check of the winning definition on the inspected component.

title: Start a CSS Animation Partway Through Its Timeline
description: Use a negative animation delay to inspect an offset phase. Distinguish elapsed progress from faster playback and check iteration, fill and reduced-motion behavior.
keyword: css negative animation delay start halfway
body:
A negative animation delay starts the animation as though some of its active time has already elapsed. It does not increase playback speed. Use a small controlled specimen to inspect a phase offset before applying the technique to several decorative elements.

Freeze a known point in the timeline

@keyframes move-sample {
  from { transform: translateX(0); }
  to { transform: translateX(100px); }
}
.sample {
  animation: move-sample 4s linear infinite;
  animation-delay: -1s;
  animation-play-state: paused;
}

For this linear, normal-direction example, the initial frozen state is one second into a four-second iteration, or a 25px translation. Remove the paused state in a local fixture to observe the same four-second pace continuing from that offset. Keep the animation decorative and provide a reduced-motion alternative before shipping it.

Reference: MDN negative animation delay.

Check more than the first iteration

Iteration count and direction affect what an offset means. A negative delay that skips beyond a finite animation’s active duration can put it into its after phase, where fill behavior matters. An alternating direction also changes the mapping between elapsed time and the visible keyframe value.

When several animations are listed, inspect the corresponding delay and duration entries. Copying one negative value into a list without matching the intended animation can stagger the wrong effect. A later animation shorthand can also reset a delay you set earlier.

Review the actual motion contract

  • Compare zero, positive and negative delay with the same duration.
  • Inspect the initial state and the transition into the next iteration.
  • Test finite playback and the chosen fill mode.
  • Check a paused state and the reduced-motion path.

Use the fill-mode guide for before and after states and DevTools timing inspection for the running sequence. Record duration and phase offset separately in the handoff; “starts later” and “starts further through” are different requirements.
coverAlt: A four-second animation timeline starts at a one-second elapsed offset, marking 25 percent progress without changing the four-second duration.

title: Use steps() for Discrete Animation States
description: Compare step timing with linear interpolation and inspect jump boundaries. Keep decorative steps separate from real progress and provide a static motion alternative.
keyword: css steps animation jump end start
body:
The steps() timing function divides progress into discrete jumps instead of continuously interpolating it. This can suit a sprite or a deliberately stepped decorative indicator. It should not be used to fabricate the apparent completion of a real task.

Make the jump timing visible

@keyframes stepped-fade {
  from { opacity: 0; }
  to { opacity: 1; }
}
.sample {
  animation: stepped-fade 4s steps(4, end) both;
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .sample { animation: none; opacity: 1; }
}

Use a nonessential colored square for the fixture. With end, also named jump-end, the first change waits until the end of the first interval. With start or jump-start, an initial jump occurs at the beginning. Compare the first moment as well as the end; a single middle screenshot can conceal the difference.

Reference: MDN steps timing function.

Count intervals and endpoint holds deliberately

Jump-none and jump-both change endpoint behavior rather than merely renaming start and end. Jump-none requires more than one step. Choose the form from the desired timing sequence, then inspect it at the boundaries instead of treating the numeric argument as a universal count of displayed frames.

For a sprite, the background-position distance and frame width must agree with the timing. An off-by-one distance can briefly reveal an empty region or part of another frame even when the timing function is valid. Keep the artwork geometry and timing calculation in the same fixture.

Test the behavior the user will receive

  • Inspect immediately before and after a jump.
  • Check iteration restart if the animation repeats.
  • Review pausing and any negative delay separately.
  • Confirm the static alternative communicates all necessary information.

Use a real value and semantic progress control for task completion. Keep this example’s steps confined to visual timing. If a discontinuity was unintended, compare the easing with linear in the animation inspector before changing keyframes. A clear handoff describes when each state appears, including endpoint holds, not only the total duration.
coverAlt: A staircase timing diagram shows four discrete jumps across a timeline instead of continuous interpolation.

title: Keep an SVG Stroke from Thickening When the Shape Scales
description: Use non-scaling-stroke for SVG line work that needs a stable stroke treatment. Compare scaled geometry, clipping and small-size legibility before applying it broadly.
keyword: svg vector effect non scaling stroke
body:
Vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke" keeps SVG stroke width from following the ordinary scaling of the geometry. It can help line-based diagrams stay consistent when their viewBox is displayed at different sizes. It does not make every part of the graphic or every kind of zoom invariant.

Compare two display sizes of the same path

<svg viewBox="0 0 100 60" width="300" height="180"
     aria-hidden="true">
  <path d="M10 45L35 15L60 40L90 10"
        fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"
        vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke" />
</svg>

Render the same fixture at 300px and 600px widths with proportional heights. Then remove vector-effect and compare. The geometry still grows in both cases, while the stroke treatment differs. Use a decorative specimen here; meaningful charts or diagrams still need appropriate accessible content and explanation.

Reference: MDN SVG vector effects.

Inspect the actual edge cases

A thin stable stroke can become visually insignificant beside a very large shape, while a large stable stroke can crowd small details at a tiny size. Review actual usage sizes rather than judging the property from one enlarged preview. Browser zoom and device pixel density still influence the final display.

Check the viewBox boundary, line caps and joins. Stroke can extend beyond the underlying path and be clipped at the viewport edge. A property intended to stabilize line weight does not automatically add safe coordinate space around the drawing.

Keep the asset contract explicit

  • Test the smallest and largest intended render sizes.
  • Compare thin diagonals and tight corners.
  • Review the graphic on light and dark surfaces.
  • Check CSS rules that override presentation attributes.

Vector-effect can also be set through CSS, so inspect the computed result when the attribute appears ineffective. Use the viewBox guide for coordinate scaling and transform-box inspection for an unexpected pivot. Record whether stroke weight should scale with the artwork; neither choice is correct for every icon or illustration.
coverAlt: Two differently sized line drawings use the same stroke width, illustrating non-scaling-stroke while their geometry grows.

title: Fit an SVG ViewBox with meet, slice or none
description: Compare SVG aspect-ratio alignment when the viewport shape differs from the viewBox. Check empty space, cropping and distortion as separate design decisions.
body:
PreserveAspectRatio controls how an SVG viewBox fits a viewport with a different shape. Meet shows the whole viewBox while preserving proportions; slice fills the viewport and can crop it. None allows nonuniform scaling, which can distort circles and other geometry.

Use mismatched shapes to reveal the choice

<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="240" height="120"
     preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet" aria-hidden="true">
  <circle cx="50" cy="50" r="40" fill="#2878dd" />
</svg>

The square coordinate region is displayed in a wide viewport. Meet keeps the full circle and leaves side space. Compare xMidYMid slice with the same viewport, then none. Make the viewport boundary visible in the fixture so unused space and clipping are easy to distinguish.

Reference: MDN preserveAspectRatio.

Choose alignment as well as scaling

The x and y alignment keywords determine how remaining space or excess artwork is distributed. Centering is only one option. If a mark must stay attached to a particular edge, test the corresponding alignment with the actual drawing and both wide and tall viewport shapes.

The normal SVG scaling use of this attribute depends on a viewBox; an SVG image element has additional behavior described in the reference. Also distinguish the SVG’s internal mapping from CSS sizing of an outer img element. A surrounding object-fit rule and an internal SVG setting can answer different fitting questions.

Review geometry and content boundaries

  • Compare circles, squares and text for accidental stretching.
  • Check every viewport ratio used by the component.
  • Inspect clipping of strokes near the edge.
  • Test meaningful artwork rather than only a centered placeholder.

Do not select none simply to remove empty space if it changes the brand mark’s proportions. If a genuinely different composition is needed, prepare the appropriate asset instead of stretching one drawing into every slot. Use the viewBox sizing guide to establish the coordinate region first, then document the chosen alignment and cropping policy.
coverAlt: Two wide SVG viewports show a complete circle with meet and a larger cropped circle with slice, preserving the circle proportions in both.

title: Keep an Unavailable Action Discoverable with aria-disabled
description: Use aria-disabled when an unavailable action should remain in the focus path. Guard activation explicitly and explain the reason without relying on dimming alone.
keyword: aria disabled vs disabled focusable button
body:
Aria-disabled communicates an unavailable state without automatically removing a control from keyboard navigation or blocking its behavior. It can be useful when users need to discover an action and understand why it is unavailable. Use native disabled when its built-in behavior matches the requirement.

Keep the action and reason connected

<button type="button" id="export-review" aria-disabled="true"
        aria-describedby="export-reason">Export review</button>
<p id="export-reason">Add a review item before exporting.</p>
const button = document.querySelector('#export-review');
button.addEventListener('click', () => {
  if (button.getAttribute('aria-disabled') === 'true') return;
  // Run the actual authorized export workflow here.
});

The guard prevents this handler’s action while the state is true. Because this is a native button, keyboard activation can follow the same click path. Any separate shortcut or application command must enforce the same availability rule; the attribute itself is not enforcement.

Reference: MDN aria-disabled.

Style and scope the state deliberately

Aria-disabled does not supply the browser’s ordinary disabled styling. Add a visual treatment that remains legible, and retain a visible focus indicator. Pointer-events none is not a complete substitute because it does not cover keyboard or programmatic activation.

Avoid setting aria-disabled on a broad container merely to dim one action. Its semantics affect focusable descendants, which may include links that should remain usable. Keep the state on the intended control and update both the state and explanation when the prerequisite changes.

Test availability transitions

  • Tab to the unavailable action and read its explanation.
  • Try pointer and Space or Enter activation.
  • Satisfy the prerequisite and confirm the action becomes usable.
  • Remove the prerequisite and confirm all activation paths are guarded.

The frontend should reflect real product state, not replace server authorization. For a field that must be omitted from submission or prevented from editing, compare native disabled and readonly. For actions, document whether staying in the focus order is intentional so a later refactor does not silently change discoverability.
coverAlt: An unavailable Export review button retains a focus outline and a visible explanation to add a review item first.

title: Keep a Sortable Table’s Order and aria-sort in Sync
description: Put sort state on the active table header and sorting behavior on a native button. Reorder complete rows and verify the announced direction matches the data.
keyword: aria sort sortable table header button
body:
Aria-sort describes the current ordering of a table column or row; it does not perform sorting. Put the state on the relevant header cell, use a native button for the action and update the actual data order together with the attribute.

Start from a small correctly ordered table

<table id="samples">
  <caption>Example review samples</caption>
  <thead><tr><th scope="col" aria-sort="ascending">
    <button type="button">Name</button>
  </th><th scope="col">Owner</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><td>Alpha</td><td>Team A</td></tr>
    <tr><td>Zulu</td><td>Team B</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
const table = document.querySelector('#samples');
const header = table.querySelector('th[aria-sort]');
const body = table.tBodies[0];
const collator = new Intl.Collator('en', { numeric: true });
header.querySelector('button').addEventListener('click', () => {
  const descending = header.getAttribute('aria-sort') === 'ascending';
  const rows = [...body.rows].sort((a, b) =>
    collator.compare(a.cells[0].textContent, b.cells[0].textContent)
    * (descending ? -1 : 1));
  body.append(...rows);
  header.setAttribute('aria-sort', descending ? 'descending' : 'ascending');
});

This fixture sorts the complete rows, keeping each owner attached to the correct name. It is intentionally a small client-side table, not a pagination or server-query implementation.

Reference: MDN aria-sort.

Preserve state when the implementation grows

When another column becomes the sort key, remove aria-sort from the previously sorted header and set it on the new one. Use a direction indicator that is not color alone. Keep focus on the initiating button instead of replacing the entire header unnecessarily.

For remote data, represent the completed ordering truthfully. Do not announce that rows are sorted before the requested result is applied. Define how empty values, numbers and locale-sensitive names compare; a lexical comparison is not appropriate for every column.

Verify action and announcement together

  • Activate the header with keyboard and pointer.
  • Compare first and last rows after each direction change.
  • Check header associations and focus after updates.
  • Review the table with supported screen-reader combinations.

Reference: W3C sortable-table example and testing guidance.
coverAlt: A table header reports ascending sort order, with Alpha and Zulu rows kept together with their respective owners.

title: Build a Breadcrumb Trail That Explains Page Location
description: Use a labeled navigation region and ordered links for page ancestry. Mark the current page, keep separators decorative and let long breadcrumb labels wrap.
keyword: accessible breadcrumb nav aria current page
body:
A breadcrumb describes the current page’s place in a hierarchy, not the user’s recent browsing history. Use links to meaningful parent locations and a clearly identified current item. Keep the trail short enough to help orientation without replacing the page heading.

Represent ancestry with ordinary navigation

<nav aria-label="Breadcrumb">
  <ol class="breadcrumbs">
    <li><a href="/">Home</a></li>
    <li><span aria-hidden="true">/</span> <a href="/guides/">Guides</a></li>
    <li><span aria-hidden="true">/</span> <span aria-current="page">Color review</span></li>
  </ol>
</nav>

The routes and current title are an illustrative hierarchy. Replace them with actual parent destinations. A current-page link should carry aria-current page; for a non-link current item, the APG makes that attribute optional. The example includes it explicitly and hides the decorative separators from accessibility exposure.

Reference: W3C breadcrumb pattern.

Allow the trail to fit real content

.breadcrumbs {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: .5rem;
  padding: 0;
  list-style: none;
}
.breadcrumbs li { overflow-wrap: anywhere; }

Test a long current title and long parent labels, not only Home and Guides. Keep each separator with its following item so a wrap does not leave a misleading isolated slash. Do not hide necessary ancestor links merely to preserve one-line symmetry.

If the page has several navigation regions, distinguish their accessible labels. The breadcrumb remains a set of ordinary links; it does not need menu roles or custom arrow-key behavior. Preserve the native Tab and link activation experience.

Review the hierarchy and interaction

  • Open each parent link and confirm its destination.
  • Check that the current item matches the visible page heading.
  • Inspect the navigation name and current-page state.
  • Test wrapping, enlarged text and narrow screens.

Use the landmark guide for multiple navigation regions and current-page state guidance for repeated navigation sets. Record the actual hierarchy in the content model so breadcrumbs do not become manually maintained strings that drift from the site’s structure.
coverAlt: A breadcrumb shows Home, Guides and the current Color review page in hierarchical order above a page heading.

title: Investigate Scroll Jumps Before Disabling Anchoring
description: Use overflow-anchor as a targeted diagnostic for scroll adjustments. Separate browser anchoring from layout shifts and script-driven scrolling before choosing a fix.
keyword: css overflow anchor scroll jump none
body:
Browsers can adjust scroll position to keep the reader’s location stable when content changes above it. Overflow-anchor provides an opt-out from that scroll-anchoring behavior. Use it for a measured conflict, not as a global cure for every unexpected jump.

Reproduce one insertion above the reading point

.changing-banner {
  overflow-anchor: none;
}

Create a local fixture with a changing banner above several paragraphs. Scroll to a known paragraph, change the banner’s height and compare the result with and without the rule. The property excludes that region from anchoring selection; it does not reserve space or prevent the banner from changing layout.

Reference: MDN overflow-anchor.

Identify which mechanism moved the view

A script calling scrollIntoView, a focus operation, browser anchoring and a visible layout shift can produce superficially similar symptoms. Record the active element, scroll position and content change together. Disable one suspected behavior at a time rather than changing several overflow and height rules simultaneously.

Prefer stable space for predictable media and banners when that solves the underlying problem. If your application deliberately manages scrolling, such as a carefully implemented message view, document when it follows new content and when it preserves the reader’s position. An anchoring opt-out alone does not implement that policy.

Keep the opt-out narrow

  • Test a reader at the top, middle and bottom of the region.
  • Insert and remove content above the visible item.
  • Check keyboard focus and explicit navigation separately.
  • Review browsers in the project’s actual support policy.

Applying none broadly can remove helpful behavior elsewhere. A descendant cannot simply opt back into anchoring once an ancestor has opted the subtree out. Limit the rule to the region whose participation is causing the observed conflict and keep a record of that reproduction.

Use layout-shift diagnosis to find unstable geometry and scroll alignment inspection for explicit script movement. The repair should explain why the view moved and which behavior now owns scroll stability.
coverAlt: A scrolling region contains a changing banner above a reading paragraph, with anchoring and explicit scrolling identified as separate possible causes of movement.

title: Scale Pixel Art Without Treating Every Image as Pixelated
description: Use image-rendering for intentional pixel graphics and compare integer scaling. Keep photographs, logos and text screenshots on an appropriate rendering path.
keyword: css image rendering pixelated pixel art
body:
Image-rendering changes the scaling algorithm used to draw an image. Pixelated can suit deliberately low-resolution pixel art, but it does not recover detail missing from a photograph or screenshot. Choose the setting from the type of source artwork rather than using it as a general sharpness switch.

Compare a known pixel-art specimen

.pixel-sample {
  width: 128px;
  height: 128px;
  image-rendering: pixelated;
}

Use an original 32 by 32 pixel drawing for this fixture, then compare the 4x display with the same image using auto. The integer scale makes the intended pixel grid easy to inspect. Also try a noninteger display size to understand how the browser handles the final scaling step.

Reference: MDN image-rendering.

Diagnose soft ordinary images separately

If a UI screenshot is blurry, verify the selected resource, its density and the rendered box first. A low-resolution capture enlarged beyond its useful size may need a better source image, not a pixelated filter. Text within a screenshot can become particularly difficult to read when the wrong rendering treatment is applied.

For vector icons, inspect their paths, viewBox and stroke treatment at the intended size. This property is not a substitute for well-designed small-size geometry. Keep a class specific to the pixel-art component rather than applying the rule to all images on the site.

Review the actual output conditions

  • Compare auto and pixelated at integer and noninteger scales.
  • Check the source file dimensions and chosen responsive candidate.
  • Inspect device pixel ratios and browser zoom used by readers.
  • Review both a detailed area and the silhouette of the artwork.

Rendering results can vary by browser and display conditions, so document the tested specimen instead of promising identical physical pixels everywhere. Use the selected-source inspection guide for image evidence and responsive candidates when the page needs an appropriate higher-resolution asset. Reserve pixelated styling for artwork whose intended appearance is a visible pixel grid.
coverAlt: A simple original pixel-art shape is enlarged on an explicit square grid, distinguishing intentional pixel graphics from ordinary photographic detail.

title: Make a Single-Line Ellipsis Work Without Losing the Full Value
description: Combine text-overflow with an actual width constraint and overflow policy. Check flex minimum sizes and provide a reliable way to read the complete value.
keyword: css text overflow ellipsis not working single line
body:
Text-overflow ellipsis controls how clipped inline content is signaled; it does not create the overflow by itself. A working single-line treatment needs a constrained box, a no-wrap policy and hidden overflow. Diagnose those prerequisites before adding more ellipsis declarations.

Create a constrained text region

.file-row { display: flex; gap: .75rem; }
.file-row .name {
  min-width: 0;
  flex: 1 1 auto;
  overflow: hidden;
  white-space: nowrap;
  text-overflow: ellipsis;
}
.file-row .action { flex: 0 0 auto; }

Place the row inside a container with a meaningful available width and use a long filename. Min-width zero allows the text flex item to shrink instead of insisting on its automatic content minimum. The neighboring action remains a separate box rather than being clipped with the label.

Reference: MDN text-overflow.

Keep the complete value available

The visually shortened string is not always enough to distinguish two similar files. Provide a clear details view, copy action or other accessible way to obtain the complete value. A mouse-only hover tooltip or title attribute should not be the sole recovery path.

Check whether truncation is appropriate at all. For instructions, error messages and short primary actions, wrapping is often better. A filename list may use an ellipsis for density while a confirmation screen displays the full name. Treat those as different reading tasks rather than applying one global class.

Test ambiguity as well as geometry

  • Use two filenames that share a long prefix.
  • Check narrow layouts and enlarged text.
  • Keep focus indicators outside the clipped text box.
  • Verify the complete value can be read and copied with keyboard and touch input.

For several lines of editorial preview text, review multiline clamping instead. For content that must remain visible, use long-word wrapping. The useful acceptance check is not merely “an ellipsis appears”; it is that users can still identify and act on the correct item.
coverAlt: A constrained filename row shows an ellipsis next to a separate Details action, illustrating that the complete value needs a usable recovery path.

title: Calculate Background Position from the Remaining Space
description: Understand percentage background positioning with a worked width example. Recalculate after cover scaling and distinguish alignment from a fixed pixel offset.
body:
A percentage background position aligns a point on the image with the same percentage point in the positioning area. It is not simply that percentage of the container width measured from the left. The image’s rendered size is part of the calculation.

Work through a fixed-size example

.position-sample {
  width: 300px;
  height: 160px;
  background-image: url("/images/sample-mark.webp");
  background-size: 100px 100px;
  background-repeat: no-repeat;
  background-position: 25% 50%;
}

In a 300px-wide positioning area with a 100px-wide rendered background, the available horizontal difference is 200px. At 25%, the left offset is 50px: (300 − 100) × 0.25. Vertically, the 160px area and 100px image leave 60px, so 50% gives 30px.

Reference: MDN percentage background positioning.

Recalculate when the image grows

If the image becomes wider than the area, the difference becomes negative. With a 400px image in a 300px area, 25% produces a −25px offset. This explains why changing a percentage can appear to move a cover background in the opposite direction from an intuitive container-offset model.

Cover and contain first determine the rendered image size from its proportions and the positioning area. Use that resulting size in the reasoning. If image and area widths are equal, the horizontal difference is zero and changing the horizontal percentage has no visible effect.

Inspect the right box and syntax

  • Confirm the background positioning area selected by background-origin.
  • Temporarily use explicit background dimensions to isolate the math.
  • Compare 0%, 50% and 100% before choosing a focal position.
  • Review each image layer separately when values are listed.

Edge-offset syntax such as right 1rem expresses a different positioning instruction; do not silently interpret it as the two-percentage example above. Keep the calculation and intended focal content in the handoff. Use background fitting when the crop changes across viewport shapes, and origin and clipping when padding changes the area you meant to measure.
coverAlt: A 100-pixel background image sits 50 pixels from the left of a 300-pixel positioning area, illustrating a 25 percent position based on remaining space.

title: Choose a Font Display Policy from the Loading Experience
description: Compare swap, fallback and optional in a controlled font-loading review. Test readable fallback text and layout changes without promising exact timing across browsers.
keyword: font display swap fallback optional difference
body:
Font-display is an @font-face descriptor that controls how a font face is used while it becomes available. Choose it from the reading experience during loading, not only from the final branded screenshot. A useful comparison includes the fallback face and the layout change when a web font arrives.

Set the policy on the font face

@font-face {
  font-family: "Review Sans";
  src: url("/fonts/review-sans.woff2") format("woff2");
  font-style: normal;
  font-weight: 400;
  font-display: swap;
}
.article-copy { font-family: "Review Sans", system-ui, sans-serif; }

Use a real licensed file and correct descriptors in place of the specimen. Putting font-display on the article element does not configure the face. Keep the font, content and network conditions the same while comparing policies.

Reference: MDN font-display periods.

Compare the practical tradeoffs

Swap uses an extremely small block period and permits a later swap. Fallback uses an extremely small block period with a limited swap period. Optional has an extremely small block period and no swap period, so the web font may not replace the fallback during that view. Browser timing and decisions are not universal fixed deadlines.

The visual cost depends on the fallback’s metrics. A heading that gains a line or a button that grows after a swap can disturb the task even when the font file is relatively small. Measure the actual component, and do not claim that optional guarantees the font is never downloaded or that swap prevents every loading problem.

Review cold and repeat visits

  • Compare readable text before the custom face is ready.
  • Inspect wrapping and component dimensions after loading.
  • Repeat with a cached font under otherwise comparable conditions.
  • Test a failed request and a slow connection without hiding content indefinitely.

Use fallback-size review to investigate metric differences and measured font preloading only when early discovery is a real problem. Record the chosen policy, fallback and observed tradeoff so a later typography change does not silently invalidate the loading decision.
coverAlt: Three font-display policies are compared by their swap periods: swap allows a later replacement, fallback limits it and optional has no swap period.

title: Use a Description List for Named Metadata Values
description: Represent label-and-value metadata with dl, dt and dd before styling it as a grid. Preserve grouping, wrapping and reading order across narrow layouts.
keyword: html dl dt dd metadata description list
body:
A description list is useful for groups of names and corresponding values, such as file metadata or a short specification. Start with dl, dt and dd when that relationship describes the content. A table is more appropriate when readers need to compare values across rows and columns.

Keep each name with its value

<dl class="asset-meta">
  <div><dt>Format</dt><dd>SVG</dd></div>
  <div><dt>Dimensions</dt><dd>1200 by 630</dd></div>
  <div><dt>Color role</dt><dd>Decorative illustration</dd></div>
</dl>

The values are an illustrative metadata record. Each div groups a term and its description inside the list. Keep a consistent valid grouping structure rather than placing arbitrary headings or controls between unrelated terms and values.

Reference: MDN description lists.

Style the relationship without flattening it

.asset-meta > div {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: minmax(7rem, 1fr) minmax(0, 2fr);
  gap: .5rem 1rem;
  padding-block: .5rem;
}
.asset-meta dt { font-weight: 600; }
.asset-meta dd { margin: 0; overflow-wrap: anywhere; }
@media (max-width: 30rem) {
  .asset-meta > div { grid-template-columns: 1fr; }
}

The breakpoint and proportions are specimen values. Check the longest label and value in the real interface before adopting them. The source order remains name then value when the visual layout changes to one column, so the relationship does not depend on a desktop alignment trick.

Review content variation and semantics

  • Test an empty or unknown value with explicit product wording.
  • Include a long URL or filename and a translated label.
  • Check the reading sequence without CSS.
  • Review the structure in the supported accessibility environment.

Avoid using a description list merely to get convenient default indentation. Conversely, do not replace clear name/value relationships with disconnected spans just because the design resembles a card. If metadata becomes a comparison matrix, use real table header associations. Keep the content model clear first, then choose the layout behavior that presents it well.
coverAlt: A description list groups Format with SVG, Dimensions with 1200 by 630 and Color role with Decorative illustration.

title: Give an Illustration Context with figure and figcaption
description: Group an illustration with a meaningful caption while keeping image alternatives useful. Explain the takeaway in readable text without duplicating every sentence.
keyword: html figure figcaption vs alt text
body:
Figure groups self-contained content with an optional caption. Use figcaption to explain what the reader should take from an illustration, while the image’s alt text provides an appropriate alternative to the visual. A caption and an alternative can serve different purposes; one does not automatically replace the other.

Write the relationship before styling it

<figure class="comparison">
  <img src="/images/example-comparison.webp" width="1200" height="630"
       alt="Two cards show the same label wrapped into one line and two lines.">
  <figcaption>
    Example: allow the card to grow when its label wraps instead of fixing its height.
  </figcaption>
</figure>

Replace the specimen image with an actual matching illustration. The alternative describes the relevant visual comparison; the caption states its design implication. If the visual contains critical numbers or instructions, provide those in ordinary surrounding text too, so they remain easy to read, select and search.

Reference: MDN figure.

Reference: MDN figcaption.

Avoid duplicate or misleading descriptions

Do not repeat a long caption word for word in alt merely because both fields are available. Decide what information the image contributes and what the caption adds. A purely decorative image can have an empty alternative when the surrounding content already provides everything needed, but that decision must follow the image’s actual purpose.

Use one figcaption as the first or last child of its figure. A visually nearby paragraph outside the figure is not the same structural relationship. Multiple images can belong to one figure when they form a single comparison; unrelated screenshots often need separate context.

Check the result in the reading flow

  • Read the page with images unavailable.
  • Review the alternative and caption together for repetition.
  • Check the illustration and caption at narrow widths and enlarged text.
  • Confirm any credit or source attribution is accurate and linked where appropriate.

A caption should identify an example as an example, not imply a product test that never occurred. Use the UI-image alternative guide for visual descriptions and responsive image setup for loading and sizing. Keep the figure useful even when its polished visual treatment is not available.
coverAlt: An illustration compares a short and wrapped card label above a visible caption explaining that the card should grow with its content.

title: Read Resolved CSS Without Mistaking It for Inline Styles
description: Compare element.style with getComputedStyle, capture stable inspection values, and trace the authored rule separately when documenting a website component.
body:
An empty element.style.color does not mean the element has no color. The inline style object describes declarations attached directly to the element; getComputedStyle reads resolved values after the active cascade. Use the two answers for different inspection questions.

Capture a small inspection snapshot

const card = document.querySelector('.review-card');
if (card) {
  const resolved = getComputedStyle(card);
  const snapshot = {
    inlineColor: card.style.color,
    renderedColor: resolved.color,
    fontSize: resolved.fontSize,
    surfaceToken: resolved.getPropertyValue('--surface-card').trim()
  };
  console.table(snapshot);
}

Run this on a page containing the named component, or replace the selector. The plain object stores strings at inspection time. Keeping the returned style object itself is different: it is live and can reflect later changes. That distinction matters when comparing a closed menu with its open state.

Reference: MDN getComputedStyle.

Do not reverse-engineer a token from one result

A pixel font size does not reveal whether its author used rem, clamp or a custom property. A serialized color may differ from the original notation. Record the observed result, then use the Styles panel to locate its declaration and active conditions. A blank custom-property value can also mean you inspected the wrong scope.

For a changing animation, record when the snapshot was taken. Avoid repeatedly reading computed styles inside a large write-and-read loop; collect the evidence you actually need.

Build a reproducible comparison

Capture the same properties at two known viewport widths and component states. Include the selector, viewport, theme and screenshot with the values. If only one property changes, investigate its winning rule before copying the whole snapshot into production CSS.

Use the CSS inspection workflow to trace authorship and the cascade checklist when the expected declaration loses.
coverAlt: An inline color entry is empty while a resolved color entry is populated, with a reminder to snapshot inspection values.

title: Keep Scripted Behavior in Sync with a Media Query
description: Read a media query at startup, listen for match changes, and remove listeners when a component is destroyed so scripted behavior stays synchronized.
body:
Use matchMedia when JavaScript needs the answer to a CSS media query. Read matches immediately, then subscribe to change. A listener alone misses the initial state; a one-time read misses a later viewport or preference change.

Initialize before listening

const compact = matchMedia('(max-width: 48rem)');
const panel = document.querySelector('.review-panel');
function syncLayout() {
  if (panel) panel.dataset.layout = compact.matches ? 'compact' : 'wide';
}
syncLayout();
compact.addEventListener('change', syncLayout);
// When this component is permanently removed:
// compact.removeEventListener('change', syncLayout);

This example exposes the current match as a data attribute. It does not hide controls or move focus. The change event reports a change in the query result, rather than every pixel of resizing. Keep the function reference so teardown can remove the same listener.

Reference: MDN matchMedia.

Choose the correct source of truth

A viewport query is not a measurement of the panel itself. A narrow sidebar can hold a compact component even on a wide screen; use CSS container queries for that styling problem. Prefer CSS alone when the only effect is visual. Duplicate breakpoint logic in JavaScript and CSS creates a maintenance obligation.

For a scripted animation, the query can instead check prefers-reduced-motion. Apply the initial preference before starting motion and update the animation system when it changes.

Test crossing the boundary both ways

Open below the breakpoint, enlarge the viewport, then shrink it again. Confirm the initial state and both transitions. Mount and remove the component repeatedly to check for duplicate callbacks. Keep typed values, active selections and keyboard focus intact throughout the change.

See the reduced-motion review for motion decisions and container-query guide for component-driven styling.
coverAlt: A media-query workflow reads the initial match, listens for changes and removes the listener during teardown.

title: Set a Touch Gesture Boundary Without Disabling Page Zoom
description: Use touch-action deliberately for a custom drag surface, preserve browser panning and pinch zoom, and check cancellation on a real touch device.
keyword: css touch action pan y pinch zoom
body:
Touch-action declares which gestures the browser may handle on a surface. It does not implement dragging. For a custom horizontal interaction inside a vertically scrolling page, pan-y pinch-zoom can preserve vertical browsing and zoom while leaving horizontal gesture handling to your code.

Scope the policy to the interactive surface

.horizontal-drag-surface {
  touch-action: pan-y pinch-zoom;
}
/* Ordinary page content keeps the browser default. */

Apply this only to an element whose horizontal pointer interaction already works. A normal horizontal overflow gallery may need native horizontal panning instead, so copying this declaration there can remove the very gesture readers expect. Start by deciding whether the browser or the application owns each direction.

Reference: MDN touch-action.

Handle cancellation as part of the interaction

When the browser takes over an allowed gesture, pointer handling may be canceled. Clear temporary drag state on pointercancel as well as on completion. The effective gesture policy also depends on relevant ancestors, so inspect the chain if a local declaration appears ineffective. Changing touch-action after a gesture starts does not rewrite that gesture’s policy.

A page-wide none is a poor shortcut for a local drag bug: it can suppress useful panning and zoom. Keep equivalent buttons or other keyboard actions for any operation that otherwise requires dragging.

Review the actual touch experience

On a touch device, begin a drag horizontally, vertically and diagonally. Pinch zoom over the component, then scroll from content beside it. Confirm cancellation leaves no stuck visual state and that controls remain usable after zooming. A desktop mouse test cannot establish these outcomes.

Use overscroll-behavior for scroll chaining, which is a separate concern, and retain clear button states for alternate actions.
coverAlt: A horizontal custom drag surface preserves vertical browser panning and pinch zoom while providing alternate controls.

title: Review Scrollbar Width as a Usability Choice
description: Compare native and thin scrollbars in a bounded panel, retain keyboard access, and distinguish scrollbar appearance from the space reserved for it.
body:
Scrollbar-width chooses the platform’s default, thin or hidden scrollbar treatment. It is not an exact pixel-sizing tool. Before making a dense panel’s scrollbar thinner, check whether readers can discover, grab and operate it with their available input device.

Start with a scrollable named region

<section class="history" tabindex="0" aria-label="Review history">
  <h2>Review history</h2>
  <!-- Add enough real entries to exceed the panel height. -->
</section>
<style>
.history { max-block-size: 18rem; overflow: auto; scrollbar-width: auto; }
.history:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid currentColor; outline-offset: 3px; }
</style>

Toggle auto to thin in DevTools while keeping the content and panel size fixed. The region is explicitly keyboard focusable in this example; ensure the extra stop is useful in the actual page. The visible heading and accessible label should describe the same content.

Reference: MDN scrollbar-width.

Separate appearance from layout

The none value hides the scrollbar while content can still scroll. That can remove an important cue and a direct manipulation mechanism. Do not assume every reader has a wheel or trackpad. Operating-system settings and overlay scrollbars affect what appears, so a screenshot from one machine is incomplete evidence.

If the problem is content shifting when a scrollbar appears, investigate scrollbar-gutter instead. Making the scrollbar thin does not provide the same layout contract.

Check the end of the panel

Test a mouse drag on the thumb, keyboard scrolling after focus, and a touch gesture. Reach the last entry and then leave the region with Tab. Repeat with the operating system configured to show scrollbars persistently where possible. Retain the default width when the smaller target makes the panel harder to use.

Compare reserved scrollbar space and nested scroll chaining before changing unrelated overflow rules.
coverAlt: A scrolling panel compares a broad default scrollbar with a thinner scrollbar, emphasizing reach and keyboard operation.

title: Choose Gaps or Resizing for Repeated Background Tiles
description: Compare background-repeat space and round using a fixed-size tile, then inspect narrow widths where tile count and spacing change.
body:
Use background-repeat: space when complete tiles should keep their size and gaps can absorb the remaining room. Use round when tiles may resize to fit without gaps. This decision is different from stretching one large image with cover.

Compare one axis at a time

.tile-strip {
  inline-size: 310px;
  block-size: 60px;
  background-image: linear-gradient(#b7d5ff, #b7d5ff);
  background-size: 90px 40px;
  background-position: left center;
  background-repeat: space no-repeat;
}

The solid gradient is a self-contained tile specimen. With no padding or border, a 310px-wide strip fits three 90px tiles and distributes the remaining 40px into two 20px gaps. Switch only space to round to compare a gapless fit that adjusts tile width. Use a visibly asymmetric real motif next to reveal distortion.

Reference: MDN background-repeat.

Expect changes at tile-count boundaries

With space, the first and last tiles normally meet the edges when multiple tiles fit. If only one fits, background-position becomes relevant; if even one cannot fit, clipping can occur. Round adjusts the repetition to the available dimension. Do not infer the final pattern from the nominal background-size alone.

The first repeat keyword controls the horizontal direction and the second the vertical direction. Multiple background layers need corresponding comma-separated settings; inspect the layer you actually intend to change.

Resize around the difficult widths

Check widths just above and below the point where another tile fits. Look for abrupt spacing changes, clipped logos or squashed decorative marks. A decorative texture can tolerate adjustments that a recognizable brand mark cannot. Keep meaningful labels as content instead of embedding them in a repeated background.

Review background sizing and position calculations when the tiling is correct but its scale or placement is not.
coverAlt: Three fixed tiles use gaps under space, while round fills the strip with resized tiles and no gaps.

title: Why a 50 Percent Border Radius Makes an Ellipse
description: Compare percentage radii with large fixed radii on rectangular badges, and preserve a true circle by controlling the rendered box dimensions.
keyword: border radius 50 percent ellipse vs pill
body:
A 50% border radius produces a circle only when the rendered box is square. On a wide rectangle, the horizontal and vertical radii resolve against different dimensions, producing an ellipse. A capsule-shaped label usually needs a large length radius instead.

Compare identical rectangles

.badge {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  inline-size: 240px;
  block-size: 80px;
  display: grid;
  place-items: center;
  background: #dceaff;
}
.ellipse { border-radius: 50%; }
.pill { border-radius: 999px; }

Give two elements the badge class and one modifier each. At these dimensions, the percentage version has horizontal radii of 120px and vertical radii of 40px. The oversized equal length radii are reduced to fit, creating rounded ends with a straight middle. These are two different outlines, even though both are often called fully rounded.

Reference: MDN border-radius.

Check the border box before changing the token

A declared width and height do not necessarily describe the final outer box when padding, borders, minimum sizes or flex shrinking intervene. Measure the rendered element. For an avatar, establish equal dimensions or an appropriate aspect ratio, then decide how the image fits inside.

The slash syntax separates horizontal and vertical radii, such as 40px / 20px. It is useful for intentional elliptical corners, but adds complexity if the desired result is an ordinary pill.

Test content growth, not just the empty shape

Replace a short badge label with a longer one and enlarge text. Avoid a fixed height that clips the label merely to preserve the initial silhouette. A real button also needs enough usable interior space and a visible focus indicator. Put the chosen geometric rule in the handoff instead of the vague instruction “maximum rounding.”

Use the radius-system guide for reusable roles and the aspect-ratio guide when the box itself must stay square.
coverAlt: The same wide rectangle forms an ellipse at fifty percent radius and a capsule with large equal length radii.

title: Trace Alternating Animations One Iteration at a Time
description: Distinguish normal, reverse, alternate and alternate-reverse playback, then check iteration boundaries and the final state of a finite animation.
body:
Animation-direction controls how each iteration traverses the keyframes. Alternate runs forward first and backward second; alternate-reverse begins backward. It does not double the declared duration of an individual iteration, although a round trip takes two iterations.

Make the first two passes easy to observe

.sample-dot {
  animation: travel 2s linear 2 alternate;
}
@keyframes travel {
  from { transform: translateX(0); }
  to { transform: translateX(120px); }
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .sample-dot { animation: none; }
}

Use a small visible element in a track wide enough for the movement. This finite specimen runs from 0 to 120px during the first two seconds and returns during the next two. Linear timing isolates direction from easing. The example intentionally avoids an endless attention-catching loop.

Reference: MDN animation-direction.

Distinguish direction from the end-state policy

Normal starts each pass from the first keyframe. Reverse traverses the sequence backward each time. Alternating modes switch direction on successive passes. Reversing playback also reverses the timing-function progression, so an eased return may feel different from a separately authored forward movement.

When playback finishes, fill mode determines whether an animation value remains applied. The last relevant keyframe depends on direction and iteration count. Do not assume forwards always means the 100% keyframe.

Use a timeline table in the review

For this specimen, record 0px at the start, 120px at two seconds and 0px at four seconds. Change to three iterations and check the new ending deliberately. Pause near each boundary when investigating a visible jump; also inspect delays and the underlying transform. Review the reduced-motion state separately.

See fill-mode behavior for before-and-after values and the motion preference checklist for a useful static alternative.
coverAlt: A finite alternating animation moves forward from zero to 120 pixels in the first two seconds and returns during the next two.

title: Give Hover Entry and Exit Different Transition Delays
description: Place transition delays in the destination state, compare quick entry and exit, and avoid delaying the feedback that tells a user an action worked.
keyword: css transition delay hover in out
body:
A hover transition can wait before entering and return immediately on exit. Set the default delay to zero and the hovered state’s delay to the desired wait. The transition settings in the new state determine how that change begins.

Delay only a decorative surface change

.preview-card {
  background-color: #f4f6f8;
  transition-property: background-color;
  transition-duration: 180ms;
  transition-delay: 0ms;
}
.preview-card:hover {
  background-color: #e4f3eb;
  transition-delay: 250ms;
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .preview-card { transition: none; }
}

Entering hover uses the 250ms wait. Leaving restores the base delay, so the return can begin immediately. The example only changes decoration; it does not hide a panel or introduce a delayed action. Keep actual keyboard focus styling immediate and independent of the hover effect.

Reference: MDN transition-delay.

Inspect interruption instead of assuming a full cycle

A user may leave before the waiting period ends or reverse direction while the color is changing. Reversing transitions can use shortened timing, so do not calculate every interrupted sequence as a complete forward duration plus a complete backward duration.

For several properties, delay values follow the transition-property list. A short list repeats and an overlong list is truncated. Keep lists explicit when different effects need different schedules; otherwise a later edit can assign the wait to the wrong property.

Try quick passes and deliberate holds

Move the pointer across the card quickly, hold it, then leave halfway through the transition. Check keyboard focus, touch activation and reduced motion. If the delay makes a button appear unresponsive, remove it from the action feedback rather than adding a longer animation to compensate.

Use forced interaction states to inspect declarations and an explicit transition list to keep the effect bounded.
coverAlt: Hover entry shows a 250 millisecond wait before a 180 millisecond color transition; exit begins without an added delay.

title: Account for SVG Line Caps When Aligning Icons
description: Compare butt, round and square caps on identical SVG paths, then check how stroke width changes the visible endpoint and spacing around an icon.
keyword: svg stroke linecap round square butt
body:
Two SVG strokes with identical path endpoints can occupy different visible lengths. Butt caps stop at the endpoints; round and square caps extend beyond them. Inspect the painted shape before moving path coordinates to compensate for an apparent alignment error.

Keep the geometry constant

<svg viewBox="0 0 120 100" width="240" height="200" aria-hidden="true">
  <g stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="12">
    <path d="M20 20H100" stroke-linecap="butt" />
    <path d="M20 50H100" stroke-linecap="round" />
    <path d="M20 80H100" stroke-linecap="square" />
  </g>
</svg>

All three centerlines run from x=20 to x=100. With a 12-unit stroke, the round and square caps extend six units beyond each endpoint; butt does not. Round ends are semicircular while square ends stay rectangular. The generous viewBox keeps the extensions visible.

Reference: MDN stroke-linecap.

Separate endpoints from corners

Line caps affect open subpath ends. Corners where segments meet are controlled by stroke-linejoin, so changing linecap will not round a sharp elbow in the middle of a continuous path. A closed path has no exposed pair of ends to treat the same way.

Check the computed presentation when an exported attribute seems ignored: a CSS stroke-linecap declaration can override the presentation attribute. Also inspect clipping around the SVG viewport before concluding that the cap setting failed.

Review the icon at its actual size

Put the icon next to its real label and compare at the intended CSS dimensions. A cap that looks balanced in a large vector editor can alter a small icon’s apparent weight or gap. Record both the path bounds and the stroke treatment in the handoff, especially if multiple icons share a grid.

Use non-scaling strokes deliberately when resizing, and currentColor to keep decorative icons synchronized with their text.
coverAlt: Three identical line centerlines show butt, round and square caps extending to different painted boundaries.

title: Restore Holes in a Compound SVG Path with the Right Fill Rule
description: Inspect compound paths with nonzero and evenodd, verify contour direction, and avoid painting a fake background-colored hole into a reusable icon.
keyword: svg fill rule evenodd nonzero holes
body:
When a hole disappears from an exported SVG icon, inspect the compound path and its fill rule. Evenodd treats nested regions by crossing parity; nonzero also depends on contour direction. A white rectangle over a filled shape is not a transparent hole.

Compare the same two contours

<svg viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="160" height="160" aria-hidden="true">
  <path fill="currentColor" fill-rule="evenodd"
        d="M10 10H90V90H10Z M30 30H70V70H30Z" />
</svg>

This original square-ring specimen has two clockwise contours in one path. Evenodd leaves the inner square open. Change the rule to nonzero without editing the coordinates and the interior fills. Then reverse only the inner contour to investigate how winding direction changes the nonzero result.

Reference: MDN fill-rule.

Check whether the export is actually compound

Fill-rule does not make two independent sibling rectangles subtract from each other. The relationship in this example exists inside one compound path. If an editor exported separate filled elements, inspect its boolean-path or export settings instead of repeatedly changing a rule on the wrapper.

A CSS fill-rule can override the presentation attribute. A clipping path may also involve clip-rule rather than the fill rule you are examining. Identify which operation produces the visible boundary before changing the artwork.

Place the icon on contrasting surfaces

Test a light surface, a dark surface and a patterned surface. A true hole exposes each background; a painted white patch does not. Check small-size legibility after optimization and compare the optimized path with the original export. Preserve the intended fill rule when moving the SVG into a shared component.

Use currentColor icons for theme-aware paint, and check repeated SVG identifiers if the failure only appears when several instances are present.
coverAlt: Two compound square paths with matching contour directions fill completely under nonzero and reveal an inner hole under evenodd.

title: Show a Calculated Result with HTML output
description: Associate a calculated result with its inputs, handle empty numeric values, and keep displayed output separate from data submitted by the form.
keyword: html output element calculation form submission
body:
The output element represents a calculation or user-action result. Its for attribute can identify contributing inputs, but it does not perform the calculation. Write the update logic and remember that output content is not submitted as an ordinary form field.

Calculate a simple layout width

<label for="columns">Columns</label>
<input id="columns" type="number" min="1" step="1" value="3">
<p>Total at 80px per column: <output id="total" for="columns">240px</output></p>
<script>
const columns = document.querySelector('#columns');
const total = document.querySelector('#total');
function update() {
  const n = columns.valueAsNumber;
  total.value = Number.isFinite(n) && columns.validity.valid
    ? `${n * 80}px` : 'Enter a positive whole number';
}
columns.addEventListener('input', update);
update();
</script>

This specimen intentionally excludes gutters. Its label and surrounding sentence explain the formula, so 240px is not an unexplained number. Empty or invalid entries show a useful message instead of NaN. The initial update keeps the result aligned with the actual starting value.

Reference: MDN output.

Decide what must be sent to the server

Giving output a name does not make its displayed result part of submission. Send the underlying inputs and calculate authoritative results on the server when needed. A hidden field can transport a value, but it is still client-controlled and should not become the authority for a price or permission.

Many browser and assistive-technology combinations announce output changes. Avoid adding several competing live regions around the same rapidly changing result. Keep the text concise and test the actual announcement behavior.

Exercise the incomplete states

Clear the input, type a fraction, enter zero and restore a valid integer. Verify that the result explains each state without stealing focus. If this pattern becomes part of a resettable form, ensure the input and output defaults remain synchronized after reset too.

Review numeric step validity for accepted values and status announcements when several updates compete for attention.
coverAlt: A three-column input produces a 240 pixel calculated result at 80 pixels per column, with empty values handled explicitly.

title: Route Submit Buttons with Native Form Overrides
description: Use formaction and formmethod for distinct native submission destinations, then verify validation, keyboard submission and any JavaScript interception.
body:
A submit button can override its form’s destination and method. This supports a normal submit path and a separate preview path without changing the form action on every click. The server still needs to implement both destinations.

Make each action explicit

<form action="/reviews/save" method="post">
  <label for="review-title">Review title</label>
  <input id="review-title" name="title" required>
  <button type="submit">Save review</button>
  <button type="submit" formaction="/reviews/preview" formmethod="post">
    Preview review
  </button>
</form>

These are illustrative endpoint paths, not services provided by the example. The save button uses the form settings; the preview button supplies overrides. Both still participate in normal validation because neither has formnovalidate. Preview should not bypass required checks accidentally just because it is a secondary action.

Reference: MDN button.

Keep native transport and custom handlers aligned

If a script cancels submission and calls fetch with a hard-coded URL, the browser’s native routing no longer supplies the complete behavior. Read the submitter deliberately and reproduce only the intended transport policy. Also decide whether preview is truly a server submission or a local display action that should use type="button".

Do not send sensitive form contents with GET merely for convenient preview routing: GET places submitted fields in a URL. Keep server-side validation and authorization appropriate to each operation.

Test each trigger independently

Activate Save, activate Preview, and press Enter from the text field. Confirm which button or default path the browser uses and inspect the request destination and method in Network. Repeat with an empty required field. If a script triggers submission, requestSubmit with the chosen button can preserve its role in native submission.

See SubmitEvent.submitter for identifying the action and requestSubmit versus submit for programmatic behavior.
coverAlt: A form branches to save and preview POST destinations, with normal validation retained on both submit buttons.

title: Choose Spellchecking by the Kind of Text Being Edited
description: Keep spelling assistance for prose while disabling it for code-like identifiers, and verify the actual browser behavior without treating it as validation.
body:
A CSS token editor and a review-notes field contain different kinds of text. Spellcheck can be useful for prose and distracting for identifiers. Set the attribute narrowly on each field instead of disabling assistance across the entire page.

Give prose and code separate policies

<label for="token">CSS token name</label>
<input id="token" name="token" spellcheck="false" value="--surface-card">
<label for="notes">Review notes</label>
<textarea id="notes" name="notes" spellcheck="true" lang="en"></textarea>

The token example is deliberately code-like; a spelling underline under surface-card would not indicate a malformed CSS custom property. The notes field contains ordinary English. Keep visible labels in place so the browser’s spelling feedback is not the only clue about what belongs in either control.

Reference: MDN spellcheck.

Do not confuse spelling with correctness

Spellcheck is an enumerated attribute: false is meaningful, rather than the presence of the attribute automatically enabling it. Omitted behavior depends on the element, inheritance and browser. A true setting is a request for available checking, not a guarantee of identical dictionaries or underlines on every device.

Spelling feedback does not enforce your application’s token syntax, and it is separate from autocomplete or keyboard correction. Validate identifiers using explicit rules. For sensitive fields, review whether enhanced spelling services could process the content; disabling a field’s spellcheck is not a general data-security guarantee.

Review editing, pasting and language changes

Type a deliberately misspelled word into notes, then paste a valid token into its field. Test with browser spelling enabled and disabled. Check a second content language if the application supports it, and retain clear errors for invalid identifiers regardless of spelling settings. Record the browser settings when a reviewer reports unexpected underlines.

Use language markup accurately and keep persistent field labels independent of editing assistance.
coverAlt: A code-like token field requests spellcheck false while a prose notes field requests spellcheck true.

title: Match the Mobile Enter Key Label to the Field’s Action
description: Use enterkeyhint to request a useful virtual-keyboard action label, while keeping submission behavior and visible controls implemented separately.
body:
Enterkeyhint asks the virtual keyboard to label its Enter key for the next action, such as search or send. It does not create that action. Pair the hint with a form or interaction whose actual behavior matches the label.

Use a native search form

<form action="/search" method="get" role="search">
  <label for="query">Search design guides</label>
  <input id="query" name="q" type="search" enterkeyhint="search">
  <button type="submit">Search guides</button>
</form>

The /search route is a specimen that your application must implement. The form supplies a native submission mechanism and the visible button provides an alternative to the keyboard action. The hint improves the label where supported; it is not responsible for the query string or results page.

Reference: MDN enterkeyhint.

Keep keyboard layout, hints and behavior separate

Input type describes the control, inputmode suggests a keyboard layout, and enterkeyhint suggests the action-key label or icon. A next hint does not give you a complete focus-management system for a custom wizard. Likewise, send does not implement message delivery or its error handling.

The exact label depends on the keyboard, browser and language. Unsupported hints should leave a usable form. Do not hide the submit button merely because one tested phone displays the desired action key.

Test on the keyboard people will use

Focus the field on a real mobile device and inspect the key. Submit by that key and by the visible button, then repeat with an external keyboard. Check that a multiline notes field still allows the intended line breaks; a misleading send label there can encourage accidental submission.

For a multi-step form, review the focus destination after every action, especially when validation prevents progress. Compare inputmode and type, and set button types explicitly so helper actions do not submit unexpectedly.
coverAlt: A search input is paired with an illustrative mobile keyboard action labeled Search, with a reminder to keep a visible submit control.

title: Read Every Selected Value from a Multiple Select
description: Use FormData.getAll for repeated field names, inspect empty selections, and keep the native multiple-select interaction understandable on different devices.
body:
A multiple select can submit several entries with the same field name. FormData.get returns just one value; getAll returns the collection. Converting the whole form directly into a plain object can silently discard repeated entries.

Preserve the repeated name

<form id="filters">
  <label for="topics">Topics (choose one or more)</label>
  <select id="topics" name="topic" multiple size="3" required>
    <option value="css" selected>CSS</option>
    <option value="type" selected>Typography</option>
    <option value="color">Color</option>
  </select>
</form>
<script>
const data = new FormData(document.querySelector('#filters'));
console.log(data.getAll('topic')); // ['css', 'type']
</script>

The selected attributes establish this specimen’s initial choices. Read a fresh FormData after a later user change; the original object is a snapshot, not a live view of the form. Keep array handling on the receiving side too so the second choice does not disappear after transport.

Reference: MDN select.

Define what an empty selection means

Without selected options, the field contributes no selected values and getAll returns an empty array. Required can prevent ordinary valid submission with no choice, but constructing FormData does not itself run the form’s validation workflow. A script that submits data must preserve the intended checks.

Native multiple-selection gestures vary across devices and platforms. For a short visible set of independent filters, labeled checkboxes may be easier to discover. Choose based on the interaction, not only on the space a compact list saves.

Check selection and serialization together

Select two options, deselect everything, and choose the final option alone. Inspect the array after each change and test the actual submitted request. Include keyboard use and a touch device in the review. Confirm the selected styling stays readable in forced colors rather than relying on a custom color alone.

Use optgroup for meaningful groups and compare checkbox submission rules when evaluating another control.
coverAlt: CSS and Typography are selected together and produce two values through FormData getAll rather than a single scalar.

title: Align Wrapped List Items with Their Markers
description: Compare inside and outside list markers, preserve indentation at narrow widths, and diagnose an unexpected line break before a list item’s paragraph.
keyword: css list style position inside outside wrapped text
body:
List-style-position controls whether a marker sits outside the item’s principal box or participates inside its content. For a long instruction that wraps, outside usually produces the familiar hanging alignment: continuation lines align with the text, not with the bullet.

Compare a long item in a narrow list

.instructions {
  max-inline-size: 28ch;
  padding-inline-start: 1.5em;
  list-style-position: outside;
}
.instructions li + li { margin-block-start: .75em; }

Apply this to a semantic ul or ol containing a sentence long enough to wrap. Toggle outside to inside in DevTools. With inside, the marker takes space at the start of the first line; following lines can begin at the item’s content edge. Keep the same font and width while comparing.

Reference: MDN list-style-position.

Inspect the first child when a marker stands alone

An inside marker followed by a block-level first child can appear on a line before that child. Check whether your markup wraps the item’s text in a paragraph or another block before adding negative margins. The problem may be the relationship between the marker and block content rather than an unexplained browser offset.

Removing all list padding can push outside markers against a clipping boundary. Restore adequate inline-start room instead of hiding overflow. Logical padding also follows writing direction more appropriately than a fixed left-only adjustment.

Review the full list structure

Test short items, long items, nested lists and a list item beginning with a paragraph. Increase text size and inspect both the first and last lines. Confirm that numbered steps remain visibly associated with the correct instruction. Avoid replacing native list semantics with a row of decorative text symbols just to align one screenshot.

Use ::marker styling for marker appearance and logical properties when reviewing right-to-left layouts.
coverAlt: Wrapped list text aligns after an outside marker, while inside placement reserves marker space only on the first text line.

title: Mark Up Inline Quotations Without Doubling the Quotes
description: Use q for a genuine inline quotation, keep source attribution visible, and inspect generated quotation marks before adding punctuation by hand.
keyword: html q tag double quotation marks cite
body:
Use q for a short inline quotation, not merely to decorate a slogan. Browsers commonly supply quotation marks around the element. If an imported text string already contains outer marks, wrapping it in q can produce doubled punctuation.

Keep the quotation separate from its attribution

<p>
  In this fictional editing example, the reviewer wrote
  <q>Keep the label beside the control.</q>
</p>

The sentence is explicitly fictional demonstration copy, not a testimonial or a reported product result. No literal opening or closing marks appear inside q. In a real article, reproduce the quotation accurately and identify its actual source in nearby text with an appropriate link.

Reference: MDN q.

Distinguish a source attribute from a visible citation

The cite attribute on q can point to the source document, but it does not automatically render an attribution link for readers. Provide one in ordinary content when needed. Use blockquote for a longer block quotation instead of enlarging an inline q until it happens to look like a pull quote.

Inspect the browser’s generated quotation styling, including nested quotations and the language context. A global reset or custom pseudo-element rule can remove or duplicate marks. Do not add another pair blindly before checking the computed styles.

Review copied and localized text

Paste the rendered sentence into the places readers are likely to use it and check whether the quotation remains understandable. Review the markup with styles disabled, then with your production stylesheet. For translated content, set the correct language and review punctuation conventions with someone who knows that language.

Before publishing, verify the exact wording, attribution and permission requirements for the actual quoted material. The language guide helps establish context; the figure-caption guide covers explanatory text accompanying illustrations rather than quotations.
coverAlt: A fictional editing quote appears once with generated outer quotation marks, and source attribution remains separate visible content.

title: Use placeholder-shown Without Treating It as Validation
description: Style a field while its placeholder is visible, distinguish the pseudo-class from placeholder text styling, and test empty, invalid and autofilled states.
body:
The :placeholder-shown pseudo-class matches a control while it displays placeholder text. It does not mean the user has not touched the field, and its absence does not establish that the value is valid. Keep those states separate in form design.

Style the control while the example is visible

<label for="contact">Contact email</label>
<input id="contact" type="email" required placeholder="name@example.com">
<style>
#contact:placeholder-shown { background-color: #f4f6f8; }
#contact::placeholder { color: #626871; opacity: 1; }
</style>

The pseudo-class changes the field’s background. The ::placeholder pseudo-element styles the example text itself. The label stays visible after typing. Choose actual colors by checking contrast in the rendered theme rather than assuming these specimen values suit every background.

Reference: MDN :placeholder-shown.

Name the states your design actually needs

Type an invalid email such as abc: the placeholder disappears even though validation fails. Clear the field: the placeholder returns, although the user has interacted with it. A field without a placeholder is not a reliable participant in an “all empty inputs” selector based on this pseudo-class.

Autofill and programmatic value changes can also alter the visible state. If an error should appear only after submission or deliberate interaction, track that policy explicitly instead of using not(:placeholder-shown) as proof that a field is ready for judgment.

Test a small state matrix

Review the initial empty field, a typed invalid value, a valid value, clearing after entry and an autofilled value. Keep the same persistent label in every state. Check that error text identifies the problem and remains connected to the control; a changed background alone is insufficient feedback.

Read labels versus placeholders before implementing floating-label patterns, and use connected error messages for validation results.
coverAlt: An empty email field shows its placeholder while an invalid typed value hides it, demonstrating that placeholder visibility is not validity.

title: Diagnose Gaps in Text Underlines Before Replacing Them
description: Check text-decoration-skip-ink when underlines break around letter descenders, compare the actual font, and keep links recognizable across wrapped lines.
keyword: css underline gaps text decoration skip ink
body:
An underline that breaks around letters such as g, p or y may be working as intended. Text-decoration-skip-ink lets the browser interrupt decoration near glyph ink. Determine whether you are seeing intentional gaps before replacing the underline with a border.

Compare the same text with two policies

.sample-link {
  text-decoration-line: underline;
  text-decoration-thickness: .08em;
  text-underline-offset: .12em;
  text-decoration-skip-ink: auto;
}
.sample-link.continuous { text-decoration-skip-ink: none; }

Use the same linked phrase containing descenders, such as “Typography playground,” in both specimens. Auto allows interruptions around glyphs; none draws continuously through the text’s decoration path. Keep the font, size, thickness and offset identical so the policy is the only changing variable.

Reference: MDN text-decoration-skip-ink.

Check the font and offset together

The visible gap depends on the glyph outlines and underline placement. A fallback font can produce a different result from the intended web font. Compare after the actual font loads, and inspect a language-relevant sample rather than a single Latin word if the interface supports other writing systems.

A bottom border belongs to the element’s box and does not automatically behave like text decoration across wrapped lines. Replacing an underline with a border can trade one visual difference for alignment and wrapping problems.

Keep the link recognizable at reading size

Review normal-sized body text, enlarged text and a link that spans two lines. Try default, hover and keyboard-focus states. If gaps make the underline difficult to perceive, adjust thickness or offset and compare again before forcing a continuous line through descenders. Preserve sufficient contrast and an independent focus indicator.
