Use the complete underline styling guide for the broader link treatment and font inspection to confirm which outlines you are actually judging.
coverAlt: Two simplified underline diagrams compare interruptions around glyph descenders with a continuous line crossing the same descenders.

title: Choose a Condensed Font Face Instead of Squashing Text
description: Inspect font width support and available faces, distinguish font selection from transform scaling, and verify layout with the actual loaded font.
keyword: css font width font stretch condensed
body:
A condensed font face has glyphs designed for a narrower proportion. Font-width selects an available width; it does not mechanically squeeze any arbitrary font. If the family has no matching width capability, changing the property may not produce the expected visual difference.

Compare a supported family at two widths

.width-specimen {
  font-family: "Your Width Family", sans-serif;
  font-stretch: condensed;
  font-width: condensed;
}
.width-specimen.normal {
  font-stretch: normal;
  font-width: normal;
}

Replace the specimen family with an actual loaded family offering condensed faces or a supported width axis. The older font-stretch name is included for browsers using that property name; verify which declaration your target browser accepts. The example does not download a font or establish an appropriate @font-face range by itself.

Reference: MDN font-width.

Inspect selection before manipulating geometry

Confirm the rendered font, available faces and face descriptors. A variable font needs the intended axis and a correctly exposed range. Low-level font-variation-settings can also complicate the result if it directly controls width. Change one layer at a time while recording the actual font file.

Transform: scaleX changes painted geometry without providing the same layout behavior or designed glyph shapes. Letter-spacing changes gaps between characters instead of selecting narrower letterforms. Neither is a drop-in replacement for a condensed face.

Check fit without sacrificing readability

Compare the real heading, a long label, numbers and punctuation at the intended size. Measure line breaks and the surrounding layout as well as the apparent width. Disable the web font temporarily to review fallback behavior. Do not compress critical text indefinitely to preserve a fixed screenshot; allow the container or line count to adapt.

Use the variable-font axis guide to map file capabilities and the font-loading checklist when the requested face never appears.
coverAlt: A font selection checklist checks available faces, exposed width range and the rendered font before judging condensed text.

title: Blur Behind a Panel Without Blurring Its Text
description: Separate filter from backdrop-filter, keep a readable solid fallback, and inspect the surfaces behind a translucent panel before approving its contrast.
keyword: css backdrop filter vs filter blur text
body:
Filter changes the rendered element, including its contents. Backdrop-filter changes pixels behind the element within its backdrop boundary. For a frosted panel with sharp text, apply the backdrop effect to the panel and give it a partially transparent surface.

Keep a usable surface before adding blur

.review-panel {
  color: #13261c;
  background: #eff7f2;
  padding: 1.5rem;
  border: 1px solid #bbcfc2;
}
@supports (backdrop-filter: blur(8px)) {
  .review-panel {
    background: rgb(239 247 242 / .88);
    backdrop-filter: blur(8px);
  }
}

Place the panel over a detailed decorative background so the effect can be compared. The initial solid surface is the fallback. The supported enhancement makes some background visible without applying blur to the text. These colors and opacity are specimen values to assess with the actual content behind your panel.

Reference: MDN backdrop-filter.

Inspect the backdrop boundary and compositing

An opaque panel background can conceal the effect even when the declaration is active. Ancestor effects can establish a backdrop boundary, limiting which pixels are filtered. Inspect the relevant ancestor chain before increasing blur to compensate for a missing visual change.

Do not lower the whole panel’s opacity to create transparency: that also fades its text and controls. A background alpha value and element opacity have different consequences. A blurred photograph can still contain bright and dark regions that affect readability.

Review changing content behind the surface

Move the panel over both the lightest and darkest expected background regions, then disable backdrop-filter. Read the labels, focus outlines and secondary text in each case. Scroll a representative page and inspect rendering performance if the effect feels slow. Keep a solid surface when the effect makes the interface less dependable.

Compare alpha backgrounds and opacity, and use the state-by-state contrast review with the final composited colors.
coverAlt: A translucent review panel keeps its label sharp over a softened decorative backdrop, alongside a reminder to retain a solid fallback.

title: Blend Background Layers Without Blending the Text
description: Inspect background-blend-mode with explicit layer ordering, compare a controlled gradient specimen, and keep content colors independent of decorative blending.
keyword: css background blend mode vs mix blend mode
body:
Background-blend-mode combines an element’s background layers and base color. It does not apply the same blend operation to the text inside that element. Use it for a decorative background treatment when blending the entire element would change content unexpectedly.

Use gradients to isolate the operation

.swatch {
  min-block-size: 12rem;
  background-color: #e8f3ed;
  background-image:
    linear-gradient(90deg, #8bb7ee 50%, transparent 50%),
    linear-gradient(#96cfb0 50%, transparent 50%);
  background-blend-mode: multiply, normal;
}
.swatch strong { color: #101813; }

The first gradient is the top background layer. Its multiply setting combines it with the backdrop formed by the lower layer and base color; the second layer uses normal. Toggle multiply to normal while keeping all colors fixed. The text’s declared color remains a separate content decision.

Reference: MDN background-blend-mode.

Keep the layer lists understandable

Background images, positions, sizes and blend modes are parallel lists. A later edit that inserts a new image at the front can change which mode applies to which layer. Write the intended layer order in the component review rather than relying on a visually similar screenshot.

Mix-blend-mode concerns the rendered element and its surrounding backdrop, so it is a different tool. If text changes unexpectedly, inspect whether that property is present on the element or an ancestor before rewriting the gradient.

Compare decoration and content independently

First hide the text and inspect the background intersections. Then restore the content and check readable contrast over every relevant region. If the production background uses an external image, test its missing-image state as well. Keep meaningful information in ordinary content rather than encoding it only in the overlap color.

See the multiple-background guide for list alignment and blend isolation for effects involving the element’s surroundings.
coverAlt: Two decorative background layers and a base color feed a blend operation while the text color remains a separate setting.

title: Inspect Individual Transforms Alongside the Transform List
description: Check translate, rotate and scale independently from transform, and avoid leaving a second transform active when migrating a component’s movement rules.
keyword: css individual translate rotate scale transform order
body:
The individual translate, rotate and scale properties can remain active even when transform is none. They compose in a defined order before the transform property. A migration that adds individual properties without removing an older transform can therefore apply movement twice.

Compare two deliberately different states

.specimen {
  inline-size: 40px;
  block-size: 40px;
  background: #0f7fff;
  transform-origin: 0 0;
  translate: 40px 0;
  rotate: 90deg;
  scale: 1;
  transform: none;
}
.specimen.extra { transform: translateX(20px); }

Place each specimen in an identical, sufficiently large track. The extra class adds a transform list while keeping all individual properties. With the fixed top-left origin, the additional local translation appears along the rotated axis. Compare element bounds rather than assuming the second translation simply adds 20px horizontally.

Reference: MDN transform.

Reset the property that actually moves the element

Inspect computed translate, rotate, scale and transform separately. A declaration of transform: none clears only that property’s list; it does not reset the other three. Individual properties compose as translate, rotate, scale, then transform, regardless of their order in the stylesheet.

Inside a transform function list, function order matters as well. Keep the origin and reference box constant during comparisons. Rewriting a working transform into several properties should be treated as a geometry change to verify, not just a formatting change.

Check layout and interaction after migration

Compare default, hover and animated states, including any inherited component overrides. Inspect the visual bounds and nearby content because transforms do not reserve new layout space. Ensure the transformed control still has a clear focus indicator and does not overlap another action.

Use the transform-origin guide to isolate pivots and the layout-space explanation when the element’s old space remains visible.
coverAlt: Separate translate, rotate and scale settings compose with the transform list, and transform none clears only the last list.

title: Control a Paragraph’s Last Line Without Adding Spaces
description: Use text-align-last for intentional paragraph endings, understand forced line breaks, and avoid manual spacing that fails when text or viewport width changes.
keyword: css text align last justified paragraph
body:
Text-align-last controls the final line of a block and a line immediately before a forced break. It can keep the last line of a justified paragraph aligned to the reading direction without adding spaces or extra wrapper elements.

Keep the final line aligned to the start

.specimen-copy {
  max-inline-size: 42ch;
  text-align: justify;
  text-align-last: start;
}

Use a paragraph long enough to wrap across several lines, then resize its container. Start follows text direction, unlike a hard-coded left value. This is a comparison specimen, not a recommendation to justify all interface copy; uneven word spacing can reduce readability in narrow columns.

Reference: MDN text-align-last.

Inspect forced breaks and inheritance

A br introduces a forced line ending, so text-align-last can affect more than the visually final line of a paragraph containing several breaks. If several short lines unexpectedly align differently, inspect the markup before changing the rule. Also check inherited values from a surrounding content wrapper.

The default auto generally follows text-align, with special treatment for justified text: the last line aligns to the start. Setting justify on text-align-last can spread a short ending across the available width. That may create much larger gaps than the designer intended.

Review natural wrapping with real copy

Try an ending with one word, an ending with several words and a paragraph that becomes a single line at a wide viewport. Increase text size and inspect a right-to-left sample if the site supports one. Remove manual spaces and unnecessary br elements that were added merely to reproduce a screenshot.

Judge the full paragraph’s rhythm, not just the final line’s symmetry. The reading-width guide helps establish the container, while text-wrap options address line breaking rather than last-line alignment.
coverAlt: A justified paragraph diagram has full middle lines and a shorter final line aligned to the start of the text block.

title: Control Tab Stops in Displayed Code Without Rewriting It
description: Use tab-size with preserved whitespace, distinguish tabs from spaces, and compare copied source with the visual indentation in a code specimen.
keyword: css tab size pre code indentation
body:
Tab-size changes the visual spacing of tab characters in preserved text. It does not replace tabs with spaces in the source. If a code sample’s indentation refuses to change, first inspect whether its leading characters are tabs at all.

Preserve whitespace and set the tab interval

<pre class="code-sample"><code>card {
	color: blue;
}</code></pre>
<style>
.code-sample {
  white-space: pre;
  overflow: auto;
  tab-size: 4;
  font-family: monospace;
}
</style>

The numeric character reference creates one actual tab before color. The value 4 establishes tab intervals based on four space advances in the selected font. A tab advances to a tab stop, so its visible width depends on the preceding position; it is not always equivalent to inserting exactly four spaces.

Reference: MDN tab-size.

Check the rendering pipeline

A formatter, Markdown processor or syntax highlighter may expand tabs before the browser receives the text. Inspect textContent and the generated markup when changing tab-size has no effect. Normal whitespace collapsing can also prevent the intended tab layout from surviving.

Length values are possible, but a fixed pixel interval does not scale with the font the same way a number-based interval does. Choose the representation that matches the source viewer’s purpose and test it with the actual font.

Keep copying and navigation useful

Copy the specimen into a plain-text editor to see what readers actually receive. Test a line with a tab after existing characters, a line indented with spaces and an unusually long line. Ensure horizontal scrolling does not create overflow for the whole page or hide a copy button’s focus indicator.

Use whitespace rules when deciding whether lines may wrap, and the long-content guide for prose that should not behave like source code.
coverAlt: A tab character advances to a stop in a displayed code line, with a comparison between source tabs and ordinary spaces.

title: Explain Abbreviations Without Depending on a Hover Tooltip
description: Use abbr for abbreviation semantics, provide unfamiliar expansions in visible text, and keep explanations available on touch and keyboard devices.
body:
An abbreviation’s meaning should not depend on a reader discovering a browser tooltip. Use abbr when the semantics are useful, and explain an unfamiliar term in visible text at an appropriate point in the reading flow.

Expand the term where it first matters

<p>
  Document Object Model (<abbr>DOM</abbr>) inspection helps you
  connect a visible component with its rendered markup.
</p>

The expansion is available without hovering, focusing or guessing. The abbr element marks the shortened form; it does not require a title attribute. Later uses can stay concise when the context remains clear. In a long reference page, a visible glossary link can be more useful than repeating the full expansion in every sentence.

Reference: MDN abbr.

Use title as supplementary information

When title is used on abbr, its content should be the full expansion or description. Each occurrence stands on its own: adding a title to one DOM abbreviation does not automatically define every other occurrence on the page.

Browser tooltip access and assistive-technology announcement behavior vary. Do not make essential instructions available only through title. Avoid turning every familiar acronym into a keyboard stop just to imitate a tooltip; that can make ordinary reading unnecessarily cumbersome.

Review the paragraph without pointer hover

Read the page on a touch device and navigate it with the keyboard. Confirm that a newcomer can understand the term from the visible sentence. Inspect any dotted underline or custom styling to ensure it does not falsely suggest a link. If the abbreviation has several meanings, use the expansion appropriate to this exact context.

Keep language markup accurate when the expansion contains a meaningful language change. See the language-markup guide and the tooltip review when supplementary help becomes an interactive component.
coverAlt: Document Object Model is written visibly beside the abbreviation DOM, so the meaning does not require hovering.

title: Highlight Search Matches with Meaningful HTML mark
description: Use mark for query-relevant text, retain readable highlighted colors, and keep result context available when assistive technology does not announce the marking.
body:
Mark identifies text that is relevant to the reader’s current activity, such as the words matching a search query. It is a better semantic fit for search-result emphasis than using strong simply because the design calls for a colored background.

Keep the query and result context visible

<p>Results for “spacing”</p>
<p>Review the <mark>spacing</mark> between a label and its control.</p>
<style>
mark { background: #fff1a6; color: #242014; }
</style>

This is a static specimen showing the resulting markup, not a search implementation. The surrounding sentence still makes sense without the highlight. The query text above the results explains why the word has been marked; the highlight does not have to carry that explanation alone.

Reference: MDN mark.

Distinguish relevance from importance

Strong expresses importance; mark expresses contextual relevance. A query match is not automatically the most important instruction in the document. Likewise, syntax highlighting in a code block usually needs styling spans rather than labeling every colored token with mark.

If your application builds highlights from user input, construct text nodes and mark elements deliberately. Do not insert a raw query as HTML. Preserve the original text and link boundaries when a match crosses punctuation or appears inside an existing anchor.

Test multiple and missing matches

Review no matches, one match and several adjacent matches. Check the highlighted foreground/background pair in every supported theme. Read the result using assistive technology: marking is not consistently announced by default, so the result title, query context and any count should remain useful without that cue.

For dynamic searches, announce a concise result count rather than flooding a live region with every highlighted word. Use the status-message guide and the contrast checklist to review the final result presentation.
coverAlt: A result for spacing highlights the matching word inside a readable sentence while keeping the query context visible.

title: Show Inserted and Deleted Copy in a Design Review
description: Use ins and del for edits, provide a plain-language change summary, and distinguish revision markup from text that is simply no longer relevant.
keyword: html ins del change tracking accessible
body:
Ins and del describe inserted and deleted content. They can make a copy review easier to compare, but a colored underline or strike-through alone is not a dependable explanation of the change. Pair revision markup with a short visible summary.

Mark the smallest useful replacement

<p>Change summary: the action label now explains what is exported.</p>
<p>
  Button label:
  <del>Continue</del>
  <ins>Export review</ins>
</p>

The wording is an illustrative design edit, not a statement about a product release. Keeping each element around only the changed phrase makes the comparison easier to scan. The ordinary summary remains useful if a reader does not perceive or hear the revision styling.

Reference: MDN ins.

Keep dates and source context truthful

The datetime attribute can record when an edit occurred, and cite can identify a resource explaining it. Neither automatically creates a visible date or clickable explanation for readers. If that information matters, include it in the surrounding content and use real dates and accessible source links.

Use revision elements for an actual edit history. Text that is merely no longer accurate or relevant can have a different semantic treatment, such as s. Do not imply a deletion-and-insertion event just to get a preferred visual effect.

Review the comparison and the final copy

Check that the old and new phrases remain distinguishable without color. Listen to the paragraph with the assistive technology your team supports; insertion and deletion boundaries may need an explicit visible explanation. Then read the final sentence with deleted text removed to ensure the proposed copy stands on its own.

In a handoff, distinguish proposed changes from accepted ones and link to the decision when available. Use machine-readable dates for real timestamps and the handoff checklist to capture ownership and acceptance criteria.
coverAlt: An illustrative copy revision replaces Continue with Export review, with an explicit change summary above the old and new labels.

title: Give an Informative Inline SVG a Reliable Name
description: Name an informative inline SVG with title and aria-labelledby, avoid duplicate IDs in repeated components, and treat decorative icons differently.
keyword: inline svg title aria labelledby accessible name
body:
An informative inline SVG needs a name that communicates its purpose. A title element can supply a short description, and an explicit aria-labelledby relationship makes the intended naming source clear. Decorative icons beside an already clear label usually need a different treatment.

Name one self-contained graphic

<svg viewBox="0 0 80 40" role="img" aria-labelledby="layout-comparison-title">
  <title id="layout-comparison-title">Two equal columns with a central gutter</title>
  <rect x="2" y="2" width="34" height="36" fill="#8bb7ee" />
  <rect x="44" y="2" width="34" height="36" fill="#8bb7ee" />
</svg>

The name explains the meaningful geometry rather than saying only “image.” Title appears first inside the SVG. The graphic is intentionally simple enough for its short name; a complex chart would also need an accessible explanation of the important data and relationships.

Reference: MDN title.

Choose the naming owner deliberately

If this SVG sits inside a button whose visible text already names the action, the button may not need a second graphic name. Hide a purely decorative icon from assistive technology in that case. Avoid simultaneously adding conflicting labels to the SVG, its wrapper and the button.

An SVG loaded through img belongs to a different embedding pattern: provide the image alternative on img rather than assuming this inline relationship can be copied unchanged. Keep the graphic’s role in the surrounding interface clear before selecting markup.

Check repeated instances in the accessibility tree

Generate unique title IDs when rendering several instances. Duplicate IDs can make a reference point to another graphic’s title. Inspect the computed role and name, then verify the reading order and whether the name adds useful information. Test with the actual browser and assistive technology rather than relying on a hover tooltip.

Use name versus description relationships to separate short identification from supporting detail, and decorative icon styling when visible text already provides the action name.
coverAlt: An inline graphic with two equal columns is connected to a title identifier that supplies its accessible name.

title: Make New-Tab Links Predictable for Readers
description: Use new tabs only when needed, disclose the behavior in the link text, and keep opener behavior separate from the visible navigation experience.
keyword: target blank link opens new tab accessible notice
body:
A link normally navigates in the current browsing context. When opening another tab or window serves a clear purpose, tell readers before activation. Target="_blank" requests a new browsing context; the browser and user settings decide its exact presentation.

Keep the notice part of the link

<a href="https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS"
   target="_blank" rel="noopener">
  CSS reference (opens in a new tab)
</a>

The destination is a real documentation page. The wording communicates the intended behavior without requiring a reader to recognize a small external-link icon. Rel="noopener" explicitly avoids giving the opened page an opener reference; modern browsers also provide implicit noopener behavior for ordinary _blank links.

Reference: MDN a.

Do not force every external link into another context

A documentation link is not automatically a reason to override familiar navigation. Consider whether the current page contains unsaved work or another concrete continuity need. Readers can often choose a new tab themselves through browser controls when the link retains normal behavior.

Opener handling and referrer handling are separate decisions. Do not add unrelated attributes just to copy a common snippet. If a project has a specific referrer policy, review that policy on its own terms.

Test the announcement and the return path

Inspect the link’s accessible name, activate it from the keyboard, and return to the original page. Make sure the notice is not duplicated by both hidden text and an icon label. If an icon is decorative, hide it from the accessibility tree while preserving the explicit wording.

Check narrow layouts so the notice wraps without separating it from the destination name. Use native links for navigation and the supporting-text guide when the interface needs a concise visible label with additional accessible context.
coverAlt: A CSS reference link visibly states that it opens in a new tab, while target and opener settings are documented beneath it.

title: Select Elements Whose IDs Contain CSS Punctuation
description: Escape dynamic CSS identifiers before constructing selectors, compare querySelector with getElementById, and keep selector escaping distinct from HTML handling.
body:
An HTML ID can contain characters that have special meaning in a CSS selector. A colon in an ID is literal data for getElementById but can begin a pseudo-class in querySelector. Escape the identifier when building a CSS selector from that value.

Try an ID with a colon

<div id="panel:preview">Preview</div>
<script>
const id = 'panel:preview';
const direct = document.getElementById(id);
const selected = document.querySelector(`#${CSS.escape(id)}`);
console.log(direct === selected); // true
</script>

The escape function receives the identifier, not the complete selector with its leading #. For a single known ID, getElementById avoids selector construction entirely. Query selectors remain useful when you need to combine an escaped identifier with a structural relationship.

Reference: MDN escape_static.

Handle missing elements separately from invalid selectors

A valid selector with no match returns null. Invalid selector syntax can throw an exception before a search succeeds. Escaping addresses the syntax problem; it does not guarantee that the target exists or that an ID is unique. Inspect the rendered DOM when a framework-generated identifier differs from the one in a design note.

CSS escaping is for CSS identifier syntax. It is not HTML sanitization, JavaScript string quoting or URL encoding. Use the appropriate API for the context instead of reusing the escaped string everywhere.

Review the full range of generated identifiers

Test a colon, a question mark and a leading digit in an isolated fixture. Compare the exact ID returned by inspection with the selector you build. Keep the query scoped to the intended document or component boundary; a normal document query does not automatically search inside every shadow root.

Use the CSS inspection workflow to identify the rendered element and a DOM breakpoint when attributes change unexpectedly while you investigate.
coverAlt: An ID containing a colon is passed through CSS escape before being used in a selector, while direct ID lookup accepts the original string.

title: Refresh DOM Queries When New Components Are Added
description: Understand querySelectorAll as a static membership list, requery after DOM changes, and avoid confusing live element references with a live collection.
body:
QuerySelectorAll returns a static list of matching elements. Adding another matching card later does not append it to the saved NodeList. The existing entries still refer to real elements, so their properties can change even though the list’s membership does not.

Compare a saved result with a fresh query

<div id="cards"><article class="card">First</article></div>
<script>
const cards = document.querySelector('#cards');
const before = cards.querySelectorAll('.card');
const added = document.createElement('article');
added.className = 'card';
added.textContent = 'Second';
cards.append(added);
console.log(before.length); // 1
console.log(cards.querySelectorAll('.card').length); // 2
</script>

The old list is a snapshot of membership at query time. If you change the first card’s text, before[0] points to that changed element; the node itself was not frozen. This is why console inspection can seem inconsistent if collection membership and node state are treated as the same thing.

Reference: MDN querySelectorAll.

Choose a refresh point that matches the application

For an audit triggered by a button, query when the audit runs. For a component that owns insertion, update its bookkeeping at insertion time. For observation of an external DOM change, a narrowly scoped observer may be appropriate. Constantly polling the entire document is usually unnecessary.

A list can retain references to nodes that have since been detached. Check isConnected when that distinction matters, and avoid accumulating obsolete query results in long-lived application state.

Test insertion, removal and replacement

Run the inspection before loading more cards and again afterward. Remove a card and compare the stored list with the current DOM. Replace a wrapper to expose code that still queries the old root. Document whether the report is a point-in-time snapshot or an actively refreshed view.

See scoped mutation observation for change notifications and the select-all example when a dynamic item set affects aggregate selection state.
coverAlt: A saved query contains one card while a new query after insertion contains two, illustrating static collection membership.

title: Observe Component Attribute Changes Without Watching the Whole Page
description: Scope MutationObserver to relevant attributes, capture old values deliberately, and distinguish asynchronous mutation records from a debugger’s call stack.
body:
MutationObserver can report DOM changes such as an attribute update on a component. Limit the observation to the evidence you need. It does not tell you every visual change, and its asynchronous callback is not a replacement for pausing the script that caused a mutation.

Watch two attributes on one component

const panel = document.querySelector('.review-panel');
const observer = new MutationObserver(records => {
  console.table(records.map(record => ({
    attribute: record.attributeName,
    previous: record.oldValue,
    current: record.target.getAttribute(record.attributeName)
  })));
});
if (panel) observer.observe(panel, {
  attributes: true,
  attributeFilter: ['class', 'aria-expanded'],
  attributeOldValue: true
});
// End the diagnostic session with observer.disconnect();

The callback reports the attribute name and captured previous value. The current value is read when the callback runs; several rapid mutations can mean it already reflects a later state. Keep that timing distinction in mind when interpreting a sequence of records.

Reference: MDN observe.

Keep the observation narrow and temporary

This setup does not observe descendants or child insertion. Add subtree or childList only for an explicit question. Logging every mutation across a large application can bury the useful event and add work to an already busy page. Disconnect after the investigation or when the component is permanently removed.

Changing a stylesheet or viewport can alter appearance without changing the observed attributes. Similarly, size changes call for a size observer rather than an assumption that every layout change must have a DOM mutation.

Use the right tool for the missing evidence

Toggle the panel through known states and compare the log with visible behavior. Trigger two quick changes to see how records and current values differ. Avoid changing the same observed attributes inside the callback unless the feedback behavior is intentional.

Use a DOM breakpoint to locate the responsible call stack, and ResizeObserver to investigate component dimensions. Preserve the reproduction steps with the evidence you collect.
coverAlt: A scoped observer watches class and aria-expanded on a single panel and distinguishes a recorded old value from a later current value.

title: Choose Input or Change Events for a Live Preview
description: Update text previews during editing with input, distinguish committed changes, and explicitly synchronize the preview after programmatic value assignments.
keyword: javascript input vs change live preview
body:
For a text field, input follows editing while change generally waits for the value to be committed, such as when focus leaves the field. A live label preview usually needs input. A programmatic value assignment still needs an explicit synchronization step.

Render the current value through one function

<label for="caption">Card caption</label>
<input id="caption" value="Review ready">
<p>Preview: <span id="preview"></span></p>
<script>
const caption = document.querySelector('#caption');
const preview = document.querySelector('#preview');
function render() { preview.textContent = caption.value; }
caption.addEventListener('input', render);
render();
</script>

The initial render matters: waiting for the first event would leave the starting preview blank. TextContent keeps the value as text. If application code later assigns caption.value, call render afterward; setting the property does not automatically dispatch an input event.

Reference: MDN input_event.

Separate a preview from an expensive side effect

A text preview can update immediately without saving to a server after every character. If another action is debounced, keep its timing and error state separate from the visible edit. For committed settings, change may better match the intended behavior, but event timing varies with the control type.

Input methods can produce composition events while a word is being assembled. A simple mirrored preview can show the current text, while a disruptive validation or submission action may need to respect composition state. Do not treat every intermediate edit as a final answer.

Test more than ordinary typing

Paste text, clear the field, use an input method, and assign a value from a reset or preset action. Confirm the initial and final previews match the control. Keep keyboard focus in the editor. Avoid making every keystroke a verbose live-region announcement when the user is already hearing their input.

Use output for calculated results and the status-message guide for concise save or completion feedback.
coverAlt: A caption field and its text preview show the same words, with input events updating the preview during editing.

title: Handle Nested Button Clicks with Scoped Event Delegation
description: Use closest to resolve clicks on button icons or labels, constrain the action to its component, and preserve native keyboard activation.
keyword: event delegation closest button nested icon
body:
A click on a button’s icon or inner span can have that child as its target. Delegated handling should resolve the owning button instead of assuming event.target is always the button itself. Keep the listener scoped to the relevant component.

Resolve the action from a stable container

<div id="tools">
  <button type="button" data-action="inspect"><span>Inspect card</span></button>
</div>
<p id="result"></p>
<script>
const tools = document.querySelector('#tools');
tools.addEventListener('click', event => {
  if (!(event.target instanceof Element)) return;
  const button = event.target.closest('button[data-action]');
  if (!button || !tools.contains(button) || button.disabled) return;
  if (button.dataset.action === 'inspect') {
    document.querySelector('#result').textContent = 'Inspection requested';
  }
});
</script>

The specimen responds to the button or its nested label. It only recognizes the explicit inspect action. Newly inserted matching buttons inside the same container can use the listener without attaching another handler to each instance.

Reference: MDN closest.

Preserve native behavior and component boundaries

Use a real button so keyboard activation already generates the expected click behavior. A div with a click listener needs much more work to behave like a button. Setting type="button" also prevents this helper action from submitting an enclosing form.

Closest searches the element and its ancestors. Check the resolved element belongs to the intended container, especially when components are nested. Shadow DOM can retarget events, so do not assume this small light-DOM pattern automatically reaches every internal action in a web component.

Exercise every activation surface

Click the label, click the button’s padding, activate with Enter and Space, and test a disabled state. Add a second button dynamically and confirm one response per activation. Remove or tear down the container’s listener when its owning component lifecycle requires it.

Compare buttons and navigation links, and use explicit button types so delegation does not conceal an unintended submission.
coverAlt: A click on a nested button label is resolved to its owning button and checked against the component container.

title: Fix Radio Choices That Deselect Another Component
description: Inspect radio names and form ownership when selecting one option clears an unrelated choice, and keep semantic fieldsets separate from grouping behavior.
keyword: radio buttons same name different fieldsets
body:
If choosing a layout clears a theme choice, inspect the radio names. Two fieldsets do not create independent radio groups by themselves. Within the same form and tree, radios sharing a nonempty name belong to the same selection group.

Give independent decisions independent names

<form>
  <fieldset>
    <legend>Theme</legend>
    <label><input type="radio" name="theme" value="light" checked> Light</label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="theme" value="dark"> Dark</label>
  </fieldset>
  <fieldset>
    <legend>Layout</legend>
    <label><input type="radio" name="layout" value="wide" checked> Wide</label>
    <label><input type="radio" name="layout" value="compact"> Compact</label>
  </fieldset>
</form>

The legends explain the decisions, while theme and layout separate their selection behavior and submitted keys. Change both names to the same string in an isolated fixture to reproduce the coupling. Distinct IDs alone would not fix it; IDs identify controls for labels and references, not radio-group membership.

Reference: MDN radio.

Inspect the actual form owner

Separate forms can have independent radio groups using the same name. A form attribute can associate a radio with a form outside its visual wrapper, so inspect input.form rather than guessing from nearby borders. Radios without a form owner can still group with other matching radios in the same tree.

Repeated components inside one form often need an instance-specific group name. Preserve the server’s expected data structure when choosing those names. A visual duplicate should not accidentally become a single shared decision.

Test selection and serialization together

Select a theme, then a layout, and verify that both remain checked. Navigate each group with the keyboard and inspect the resulting FormData. Add a second component instance to expose naming collisions that one isolated component cannot show.

Use fieldset and legend for clear group context, and the form-owner guide when controls are rendered outside the form they submit.
coverAlt: Theme and layout radio choices use separate names so a selected light theme and compact layout can remain chosen together.

title: Disable a Settings Group While Keeping Its Enable Control Usable
description: Use a disabled fieldset with an enable control in its first legend, inspect effective disabled state, and account for omitted form values.
body:
A disabled fieldset disables its descendant form controls, with an exception for controls inside its first legend. That exception can keep an enable checkbox usable while the settings it governs are unavailable.

Place the enable control in the first legend

<form>
  <fieldset id="export-settings" disabled>
    <legend><label><input id="enable-export" type="checkbox"> Enable export settings</label></legend>
    <label>File prefix <input name="prefix" value="review"></label>
  </fieldset>
</form>
<script>
const group = document.querySelector('#export-settings');
const enabled = document.querySelector('#enable-export');
function sync() { group.disabled = !enabled.checked; }
enabled.addEventListener('change', sync);
sync();
</script>

The enable checkbox stays available because it belongs to the first legend. The prefix field becomes available when the checkbox is checked. Keep the relationship understandable in the visible wording; a disabled panel without a reachable explanation or enable path can look broken.

Reference: MDN fieldset.

Inspect effective state rather than one attribute

A child input may have disabled equal to false on its own property while still being disabled by the ancestor fieldset. The :disabled selector reflects that effective state. Removing a disabled attribute from the child will not override the disabled ancestor.

Disabled fields are omitted from normal form data. Decide whether an unchecked enable control means “leave the saved settings unchanged” or “turn the feature off,” and encode that intent explicitly in the application. The server cannot infer the intended operation merely from a missing prefix field.

Check the enable path and submitted fields

Tab to the enable checkbox, toggle it, enter a prefix, and disable the group again. Inspect FormData in both states and confirm that the disappearing value is intentional. Ensure focus does not become stranded if the application disables the group while another control inside it is focused.

Compare disabled and readonly when values should remain available, and retain the group’s semantic caption when styling its border or spacing.
coverAlt: An enable checkbox in the first legend remains usable while a prefix field inside the disabled settings group is unavailable.

title: Let a Draft Action Skip Browser Validation Deliberately
description: Use formnovalidate on one submit button while keeping required checks for the final action, and preserve distinct server-side rules for drafts and completion.
body:
A form may allow incomplete drafts while requiring a title for final submission. Formnovalidate on the draft submit button skips the browser’s interactive constraint-validation step for that action. It does not erase field constraints or establish what the server should accept.

Keep the exception on the draft button

<form action="/reviews/complete" method="post">
  <label for="title">Review title</label>
  <input id="title" name="title" required>
  <button type="submit">Complete review</button>
  <button type="submit" formaction="/reviews/draft" formnovalidate>
    Save draft
  </button>
</form>

The endpoint paths are illustrative and need application handlers. Completing the empty form should be blocked by the required field. Saving a draft can proceed through native submission with that same field empty. The field remains invalid; this particular submission simply skips the interactive validation gate.

Reference: MDN button.

Keep browser policy and data policy distinct

A draft handler should deliberately support incomplete values while still checking permissions, data shape and any other requirements it needs. A completion handler should apply the full server-side rules. Client validation is useful feedback, not a substitute for those rules.

Putting novalidate on the whole form disables the browser gate for every submit action, which is a broader change. A JavaScript handler that always calls reportValidity and cancels invalid submissions can also undo the intended draft exception. Inspect how native and scripted submission interact.

Test empty, partial and complete records

Activate each button with an empty title, then repeat after typing. Press Enter from the field and verify which action is chosen; readers should not accidentally complete a review when they expect to save a draft. Confirm the request reaches the intended endpoint and the returned status explains what was saved.

See native form overrides for routing and submitter inspection when a shared handler needs to distinguish draft from completion.
coverAlt: An empty required title blocks the Complete action while a deliberate Save draft action skips the browser validation gate.

title: Understand What Dense Grid Packing Does to Visual Order
description: Compare sparse and dense auto-placement with mixed item spans, identify backfilled holes, and check keyboard order before using dense packing for controls.
keyword: css grid auto flow dense accessibility order
body:
Grid-auto-flow: dense lets a later small item fill a hole left earlier in the grid. It can improve packing while changing the visual order. The DOM and usual keyboard sequence do not automatically rearrange to follow that packed layout.

Create a visible one-cell hole

<div class="review-grid">
  <button class="wide">A</button>
  <button class="wide">B</button>
  <button>C</button>
</div>
<style>
.review-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
  grid-auto-flow: row dense;
  gap: 8px;
}
.review-grid .wide { grid-column: span 2; }
</style>

This deliberately interactive specimen exposes the ordering issue. A occupies two cells in the first row; B needs two cells and starts in the second row. Dense placement lets C return to the remaining first-row cell. Remove dense to compare the sparse placement without changing the item widths.

Reference: MDN grid-auto-flow.

Do not mistake packing for a semantic reorder

The markup still says A, B, C. Keyboard focus through the native buttons follows that sequence, which can jump from the first row to the second and back. A timeline, ordered process or action list often needs its visual arrangement to reinforce the same sequence.

Dense packing is also not a general masonry algorithm. It fills available grid holes according to grid placement rules; it does not simply stack every item under the shortest column. Inspect the actual track and span model.

Review realistic spans and content

Test several item counts, long labels and the narrowest supported column count. Tab through every control while watching its location. Keep sparse placement when packing makes the sequence confusing, and avoid repairing the visual order with positive tabindex values.

Use the visual and keyboard order checklist to assess meaning, and implicit row sizing when the newly created rows have unexpected heights.
coverAlt: A dense three-column grid puts later item C in the first-row hole beside A, while B remains on the second row and DOM order stays A B C.

title: Separate Flex Gaps from Margins in a Wrapping Tag Row
description: Use gap for spacing between flex items, padding for outer space, and inspect margins or distributed alignment when visible gaps exceed the declared value.
keyword: flex gap vs margin wrapped items spacing
body:
Gap adds spacing between flex items and lines, not padding around the container’s outer edge. A wrapping tag row becomes easier to reason about when the container owns internal gaps and padding, while each tag avoids an extra spacing margin.

Separate the three spacing responsibilities

.tag-row {
  display: flex;
  flex-wrap: wrap;
  gap: 16px 12px;
  padding: 16px;
  justify-content: flex-start;
}
.tag-row > .tag {
  margin: 0;
  flex: 0 0 100px;
}

For this row-direction specimen, 16px separates lines and 12px separates items within a line. Padding creates the outside breathing room. Fixed 100px items make the wrapping threshold easy to observe; production tags may instead size to their actual labels.

Reference: MDN gap.

Inspect all contributors to the visible distance

If the gap looks larger than 12px, check child margins, item dimensions and alignment such as space-between. Distributed free space can add separation beyond the declared gutter. Setting gap does not cancel old margins inherited from a previous spacing approach.

Wrapping flex lines distribute their items independently. The final short line does not inherit a column grid from the line above. If all tags must align in shared columns, consider whether Grid better expresses the requirement.

Test one item and a partial final line

Compare a single tag, a full row and a row that wraps by one item. Measure both an interior gap and the distance to the container edge. Remove an item and confirm no leftover end margin survives. Increase text size before deciding whether fixed item widths are appropriate for real labels.

Use spacing tokens to name the chosen distances and flex alignment guidance when line distribution adds space beyond the gutters.
coverAlt: A wrapping tag row separates outer padding, horizontal gaps and line gaps, with a partial final row aligned to the start.

title: Find the Missing Reference Behind a Percentage Height
description: Trace the containing block behind height percentages, compare an explicit parent height with content-driven sizing, and avoid clipping text to force a fit.
body:
A percentage height needs a resolvable reference. In ordinary block layout, a child with height: 100% does not automatically fill a parent whose height is determined by its contents. Inspect the containing block and layout mode before adding more percentage declarations.

Compare a definite height with an automatic one

.frame { height: 240px; background: #eef4f0; }
.frame > .sample { height: 50%; background: #b8d5fa; }
.frame.auto { height: auto; }

Put a small amount of text in sample and render two frames, adding auto to the second. In this simple block specimen, the first child is 120px tall. The second relies on content because the percentage does not resolve against an explicitly sized parent in the same way. Keep padding and borders out of the first comparison.

Reference: MDN height.

Follow the containing block rather than a visual wrapper

Absolute positioning, flex layout and grid sizing have additional rules for resolving dimensions. A broad statement that percentages never work without pixel heights would be wrong. Identify the actual layout context, then inspect the computed size and the authored rule together.

A minimum height is also not always interchangeable with a definite height for a descendant’s percentage calculation. If the intended behavior is stretching within a flex or grid area, express that through the layout model instead of constructing a chain of arbitrary 100% values.

Confirm the content can still grow

Replace the sample text with several paragraphs and enlarge the font. Check whether the fixed demonstration height now causes overflow. For production copy, a minimum size or content-driven layout may serve the design better than an exact height. For media, an aspect ratio can establish a useful box without depending on a parent’s content height.

Use the containing-block guide for positioned elements and the aspect-ratio guide for predictable media sizing.
coverAlt: A child at fifty percent of an explicit 240 pixel parent resolves to 120 pixels, while a content-sized parent needs a different sizing analysis.

title: Shrink a Grid Track Without Hiding Its Overflowing Content
description: Compare 1fr with minmax(0, 1fr), separate track sizing from content overflow, and choose wrapping or local scrolling for the item inside the track.
body:
A 1fr track can retain an automatic minimum influenced by its contents. Minmax(0, 1fr) gives the track an explicit zero minimum so it can fit the available space. That changes track sizing; it does not make long text or code fit inside by itself.

Give the content its own overflow policy

.inspector {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: 12rem minmax(0, 1fr);
  gap: 1rem;
}
.inspector pre { min-inline-size: 0; overflow: auto; }
@media (max-width: 40rem) {
  .inspector { grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr); }
}

Place navigation in the first column and a section containing a long preformatted code block in the second. Compare the flexible track with a plain 1fr while keeping the same code. Local scrolling preserves source lines; ordinary prose may instead need wrapping. The narrow-screen rule removes the fixed sidebar rather than pretending the desktop arrangement always fits.

Reference: MDN minmax.

Separate the track from the grid item

Track minimums and an item’s minimum size are related but distinct inspection points. Min-inline-size: 0 on a relevant item can allow that item to shrink, while minmax changes the grid track’s lower bound. Inspect both when a nested component still overflows after changing the parent grid.

Overflow: hidden on the entire page can conceal the symptom while cutting off content or focus indicators. Prefer a deliberate content policy at the specific element that needs it.

Measure both the grid and the code panel

Compare document width with viewport width, then inspect the code panel’s scrollWidth and clientWidth. A scrollable code block can be wider internally while the overall page remains within the viewport. Test a long URL, an image and a focused control as separate cases; their appropriate overflow behavior can differ.

Use the overflow investigation to locate the offender and the long-word guide for content that should wrap instead of scroll.
coverAlt: A fixed sidebar sits beside a flexible track with a zero minimum, while the code inside has its own local scrolling policy.

title: Align One Flex Item Without Changing the Whole Row
description: Use align-self for a single cross-axis exception, inspect auto margins and explicit sizes, and recheck the axis when flex-direction changes.
keyword: css align self not working auto margin
body:
Align-self overrides the group alignment for one flex or grid item. In flexbox it works on the cross axis, which depends on flex-direction. If the declaration seems ineffective, check the parent’s layout mode and the item’s cross-axis margins first.

Create a visible cross-axis exception

.toolbar {
  display: flex;
  align-items: center;
  min-block-size: 100px;
  gap: 1rem;
}
.toolbar .status { align-self: flex-start; }

Use a short status item beside a button in the toolbar. The default group aligns centrally while the status aligns at the cross-start edge. This row-direction specimen has enough height to make the difference visible. Without spare cross-axis room, several alignment values can appear to produce the same result.

Reference: MDN align-self.

Check competing sizing and margin rules

An auto cross-axis margin takes precedence over align-self for a flex item. Inspect margins before increasing selector specificity. Stretch also needs compatible sizing: an explicitly sized item does not simply ignore that size and fill every available dimension.

Changing the container to flex-direction: column changes the cross axis to the horizontal direction in ordinary horizontal writing. An override originally intended to move an item upward can then affect its horizontal placement. Grid alignment follows its own area-based model rather than flex lines.

Test the exception through responsive states

Switch the toolbar between its row and column arrangements, add a longer status and increase text size. Confirm that the exception still communicates the intended hierarchy. Avoid using alignment to simulate a different reading order when the markup sequence should change instead.

Record why the single item differs from its neighbors so a future component variant does not accidentally remove that distinction. Use item versus line alignment for the parent rules and auto margins when flexible separation is the actual requirement.
coverAlt: A tall flex row contains centered neighboring items and one status item aligned to the cross-start edge.

title: Audit Shorthand Resets Before Increasing CSS Specificity
description: Inspect the longhands written by a shorthand, identify omitted values that reset earlier styling, and make component variants change only their intended properties.
body:
A shorthand writes a collection of properties, including values you did not spell out. A later declaration can therefore erase part of a component’s styling without mentioning that part by name. Inspect the affected longhands before treating the problem as insufficient specificity.

Reproduce a disappearing background image

.panel {
  background-color: #eff5f1;
  background-image: linear-gradient(90deg, #dceaff, transparent);
  background-repeat: no-repeat;
}
.panel.quiet { background: #e8efe9; }
/* If only the color should change, use instead:
.panel.quiet { background-color: #e8efe9; }
*/

The quiet shorthand resets the background image rather than preserving it. The commented alternative changes only the color. Toggle the two approaches in DevTools and inspect background-image, not just the visible swatch next to background-color.

Reference: MDN shorthand properties.

Expand the relevant family of longhands

The same investigation applies beyond backgrounds. A font shorthand can reset style or variant details, and a border shorthand can replace widths, styles and colors established elsewhere. The exact reset behavior belongs to each shorthand’s definition, so avoid assuming that an omitted value means “leave unchanged.”

Rule order and cascade precedence still matter. A shorthand does not have inherently greater specificity than a longhand; it participates through the properties it sets. Adding !important can disguise the reset while creating a harder future override.

Review variants as explicit changes

List the properties a variant is meant to change, then compare the computed longhands before and after applying it. Check hover, focus and theme combinations where another shorthand may enter the cascade. A compact declaration is useful only when its full set of effects matches the component’s intent.

Keep the final fix narrow when only one detail should change, or write the complete shorthand intentionally when replacing the whole treatment. See the cascade workflow and background-layer guide for tracing the winning declarations.
coverAlt: A background shorthand clears the image layer, while a background-color-only variant preserves the image and changes just the base color.

title: Group Native Disclosures So Only One Opens at a Time
description: Use the details name attribute for exclusive disclosure groups, keep group names scoped to the intended set, and test whether exclusivity helps readers compare content.
body:
Details elements with the same name can form an exclusive group: opening one closes another open member. Use this native behavior when readers should view one section at a time. Leave disclosures independent when comparing several sections side by side is more useful.

Give the intended pair one group name

<details name="export-help">
  <summary>Image export</summary>
  <p>Choose dimensions appropriate to the intended display.</p>
</details>
<details name="export-help">
  <summary>Token export</summary>
  <p>Keep token names and units consistent with the receiving project.</p>
</details>

The shared name supplies the grouping behavior in supporting browsers; the summary remains the native control. Opening either disclosure should close the other, and closing the active one can leave both closed. This is not a requirement that exactly one panel must always remain open.

Reference: MDN details.

Avoid accidental groups across repeated components

Members do not need to sit next to each other to share a name. Reusing export-help in several independent widgets can connect sections that were meant to operate separately. Generate distinct group names for unrelated component instances.

Do not set multiple open attributes and rely on all panels starting expanded within the exclusive group. Also remember that open="false" still means the Boolean open attribute is present; remove it to close the element.

Test the native control before adding scripting

Open each summary with the pointer and keyboard, then test a repeated widget elsewhere on the page. Check that content remains usable where grouping support differs, even if several sections can stay open. Avoid layering a custom click handler that fights the browser’s own state changes.

Review whether automatically closing earlier content interrupts a comparison task. Use basic disclosure guidance for the native pattern, or the custom accordion guide when requirements genuinely need a different implementation.
coverAlt: Two native disclosures share a group name; the image export section is open and the token export section is closed.

title: Review Autofocus Before Moving a Reader Past Page Context
description: Check when autofocus is appropriate, compare page entry with a deliberately opened dialog, and verify keyboard, scrolling and mobile-keyboard behavior.
body:
Autofocus can save a step when entering text is the clear immediate task. It can also move readers past the page heading, trigger scrolling or display a mobile keyboard before the surrounding context has been understood. Treat it as an interaction decision, not a default form decoration.

Compare an intentional dialog entry point

<button id="open-search" type="button">Open guide search</button>
<dialog id="search-dialog">
  <form method="dialog">
    <label for="guide-query">Search guides</label>
    <input id="guide-query" autofocus>
    <button>Close</button>
  </form>
</dialog>
<script>
const dialog = document.querySelector('#search-dialog');
document.querySelector('#open-search').addEventListener('click', () => dialog.showModal());
</script>

This specimen opens a search-labeled field only after the reader chooses the dialog action. It demonstrates focus placement, not a working search service. The native dialog has a close path, and the input has a persistent label. An autofocus field on initial page load presents a different context.

Reference: MDN autofocus.

Check competing focus instructions

Use only one autofocus candidate within the relevant document, dialog or popover. An attribute value of false does not disable this Boolean attribute; remove it instead. Scripts that call focus can introduce another competing move, so inspect both markup and event handlers when focus seems to jump twice.

Autofocus does not guarantee the same behavior in every navigation situation. Fragment navigation and browser decisions can affect the outcome. Do not build an essential workflow that fails whenever automatic focus does not occur.

Review the first information a reader encounters

Load the page from its ordinary URL and from an anchor link. Open and close the dialog with the keyboard, and inspect where focus returns. On a touch device, check whether the keyboard obscures useful instructions. Listen to the initial announcement with the assistive technology being supported.

Use the dialog focus checklist for entry and exit, and controlled focus movement when a script needs a deliberate scrolling policy.
coverAlt: An explicit Open search action leads to a dialog field with a visible focus outline, distinguishing chosen entry from page-load focus movement.

title: Remove an Underline at Its Source Instead of Fighting a Child
description: Trace text-decoration drawn by an ancestor, understand why a child’s none declaration cannot erase it, and preserve a clear link affordance when changing markup.
keyword: text decoration none child underline parent
body:
A child can have text-decoration: none and still appear underlined when the decoration is drawn by an ancestor. This is decoration propagation, not ordinary inheritance of the child’s text-decoration value. Inspect where the underline starts before increasing specificity on the child.

Use a minimal ancestor-and-child comparison

<p class="decorated">Review <span>this label</span> carefully.</p>
<style>
.decorated { text-decoration: underline; }
.decorated span { text-decoration: none; }
</style>

The span’s words remain within the ancestor’s decorated text. Looking only at the span’s computed text-decoration can therefore mislead an inspection. Toggle the declaration on decorated to identify the owner of the visible line. Keep the same markup while isolating that one change.

Reference: MDN text-decoration.

Move the decoration to the intended text range

If only certain words should have the line, apply it to those text ranges rather than to a wrapper spanning everything. Do not use stronger selectors on the child to fight a decoration drawn elsewhere. Changes to display or formatting context can alter rendering, but they can also introduce wrapping and alignment differences.

For a navigation link, removing the underline may remove a useful affordance. Decide how the entire clickable range remains recognizable instead of styling a child to look unrelated to its parent link.

Compare appearance with computed evidence

Inspect the ancestor and descendant in DevTools, noting which node owns the declaration. Add a line break by narrowing the container and check where the decoration continues. Review hover and focus states separately because another rule may introduce a second decoration.

Document the relationship in the component handoff so the next reviewer does not interpret a computed none as proof that no line can be visible. Use the resolved-style guide for evidence and the underline styling guide for a readable final treatment.
coverAlt: A line drawn by an ancestor continues through a child word even though the child has text-decoration none.

title: Distinguish Zero from Letter O with a Supported Font Feature
description: Use slashed-zero for identifiers when the font supports it, compare real glyphs and fallback behavior, and preserve the original characters when copying.
keyword: css font variant numeric slashed zero
body:
Slashed-zero asks a supporting font to use an alternate zero glyph. It can help distinguish the digit 0 from the letter O in identifiers, but it does not replace the underlying character or manufacture a feature missing from the font.

Compare the same identifier in two specimens

.identifier { font-variant-numeric: slashed-zero; }
.identifier.baseline { font-variant-numeric: normal; }

Use a clearly labeled example string such as REVIEW-0O10 in both elements. Keep the font family, weight and size identical. Then compare the actual rendered zero and letter O. The short rule intentionally leaves font selection to the project; first confirm the loaded font provides a suitable alternate.

Reference: MDN font-variant-numeric.

Keep numeric features independent

Slashed-zero and tabular-nums solve different problems. The first changes the zero’s shape; the second requests equal-width figures for alignment. They can be combined when supported, but one does not imply the other. A monospace family can still have a zero design that is difficult to distinguish at a small size.

A CSS declaration appearing in the Styles panel does not prove the requested glyph exists in the active font. Check the rendered font and compare after loading completes. A fallback face can change the result even while the property remains present.

Test recognition and copying in context

Review mixed letters and numbers at the size used in the interface, including a narrow mobile layout. Copy the identifier into a plain-text editor and confirm the original zeros remain zeros. Do not replace 0 with a visually similar Unicode character just to imitate the slashed shape; that would change the identifier’s value.

Consider a copy control or clearer grouping for long codes, while preserving a readable selectable value. Use font inspection to verify the active face and tabular numerals when numeric column alignment is also required.
coverAlt: Schematic glyphs distinguish a slashed digit zero from a letter O, with a reminder that the real font must support the alternate.

title: Review Text Shadows at the Actual Reading Size
description: Separate glyph shadows from box shadows, inspect offsets and blur one value at a time, and avoid relying on a glow to make a variable background readable.
keyword: css text shadow readability offset blur
body:
Text-shadow follows the glyphs rather than the element’s rectangular box. A restrained shadow can support a deliberate visual treatment, but a blurred halo can also make small labels harder to read. Judge it at the actual display size and background.

Use one shadow before stacking several

.hero-label {
  color: #fff;
  background-color: #203b30;
  padding: .5em;
  text-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / .35);
}

The specimen gives white text a known dark surface before adding a small shadow. Compare against text-shadow: none, then change the vertical offset and blur separately. Keep font weight and size fixed so the shadow’s contribution is visible. These values are an inspection starting point, not a universal recipe.

Reference: MDN text-shadow.

Inspect the correct shadow model

Text-shadow uses horizontal offset, vertical offset, optional blur and color. It does not accept the spread or inset controls used by box-shadow. Comma-separated shadows can stack several effects, with the first listed drawn in front. An inherited text shadow can also reach labels that were never intended to have a glow.

Large blur does not establish reliable readability over every part of a photograph. Compare the composited text against the lightest and darkest expected background regions, and use a stable surface or overlay when needed.

Check small text and alternate rendering

Inspect the real text at normal zoom, then enlarged. Compare a short heading with a dense line of secondary copy; an effect suitable for one may damage the other. Review themes and forced-colors behavior without assuming the decorative shadow will survive unchanged.

Remove inherited shadows from controls that need crisp edges, and verify that any decorative treatment still leaves the content readable. Use the box-shadow guide for rectangular surfaces and the contrast workflow for the final text/background combination.
coverAlt: A text shadow specimen places white lettering over a dark stable surface and identifies offset, blur and alpha as separate review controls.

title: Keep Gradient Text Readable When Its Effect Is Unavailable
description: Apply background-clip text as an enhancement, retain a solid color path, and check forced colors, printing and contrast across the full gradient.
keyword: background clip text gradient fallback color
body:
Gradient text usually combines a clipped background with transparent foreground color. If the background effect is unavailable or suppressed, that transparent text can disappear. Start with a readable solid color and add the effect only within a deliberate enhancement rule.

Keep the plain-text path explicit

.gradient-title { color: #174e37; }
@supports (background-clip: text) {
  .gradient-title {
    background-color: #174e37;
    background-image: linear-gradient(90deg, #174e37, #1756a0);
    background-clip: text;
    color: transparent;
  }
}
@media print, (forced-colors: active) {
  .gradient-title { background: none; color: CanvasText; }
}

Test this specimen on the intended light surface. The support query gates the effect, and the solid background color provides a base within the clipping treatment. The later media rule restores visible foreground text when the decorative background is deliberately removed.

Reference: MDN background-clip.

Inspect every color behind the letterforms

A gradient can have a readable endpoint and an unreadable middle. Check the entire text range and the actual page background, including where the heading wraps. A changed width can move a different gradient region under a word even when the CSS colors remain identical.

Be cautious when mixing prefixed text-fill properties with this pattern: a separate transparent fill declaration can survive a color reset. Inspect every property that affects the glyph’s paint before concluding the fallback is complete.

Review with the decoration removed

Disable the enhancement, emulate forced colors and inspect print preview. Confirm the heading remains present, selectable and meaningful without the gradient. Try a long title and increased text size. Keep ordinary text content in HTML instead of replacing the heading with an image solely to achieve the effect.

Use the forced-colors checklist for system colors and the gradient-stop guide to inspect the color progression itself.
coverAlt: A plain solid heading and a gradient-enhanced heading share the same readable words, with a separate forced-colors and print fallback.

title: Pair a Conic Gradient Chart with Its Actual Values
description: Use conic-gradient for an illustrative proportion graphic, calculate stops from the data, and keep labels and values available outside the CSS background.
keyword: css conic gradient pie chart accessible labels
body:
A conic gradient can draw proportion segments around a center, but a CSS background does not expose the underlying data as readable content. Keep the values and labels in HTML, and treat the colored shape as a supporting view of the same information.

Build a clearly labeled example dataset

<figure>
  <div class="split" aria-hidden="true"></div>
  <figcaption>Illustrative review allocation</figcaption>
</figure>
<ul><li>Layout: 50%</li><li>Typography: 30%</li><li>Color: 20%</li></ul>
<style>
.split {
  width: 10rem; aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 50%;
  background: conic-gradient(#174f99 0 50%, #78b99a 50% 80%, #e4be65 80% 100%);
}
</style>

The values are an invented arithmetic specimen, not measurements of a Penta AI review. The cumulative stops are 50%, 80% and 100%. Repeating a boundary at the next color creates a hard transition rather than a blended region between categories.

Reference: MDN conic-gradient.

Keep the graphic and text from drifting apart

For real data, derive both the text and cumulative stops from the same validated values. Define what should happen with zero totals, missing categories or rounding that does not sum neatly to 100. Do not silently alter a number just to make the final segment look tidy.

Color alone should not be the only way to identify a category. A nearby text list makes exact values available without visual angle estimation. Consider a labeled bar chart or table when comparison is easier in that form.

Review without the circular graphic

Disable background images and read the remaining content. Confirm the title identifies what the percentages describe and the values remain complete. Check that the visible palette is distinguishable on the intended surface, then inspect a narrow layout and enlarged text.

Use the figure-caption guide for the relationship between visual and explanation, and the contrast review for labels and any meaningful graphical boundaries.
coverAlt: An explicitly illustrative allocation chart shows Layout 50 percent, Typography 30 percent and Color 20 percent beside the corresponding segments.

title: Read Data Attributes as Strings When Inspecting State
description: Parse data attribute values explicitly, understand dash-to-camelCase names, and avoid treating the string false as a Boolean false in component logic.
body:
Dataset exposes data-* values as strings. A component with data-expanded="false" does not give JavaScript a Boolean false; it gives a nonempty string. A truthiness check can therefore reverse the state you meant to inspect.

Parse the value you actually expect

<div id="review-panel" data-expanded="false" data-item-count="3"></div>
<script>
const panel = document.querySelector('#review-panel');
const expanded = panel.dataset.expanded === 'true';
const count = Number(panel.dataset.itemCount);
console.log(expanded); // false
console.log(count); // 3
</script>

The HTML name data-item-count becomes dataset.itemCount. The strict comparison defines the accepted true representation. Numeric conversion still needs validation if the value may be missing, empty or malformed; Number alone is not a complete data contract.

Reference: MDN dataset.

Distinguish missing values from serialized values

Assigning to a dataset property writes a string representation back to the attribute. Assigning false produces "false" rather than removing the attribute. Use delete panel.dataset.expanded when the attribute should be absent, and decide whether absence means default, unknown or another explicit state.

Custom data attributes do not automatically communicate an expanded or pressed state to assistive technology. Keep native behavior or the appropriate ARIA state synchronized through the application’s actual state model instead of using data attributes as a substitute.

Test unexpected input representations

Inspect false, true, an empty attribute and a missing attribute. Try a malformed numeric count and check that the interface does not display NaN or silently accept it. If both CSS and JavaScript read the state, document the exact allowed strings so the selectors and logic agree.

Use the delegated-action example for a bounded data-action vocabulary and the expanded-state guide when the value represents an actual disclosure control.
coverAlt: The data-expanded attribute contains the string false, and an explicit comparison with true produces the Boolean false.

title: Let Unknown User Text Choose Its Base Direction
description: Use dir auto for text whose direction is not known in advance, inspect punctuation and leading characters, and keep language identification separate from direction.
keyword: html dir auto user generated text direction
body:
Use dir="auto" for user text whose base direction is not known in advance. The browser generally determines direction from the first strong directional character. It does not translate the content or identify its language for you.

Compare two standalone review notes

<p dir="auto">Review the spacing beside the label.</p>
<p dir="auto" lang="ar">مراجعة التصميم</p>
<style>
[dir="auto"] { text-align: start; }
</style>

The English note begins with left-to-right text, and the Arabic specimen begins with right-to-left text. Start alignment follows the resolved direction. The known Arabic specimen has lang="ar" separately; an application should not guess a language merely because direction resolves to right-to-left.

Reference: MDN dir.

Test the characters that establish direction

Leading punctuation or digits may not determine the base direction, so inspect the first strong character rather than only the first visible symbol. A Latin identifier at the start of an otherwise right-to-left note can affect the result. Use explicit direction when the application already knows the correct value.
