For a small unknown-direction name embedded inside a larger sentence, bdi can be the more appropriate isolation pattern. A whole paragraph and an inline fragment do not always need the same wrapper or alignment policy.

Review mixed text without rearranging the source

Try a note beginning with a number, one beginning with an English product identifier and one containing punctuation near a right-to-left phrase. Copy the text to a plain editor and confirm that the logical source order remains correct. Do not manually reverse characters to imitate the desired visual order.

Inspect a live input or textarea separately if users edit the text; caret movement and selection also matter. Compare the bdi guide for inline isolation and language markup for pronunciation and language-specific behavior.
coverAlt: Two text-direction diagrams begin at opposite edges, with a note that automatic direction follows strong text characters rather than identifying a language.

title: Choose Plain-Text Editing Deliberately with contenteditable
description: Use plaintext-only for a custom editable surface, keep its accessible name and focus visible, and account for submission and paste behavior beyond the attribute.
body:
Contenteditable="plaintext-only" enables editing without retaining rich text formatting from the editing interaction in supporting browsers. It can suit a custom text surface, but it does not turn a div into a native form field. For an ordinary multiline form value, textarea is often the simpler starting point.

Name the editable surface explicitly

<p id="notes-label">Review notes</p>
<div contenteditable="plaintext-only" role="textbox"
     aria-multiline="true" aria-labelledby="notes-label"
     class="notes-editor"></div>
<style>
.notes-editor { min-block-size: 5rem; padding: .75rem; border: 1px solid; }
.notes-editor:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #174f99; outline-offset: 3px; }
</style>

The role and label explain the custom surface to accessibility APIs; the visible outline identifies focus. The example deliberately does not claim to implement saving, form validation or a complete editor. Those behaviors need explicit application design.

Reference: MDN contenteditable.

Account for what native controls normally provide

A contenteditable div is not automatically serialized as a named form value. Decide how to read, normalize and save its text, including line breaks. Do not treat a name attribute added to the div as equivalent to a textarea’s name.

Contenteditable is enumerated, with meaningful values including false and plaintext-only. Missing or invalid values can inherit editability from an ancestor. The plain-text editing mode is also not a general sanitizer for HTML that other application code inserts.

Test real editing paths and unsupported behavior

Type several lines, paste formatted text, undo, select a range and use an input method. Inspect both the visible result and stored text. Test the browsers and assistive technology your interface supports, and keep a usable fallback where the desired editing mode is unavailable.

Compare the effort with a labeled textarea before committing to a custom editor. Use persistent labeling and the caret and selection guide to review the editing experience itself.
coverAlt: A labeled plain-text notes editor has a visible focus boundary and a reminder that saving, validation and form submission need deliberate implementation.

title: Wait for Font Loading Before Measuring a Text Specimen
description: Use document.fonts.ready before a controlled measurement, verify the actual rendered face, and avoid treating one resolved promise as permanent page stability.
keyword: document fonts ready measure text width
body:
Font loading can change line breaks and element dimensions after an initial measurement. Await document.fonts.ready before measuring a prepared text specimen, then verify which font actually rendered. A settled loading phase does not prove that the intended font loaded successfully.

Measure the existing specimen after fonts settle

async function measureLabel() {
  const label = document.querySelector('.measurement-label');
  if (!label) return;
  await document.fonts.ready;
  const rect = label.getBoundingClientRect();
  console.table({ width: rect.width, height: rect.height,
    font: getComputedStyle(label).fontFamily });
}
measureLabel();

Place the target text and its styles in the document before running the function. The result measures the rendered box, not a font’s abstract glyph advance. The computed family list is useful context, but the browser’s rendered-font inspection is needed to confirm which actual face supplied the glyphs.

Reference: MDN ready.

Keep the measurement conditions controlled

Record viewport size, text, font weight, size, spacing and any transform. A changed container width can alter wrapping independently of font loading. Failed font requests may leave fallback text after the readiness promise settles, so inspect request errors and the rendered face rather than treating readiness as success evidence.

Later DOM or style changes can introduce new font needs. Awaiting one readiness promise does not freeze the page or guarantee that a subsequently inserted component uses the same settled conditions.

Compare a cold load with a repeat visit

Capture the same specimen with the font uncached and then cached. Inspect dimensions after the relevant readiness point in both runs, and deliberately block the font to document fallback behavior. A measurement report should state those conditions rather than claiming an unexplained width difference is a typography defect.

Use the font-loading checklist for failures and the bounds-versus-layout measurement guide when transforms or fractional geometry affect the numbers.
coverAlt: A measurement workflow prepares the specimen, waits for document fonts readiness and then measures the box while separately verifying the rendered font.

title: Decode a Replacement Image Before Swapping the Preview
description: Keep the previous preview while a new image decodes, handle failed requests, and guard against an older selection replacing a newer one.
keyword: image decode promise replace preview race condition
body:
Image.decode returns a promise that resolves when image data is ready for use. For a preview switcher, decode the replacement before inserting it so the current preview can remain visible while loading. Also guard against an older request finishing after a newer choice.

Only the newest request may replace the preview

let previewVersion = 0;
async function updatePreview(src, alt) {
  const version = ++previewVersion;
  const image = new Image();
  image.alt = alt;
  image.src = src;
  try {
    await image.decode();
    if (version !== previewVersion) return;
    document.querySelector('#preview').replaceChildren(image);
    document.querySelector('#preview-status').textContent = 'Preview updated';
  } catch {
    if (version === previewVersion) {
      document.querySelector('#preview-status').textContent = 'Could not load the selected preview';
    }
  }
}

Provide the preview container, a suitable status region and real image URLs before calling this function. Pass alt text matching the selected image’s purpose. The version check suppresses stale completions; it does not cancel their network requests.

Reference: MDN decode.

Preserve layout and failure context

Reserve an appropriate preview area and style inserted images to fit it. Decoding alone does not prevent layout shifts from unexpected image dimensions. On failure, this specimen keeps the old preview visible and reports that the selected replacement did not load, so the retained image is not mistaken for a successful update.

A request failure, corrupt image or changed source can reject decoding. Do not swallow every rejection and then announce success. For responsive images, configure the relevant source selection before decoding the image you intend to insert.

Test rapid choices and a broken image

Choose two previews quickly while delaying the first response. Confirm that the first cannot overwrite the second. Request an invalid image and verify the old preview remains with a clear message. Check keyboard focus stays on the initiating control and that announcements do not repeat unnecessarily.

Use selected-source inspection and responsive-image setup when the displayed file differs from the one expected.
coverAlt: An existing preview stays visible while a replacement decodes, and a version check allows only the latest selection to replace it.

title: Base a Scripted Animation on Elapsed Time, Not Frame Count
description: Use the requestAnimationFrame timestamp for consistent duration, stop the loop at completion, and provide a reduced-motion path and cleanup function.
body:
Adding a fixed number of pixels on every animation frame ties speed to the display’s refresh rate. Calculate progress from the requestAnimationFrame timestamp instead, so a finite movement uses elapsed time rather than an assumed number of callbacks.

Run one bounded movement

function startSlide(dot) {
  if (matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches) {
    dot.style.transform = 'translateX(120px)';
    return () => {};
  }
  let start, frameId;
  function frame(now) {
    if (start === undefined) start = now;
    const progress = Math.min((now - start) / 800, 1);
    dot.style.transform = `translateX(${120 * progress}px)`;
    if (progress < 1) frameId = requestAnimationFrame(frame);
  }
  frameId = requestAnimationFrame(frame);
  return () => cancelAnimationFrame(frameId);
}

Call this with a real element inside a track large enough for the movement. Save the returned cleanup function and call it before removing the component or starting a replacement loop. The specimen travels 120px over 800ms of elapsed callback time and stops requesting frames at completion.

Reference: MDN requestAnimationFrame.

Define what happens while the page is hidden

Browsers commonly pause animation-frame callbacks in background tabs. When callbacks resume, the elapsed timestamp can jump forward. This formula advances to the corresponding progress, potentially finishing immediately. A timer-like experience that must pause while hidden needs a different, explicit elapsed-time policy.

The initial reduced-motion check avoids the movement in that state. If the animation is long-lived or restartable, also respond to preference changes rather than assuming the initial value remains permanent.

Review duration and interruption separately

Compare the movement on different refresh-rate displays where available. Interrupt it by removing the component, restart it and switch tabs during playback. Confirm there is only one active loop and that completion leaves a meaningful static state.

Use the motion review to decide whether movement is needed, and media-query change listeners to keep scripted behavior synchronized with preferences.
coverAlt: An 800 millisecond timeline maps elapsed progress from zero to 120 pixels, independent of an assumed number of animation frames.

title: Interpret Intersection Ratios Without Calling Them Visibility Proof
description: Use IntersectionObserver thresholds for geometric intersection checks, inspect the chosen root, and distinguish partial overlap from actual readable visibility.
body:
IntersectionObserver reports geometric intersection between a target and a root region. An intersection ratio is not proof that a reader saw or read the content. Use it for a clearly defined layout or loading question, and identify the root and thresholds in the evidence.

Log a few meaningful thresholds

const target = document.querySelector('.review-section');
const observer = new IntersectionObserver(entries => {
  console.table(entries.map(entry => ({
    intersecting: entry.isIntersecting,
    ratio: entry.intersectionRatio,
    time: entry.time
  })));
}, { root: null, threshold: [0, 0.5, 1] });
if (target) observer.observe(target);
// End the inspection with observer.disconnect();

Root null uses the document viewport. The chosen thresholds expose entry, half-area intersection and full intersection boundaries, with an initial notification after observation. They do not request a callback for every pixel of movement. Keep the target’s dimensions known when interpreting the ratio.

Reference: MDN Intersection Observer API.

Choose the root that matches the scrolling task

For a component inside a scrolling panel, an explicit ancestor root may answer the intended question better than the viewport alone. Root margins can expand or shrink the effective region, so record them if they are used. A target taller than the available root may never reach a ratio of one.

The ordinary intersection calculation does not establish readability or absence of occlusion by every overlay. Opacity, covering content and the user’s attention are separate concerns. Avoid labeling this diagnostic as a verified view or impression without a suitable measurement definition.

Test boundaries and cleanup

Scroll the target in slowly, resize the root, and place it in a nested scrolling panel. Compare the logged ratios with the expected geometry. Disconnect when the diagnostic ends, and avoid using the callback to repeatedly change layout in a way that causes unnecessary new threshold crossings.

Use content-visibility for rendering decisions and the accessibility-tree guide for a different kind of exposure; neither is established by intersection alone.
coverAlt: A target crosses a viewport boundary with half its area inside, illustrating geometric intersection rather than proof that a reader saw the content.

title: List a Component’s Animations Before Pausing Them
description: Inspect getAnimations with a deliberate subtree scope, identify current play states and timing, and avoid assuming the returned list covers every moving image or script.
body:
GetAnimations returns Animation objects affecting an element, including CSS animations, CSS transitions and Web Animations. With subtree enabled, it can include descendants too. Start with a scoped inventory before pausing or canceling effects across a whole page.

Inspect the component’s current animation objects

const component = document.querySelector('.review-component');
const animations = component ? component.getAnimations({ subtree: true }) : [];
console.table(animations.map(animation => ({
  id: animation.id,
  state: animation.playState,
  currentTime: animation.currentTime,
  duration: animation.effect?.getComputedTiming().duration
})));

The returned array describes the objects found at this point in the investigation. Query again after triggering a transition or creating another effect. An empty ID is possible; it is not evidence that the animation is invalid. Inspect the target and source rule when the row needs a more useful label.

Reference: MDN getAnimations.

Distinguish pausing from removing an effect

Pause retains an animation’s current position. Cancel removes its effect and resets its playback state, which can visibly expose the underlying style. Do not use cancellation as an interchangeable pause button in a design review.

The inventory does not represent every source of motion. Video, animated image files and arbitrary requestAnimationFrame drawing loops are not automatically included as Animation objects. If motion continues after pausing this list, identify its implementation before assuming the API failed.

Review the exact interaction that creates motion

Capture the list before and after hovering, expanding or dismissing the component. Include pseudo-element effects where relevant. If you temporarily pause objects, record what you changed and restore only the intended playback states; blindly playing everything can resume effects that were already paused for a reason.

Use DevTools animation inspection for visual timing analysis and play-state guidance for a CSS animation’s own pause control.
coverAlt: A component-scoped animation inventory lists state, current time and duration, with a distinction between pausing and canceling effects.

title: Reserve Scroll-Target Clearance on the Scrolling Container
description: Use scroll-padding-top for a shared scrollport inset, distinguish it from target scroll margins and ordinary padding, and check sticky toolbars at different sizes.
keyword: scroll padding top container sticky header
body:
Scroll-padding-top defines an inset in a scrolling container’s preferred viewing region for targeted scrolling. It can reserve clearance for a sticky toolbar shared by many targets. It does not add ordinary layout padding above the content.

Apply the inset to the element that actually scrolls

.review-scroll {
  block-size: 240px;
  overflow: auto;
  scroll-padding-top: 56px;
}
.review-scroll .toolbar {
  position: sticky;
  top: 0;
  block-size: 40px;
  background: #fff;
}

Put the toolbar and several section headings inside review-scroll, then target a middle heading with scrollIntoView({block: "start"}). The specimen leaves 40px for the toolbar plus 16px of breathing room. A declaration on a nearby wrapper that never scrolls will not establish the same scrollport policy.

Reference: MDN scroll-padding-top.

Keep container and target offsets distinct

Scroll padding belongs to the scrolling container; scroll margin belongs to a target. They can interact, so inspect both before doubling an offset to fix a remaining overlap. Ordinary padding affects layout and scrollable content dimensions, which is a different operation.

The requested alignment is limited by the available scroll range. A target near the beginning or end may not reach the exact desired position if the container cannot scroll farther. Also avoid treating scroll padding as a universal guarantee for every browser’s focus-scrolling behavior.

Test toolbar growth and nested scrolling

Increase text size until the toolbar wraps, then recheck the inset. Use an actual size-driven value or revise the layout if a fixed 56px no longer describes the covered region. Test anchor navigation, scripted scrolling and keyboard movement separately, including a nested panel inside the main page.

Use the target-margin guide for exceptions on individual headings and scrollIntoView alignment for the requested scrolling behavior.
coverAlt: A scrolling panel reserves a top region for a 40 pixel toolbar plus 16 pixels of clearance before the targeted heading.

title: Find the Explicit Grid Edge Behind a Negative Line Number
description: Trace grid-column: 1 / -1 to the explicit grid, compare implicit columns, and inspect the overlay before changing a full-width item’s placement.
body:
In CSS Grid, a negative line number counts backward from the explicit grid’s end. A declaration such as grid-column: 1 / -1 does not promise to include every implicit column that another item creates. Inspect the template and placement together when a supposed full-width heading stops early.

Create an extra column deliberately

.review-grid {
  display: grid;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 100px);
  grid-auto-columns: 80px;
  gap: 12px;
}
.review-grid .heading { grid-column: 1 / -1; }
.review-grid .outside { grid-column: 4; }

Place a heading and a separate outside item inside review-grid. The three declared columns end at line 4, also addressed as -1. The outside item starts there and creates another column. The heading spans the three explicit columns, while the new implicit column sits beyond its end.

Reference: MDN CSS grid negative line numbers.

Check whether the extra track belongs in the design

Open the grid overlay and count the declared tracks before editing the heading. If the fourth column is intentional, declare a four-column template or use placement that explicitly covers it. If it comes from an incorrect item assignment, fix that assignment instead of stretching every other item to accommodate the mistake.

Negative numbering is tied to the explicit grid, not the last visible card. Empty explicit tracks still matter. Responsive templates can change the number of explicit tracks while preserving the meaning of their final line.

Test the placement across template changes

Remove the outside declaration, then restore it and compare the overlay. Change the template to two columns and confirm which edge -1 now identifies. Record the template, item placement and writing direction when handing off the bug; a screenshot alone hides why the extra space exists.

Use a deliberate small specimen before applying the correction to a dashboard with many spans. Avoid assuming that changing auto-flow will redefine the explicit grid boundary.

Review explicit and implicit track sizing. Plan responsive grid areas.
coverAlt: Three blue explicit grid columns end at line minus one, while a fourth green implicit column lies beyond the heading span.

title: Resolve Percentage Gaps Against the Right Container Size
description: Measure percentage gaps against a definite content box, then test automatic sizing and compare grid and flex behavior before choosing a spacing token.
body:
A percentage gap refers to the corresponding dimension of the container’s content box. The difficult case is a dimension that depends on its contents: the gap and container size can depend on each other. Grid and flex layout do not resolve every cyclic percentage case the same way.

Start with a definite inline size

.gap-demo {
  display: grid;
  inline-size: 400px;
  grid-template-columns: repeat(2, minmax(0, 1fr));
  column-gap: 10%;
}
.gap-demo > div { min-block-size: 60px; }

Two items in this horizontal-writing specimen leave a 40px column gap. The remaining 360px is shared between the tracks, making each 180px wide. Padding is outside the content-box reference in this initial example; changing box-sizing or the actual content width changes the arithmetic.

Reference: MDN CSS percentage gap sizing.

Isolate cyclic sizing instead of generalizing from one layout

Next try an automatically sized block direction with a percentage row gap and fixed-height children. In grid, a cyclic percentage gap can contribute zero during intrinsic sizing and still produce a gap during layout, allowing content to overflow the resulting box. Flex percentage gaps can resolve differently when the relevant size is indefinite.

Do not transfer a successful grid result directly to a column flex container. Keep the layout mode, gap direction and definite or indefinite dimension in the reproduction. A computed percentage string alone does not tell you the visible distance.

Choose a gap that communicates the spacing intent

Measure adjacent item rectangles after layout and compare their separation with the container’s content dimensions. Repeat with longer text, a narrow viewport and an explicit size removed. This distinguishes a percentage-resolution problem from distributed alignment adding extra space.

If the design needs a stable spacing step rather than a container-relative distance, use a length token such as 1rem. Percentage spacing should be intentional and reviewed at the smallest and largest supported container sizes.

Separate gaps from margins. Build a useful spacing scale.
coverAlt: A 400 pixel content box contains two 180 pixel tracks separated by a 40 pixel gap, illustrating a ten percent column gap.

title: Calculate an Image Crop Offset from object-position
description: Work through object-position percentage math using a known image and box, identify the axis that can move, and verify the crop at responsive sizes.
body:
Object-position percentages align a point in the fitted image with the same percentage point in its box. They are not a simple instruction to move the image that percentage of its own width. Calculate the remaining space after object-fit has scaled the content.

Use a specimen with known geometry

.crop-demo {
  display: block;
  width: 200px;
  height: 200px;
  object-fit: cover;
  object-position: 25% 50%;
}

Use a 400-by-200 image with labeled left and right edges. Cover keeps this image at 400 by 200 inside the 200px square. The horizontal remaining space is 200 minus 400, or -200px. Multiplying by 25% gives a -50px offset: the leftmost 50px of image content is cropped. Vertical remaining space is zero, so changing the second percentage has no visible effect in this specimen.

Reference: MDN object-position percentage calculation.

Distinguish a position value from a focal coordinate

A recorded subject coordinate is not automatically the object-position value that centers that subject in every crop. The fitted dimensions and box proportions also matter. Compare the intended visible region after scaling before copying a number from an image editor into CSS.

At 0% the left edges align; at 100% the right edges align. At 50%, equal excess is cropped on both sides. These comparisons make it easier to detect a reversed assumption about which direction a larger percentage moves the visible window.

Recalculate after changing the box shape

Change the square to a wide rectangle, then to a portrait box. Measure the fitted dimensions again; the overflowing axis may change. Keep the same source while testing positioning so a responsive source swap does not confuse the result.

Use a separately composed image if the required subject cannot survive the crop. Positioning does not recover content outside the source or reduce the downloaded file size.

Choose the image fitting policy. Verify the selected source and natural dimensions.
coverAlt: A square viewport clips a wide illustrative image with a fifty pixel left offset; the arithmetic uses negative remaining space times twenty-five percent.

title: Request Fraction Glyphs Without Changing the Source Text
description: Compare diagonal and stacked fraction features in the actual font, limit styling to the intended values, and preserve the original text for copying.
body:
Font-variant-numeric can request diagonal or stacked fraction glyphs from a font that supports them. The property changes presentation, not the mathematical meaning or underlying characters. A declaration can be valid even when the selected font has no suitable alternate.

Keep the specimen and surrounding text separate

.fraction { font-variant-numeric: diagonal-fractions; }
.fraction.stacked { font-variant-numeric: stacked-fractions; }
.fraction.baseline { font-variant-numeric: normal; }

Render the same source string, such as 3/8, in three spans using the baseline, diagonal and stacked variants. Keep the family, size and weight identical. The CSS deliberately does not name a font: select a project font with documented support and inspect the actual rendered glyphs after it loads.

Reference: MDN CSS font fraction glyphs.

Limit the feature to actual fractions

A slash also appears in dates, paths and identifiers. Applying fraction styling to an entire metadata panel can change sequences that were never intended as arithmetic. Wrap the fraction itself and leave unrelated text under its normal numeric policy.

Do not substitute similar-looking Unicode characters solely to imitate a font feature. That can change copying, searching and downstream parsing. For a complex mathematical expression, typographic fraction alternates are not a replacement for suitable mathematical markup and an accessible explanation.

Compare fallback and reading-size behavior

Disable the web font and examine the fallback. The fraction should remain understandable as ordinary text if the alternate is unavailable. Check the smallest supported size, especially whether numerator and denominator remain legible. A compact stacked form can need more care than an ordinary slash.

Copy the specimen into a plain-text editor and confirm the intended source sequence. Record the font file and feature choice in the handoff so a future font replacement prompts another comparison rather than silently changing the typography.

Review another font-dependent numeric feature. Confirm the intended font loaded.
coverAlt: A source fraction 3 slash 8 is paired with a schematic stacked fraction; the diagram reminds readers that actual glyph support belongs to the font.

title: Compare Gradient Midpoints with an Explicit Color Space
description: Compare sRGB and Oklab gradients with identical stops, preserve a fallback, and record the interpolation space when handing off a color treatment.
body:
Two gradients can share their endpoint colors and still differ between those endpoints. The interpolation color space determines the path between the stops. Specify it when the intermediate colors are part of the design, and compare the complete rendered gradient rather than only its endpoint swatches.

Hold the stops constant while changing the space

.ramp {
  min-height: 5rem;
  background: linear-gradient(90deg, #bd392f, #1557c0);
}
@supports (background: linear-gradient(90deg in oklab, red, blue)) {
  .ramp.srgb { background: linear-gradient(90deg in srgb, #bd392f, #1557c0); }
  .ramp.oklab { background: linear-gradient(90deg in oklab, #bd392f, #1557c0); }
}

Place two ramps next to each other with the srgb and oklab classes. The older-syntax declaration supplies a fallback; the support query gates the explicit comparison. Keep their widths and stops identical so the midpoint difference comes from interpolation rather than changed geometry.

Reference: MDN CSS gradient color interpolation.

Record the color model with the values

A handoff containing only two hex colors is incomplete when the middle of the gradient matters. Include angle, stop positions and interpolation space. Polar spaces can also expose a hue-path choice, which is a separate decision from this rectangular-space comparison.

Do not describe Oklab as automatically accessible or visually correct. It offers a different interpolation model; the resulting colors still need review against the content and background. A pleasing midpoint can remain unsuitable behind small text.

Inspect the whole ramp under the actual content

Compare the fallback and both enhanced ramps at the intended size. Put the real heading or control over each, and examine where its letters cross the intermediate colors. Repeat after wrapping or resizing moves the content to another part of the ramp.

When exporting a static image, verify that the export reproduces the intended color treatment. A screenshot or image-tool preset with different interpolation settings may not match the CSS even when its endpoint labels look identical.

Inspect angles and stop positions. Keep gradient text readable without its effect.
coverAlt: Two gradient configuration cards share the same endpoint colors but identify sRGB and Oklab as different interpolation spaces; no measured midpoint is asserted.

title: Debug an Empty-State Selector That Whitespace Prevents
description: Inspect text nodes when :empty fails, compare comments and hidden children, and use explicit state when visual emptiness differs from DOM structure.
body:
An element can look empty while failing to match :empty. In current browser behavior, whitespace text nodes and child elements can prevent the match. The selector asks about DOM content, not whether a reader can see any pixels inside the box.

Compare three small containers

<div class="result" id="bare"></div>
<div class="result" id="space"> </div>
<div class="result" id="comment"><!-- placeholder --></div>
<style>
.result { min-height: 2rem; border: 1px solid; }
.result:empty { background: #e5f2eb; }
</style>

The bare and comment-only containers match; the space-containing one does not in current implementations. Inspect childNodes rather than only children, because children omits text nodes. A nested empty span also changes the structural test even if it contributes no visible text.

Reference: MDN CSS empty whitespace selector.

Define what empty means to this interface

A display:none child still exists in the DOM. Generated CSS content does not create a child node for this selector. Those differences make :empty a poor substitute for a richer application state such as “no search results after loading has finished.”

For a business state, set an explicit attribute or render a real status message from the application’s data. Keep loading, failed, filtered-out and truly absent results separate. A decorative background alone does not explain the empty state to a reader.

Test formatting and generated markup

Compare compact markup with a pretty-printed version that introduces a newline between tags. Repeat after a framework inserts an invisible wrapper or text node. Inspect the result in the browsers being supported because the selector’s specification and implementation behavior have differed around whitespace.

Do not strip meaningful spaces from user content simply to make a selector match. If formatting whitespace should be ignored by the product’s definition, calculate that state deliberately and keep the CSS selector aligned with it.

Refresh queries after DOM changes. Announce meaningful result states.
coverAlt: Three containers compare no child content, a whitespace text node and a comment; the bare and comment-only containers match the empty selector.

title: Limit a Component Rule to Its Direct Children
description: Use the child combinator to stop a rule reaching nested content, distinguish matching from inheritance, and document the markup contract before adding wrappers.
body:
A descendant selector reaches matching elements at any depth. The child combinator, written as >, limits the relationship to one DOM level. Use it when a component’s immediate structure is the intended target, while checking whether inherited properties still reach deeper content.

Compare direct and nested labels

<section class="review-card">
  <h2 class="label">Card title</h2>
  <div class="embedded"><h3 class="label">Embedded title</h3></div>
</section>
<style>
.review-card > .label { border-inline-start: 3px solid #1756a0; padding-inline-start: .75rem; }
</style>

The direct h2 receives the border and padding. The nested h3 does not match this selector. Replacing > with a space reaches both labels, which can explain styling that leaks into an embedded widget. The combinator itself does not add specificity.

Reference: MDN CSS child combinator nested components.

Separate matching from inherited values

A direct-child rule can still set an inherited property on a child that passes it to that child’s descendants. A font or color appearing deeper in the tree therefore does not prove the selector matched that deeper node. Inspect matched rules and inherited rules separately in DevTools.

This relationship is also a markup contract. Adding a wrapper between review-card and its title breaks the match even if the rendered arrangement looks unchanged. Decide whether the component needs a direct-child rule or a more explicit part class that survives such a wrapper.

Review nested and wrapped variants

Test the original card, a card containing another card and a variant with a title wrapper. Compare the exact nodes selected before changing specificity. If the title is meant to remain styled through wrappers, update the selector and structure together rather than piling on unrelated overrides.

Keep the selector as broad as the intended contract requires. A long chain of direct-child combinators can be just as brittle as an overly broad descendant rule when several implementation wrappers are involved.

Consider an explicit styling scope. Trace matching and cascade precedence.
coverAlt: A direct label and a nested label occupy different levels in a component tree, with only the direct label matching the child combinator.

title: Compare CSS Zoom with Transform Scaling in Layout
description: Compare CSS zoom and transform scale using fixed-size specimens, inspect neighboring layout, and keep component magnification separate from browser zoom testing.
body:
CSS zoom magnifies an element in a way that can affect surrounding layout. Transform scaling changes its visual rendering while preserving its original layout allocation. Neither operation is equivalent to testing the whole interface with the reader’s browser zoom controls.

Compare identical boxes with a following element

.sample { width: 120px; height: 80px; background: #dceaff; }
.zoomed { zoom: 1.5; }
.scaled { transform: scale(1.5); transform-origin: top left; }
.after { background: #e5f2eb; }

Put each sample in its own block container followed by an after paragraph with margins removed. Both specimens appear enlarged, but the following paragraph exposes the layout difference. The explicit top-left transform origin makes the visual comparison easier without implying that zoom uses that same origin.

Reference: MDN CSS zoom versus transform scale.

Inspect layout and visual coordinates together

Measure the rendered rectangles and the position of each following paragraph. The transformed box can overlap space occupied by its neighbor because the original allocation remains. Zoom may change how much room the layout gives the box. Avoid comparing only a screenshot of the colored rectangle.

For a preview canvas, choose magnification based on whether surrounding controls should reflow or remain fixed. Test pointer interaction and overlays in the same coordinate system as the displayed content. A coordinate value from unscaled source content may need conversion before positioning an overlay.

Keep reader-controlled zoom available

Do not use CSS zoom to force a desktop layout into a narrow screen or to counteract a user’s enlarged view. Responsive sizing and readable content are separate requirements. Test actual browser zoom and text enlargement after choosing any component-specific preview scale.

Compare the target browsers and an unzoomed fallback. Record the magnification policy in the component’s interface contract, especially if measurements, hit targets or screenshots are exported from the preview.

Inspect transform layout allocation. Review actual browser zoom and reflow.
coverAlt: A zoomed box reserves additional space before its following content, while a transformed box visually overlaps the unchanged layout position of its following content.

title: Clone Template Controls Without Duplicating Their IDs
description: Instantiate an HTML template with unique control IDs, preserve label associations, and distinguish cloning content from moving the reusable fragment.
body:
A template holds reusable markup without rendering that ordinary template content into the page. Clone its content when creating an instance, then assign instance-specific IDs before insertion. Reusing the same control ID can make labels target the wrong field.

Generate each control relationship together

<template id="note-template">
  <div class="note-row"><label>Review note</label><input type="text"></div>
</template>
<div id="notes"></div>
<script>
let nextNote = 0;
function addNote() {
  const fragment = document.querySelector('#note-template').content.cloneNode(true);
  const input = fragment.querySelector('input');
  const label = fragment.querySelector('label');
  input.id = `review-note-${++nextNote}`;
  label.htmlFor = input.id;
  document.querySelector('#notes').append(fragment);
}
addNote();
addNote();
</script>

This page-owned counter gives the two new inputs different IDs and links each label to its own input. Reserve the review-note prefix for this component or use an application-wide ID strategy if other code can create the same IDs.

Reference: MDN HTML template clone unique IDs.

Distinguish copying from consuming the fragment

Appending the original template.content moves its children out of that fragment. A later attempt can then find no reusable children. Clone first when the template is intended to remain a reusable source.

A deep clone copies the element tree and attributes, including unwanted duplicate IDs already present in that tree. It does not copy listeners registered with addEventListener. Attach instance behavior after creation or use a suitably scoped delegated listener.

Test two instances before shipping one

Click each visible label and verify the corresponding input receives focus. Check that every document ID remains unique after repeated insertion and removal. Add any describedby or labelledby references to the same instance-specific naming plan.

Keep dynamic user values as text or control values rather than interpolating them into an HTML string. This example creates fields only; saving, validation and removal are separate behaviors to implement explicitly.

Keep control labels persistent. Scope delegated component actions.
coverAlt: A reusable template creates two review fields with different input IDs and matching label references.

title: Choose DOM Text or Rendered Text for an Inspection
description: Compare textContent and innerText with hidden content and line breaks, avoid treating either as an accessible name, and write plain text without parsing markup.
body:
TextContent reads a node’s text content without using its rendered layout. InnerText reflects rendered-text behavior, including relevant visibility and line breaks. Choose the representation that answers the inspection question instead of treating the two values as interchangeable.

Compare a visible label and a hidden note

<div id="specimen">Visible label<span hidden>Internal note</span><br>Second line</div>
<script>
const specimen = document.querySelector('#specimen');
console.log(specimen.textContent);
console.log(specimen.innerText);
</script>

For this rendered element, textContent includes the hidden note and does not turn the br element into a newline character by itself. InnerText excludes the hidden span and reflects the line break. Keep the specimen attached and visible; innerText on a non-rendered element can behave differently.

Reference: MDN textContent versus innerText.

Name the representation in the review evidence

A DOM-text inventory can be useful for checking source content, while a rendered-text comparison can help explain what is presented in a particular state. Neither is a substitute for the accessible-name calculation: labels, ARIA relationships and other semantics can change what assistive technology receives.

Reading innerText can require layout work. Avoid repeatedly reading it inside a large mutation loop when the task only needs source text. Collect the necessary evidence once under controlled styles and viewport conditions.

Write plain text deliberately

Use textContent when placing a plain string into a dedicated output node. It does not parse that string as HTML. Remember that assigning it replaces the node’s children, so do not apply it to a wrapper containing controls or markup that must survive.

Try text containing angle brackets, a hidden child and several lines. Document whether the expected result preserves DOM characters, rendered line breaks or an accessible label; otherwise two correct implementations can appear to disagree.

Inspect accessible names separately. Record the styles affecting presentation.
coverAlt: A DOM text inspection includes a hidden note, while a rendered-text inspection omits it and preserves a visible line break.

title: Measure the Separate Fragments of a Wrapped Inline Element
description: Use getClientRects for a wrapped inline label, compare the union box, and avoid mistaking border-box fragments for exact glyph or line measurements.
body:
A wrapped inline element can occupy several rectangular fragments. GetClientRects exposes those border-box rectangles, while getBoundingClientRect gives an enclosing rectangle. The enclosing area can include space where the inline element has no visible content.

Measure an inline specimen after layout

<p style="width:180px;font:20px/1.5 sans-serif">
  <span id="wrapped">Inspect the spacing around this long inline label.</span>
</p>
<script>
const label = document.querySelector('#wrapped');
console.table([...label.getClientRects()].map(r => ({
  x: r.x, y: r.y, width: r.width, height: r.height
})));
console.log(label.getBoundingClientRect());
</script>

The span remains inline and wraps inside the paragraph. Several rectangles can describe its fragments. If you change it to an inline-block, the box model changes; the same method should not be expected to expose every line inside that single box.

Reference: MDN getClientRects wrapped inline fragments.

Keep the measurement’s meaning narrow

These are box rectangles, not tight outlines around each glyph. Complex inline content, bidirectional text and nested markup can make a simplistic “one rectangle equals one text line” assumption unreliable. Record the markup and layout context with the numbers.

The coordinates are relative to the viewport and can change with scrolling. An overlay positioned in document coordinates needs an appropriate conversion. Re-measure after relevant font, container or content changes instead of treating the first result as permanent.

Compare fragments with the enclosing rectangle

Draw temporary outlines for each fragment and a separate outline for the bounding rectangle. Narrow the paragraph and observe which parts change. Compare a short last line with the preceding longer lines to see why a single enclosing rectangle can overstate the occupied area.

Use the rectangles as diagnostic evidence for an annotation or selection design. Test the actual interactive target separately; geometric fragments alone do not certify that every intended point activates the expected control.

Compare visual bounds and layout width. Wait for the relevant font-loading phase.
coverAlt: Three inline fragment rectangles sit inside one enclosing rectangle, showing empty space included by the union of the fragments.

title: Find Which Element Wins a Pointer Hit Test
description: Probe viewport coordinates with elementFromPoint, inspect overlay interception, and separate pointer hit testing from keyboard focus and accessibility.
body:
When a visible button will not respond, elementFromPoint can identify the topmost hit-testable element at a chosen viewport coordinate. It helps investigate an intercepting overlay, but it does not explain every reason a click handler fails.

Probe a point inside the visible button

const button = document.querySelector('#save-review');
if (button) {
  const rect = button.getBoundingClientRect();
  const x = rect.left + rect.width / 2;
  const y = rect.top + rect.height / 2;
  const hit = document.elementFromPoint(x, y);
  console.log({ hit, insideButton: hit !== null && button.contains(hit) });
}

Run this after bringing the button into the viewport. A nested icon or label can be the returned element, so the containment check is more useful than requiring hit === button. A clipped or partly covered button may need probes at several visible points rather than only its bounding-box center.

Reference: MDN elementFromPoint pointer hit testing.

Trace the returned element before changing z-index

If an unrelated overlay wins the test, inspect its bounds, stacking context and pointer-events value. Elements with pointer-events:none are skipped by this API. Removing hit testing from a decorative layer may be appropriate, while an intentional modal backdrop needs different behavior.

The coordinates are viewport-relative. Passing document coordinates without accounting for scrolling can inspect the wrong location. A point outside the viewport can return null, and a hit inside another document can return its iframe element rather than an internal descendant.

Check the rest of the interaction path

After fixing an unintended interception, activate the control by pointer and keyboard. Check disabled state, event listeners and navigation behavior separately if it still does nothing. The hit-test result alone does not establish focusability or an accessible name.

Record the viewport, scroll position and chosen point with the returned node. This makes a bug report more actionable than a statement that “the button is under something,” especially when the obstruction changes at a breakpoint.

Review decorative overlay hit testing. Trace the relevant stacking context.
coverAlt: A hit-test point falls on a translucent overlay covering part of a button, illustrating how visible content and pointer interception can differ.

title: Remove a Component’s Event Listeners with One Abort Signal
description: Group temporary event listeners under an AbortController, return a cleanup function, and prevent repeated mounting from multiplying interface responses.
body:
A component that attaches listeners each time it opens can accumulate duplicate responses if it never removes them. Passing an AbortSignal when registering listeners gives that component instance a shared cleanup mechanism. Abort the controller when that instance is disposed.

Return cleanup from the mounting function

function mountReview(root) {
  const controller = new AbortController();
  const button = root.querySelector('button');
  const status = root.querySelector('[role="status"]');
  let count = 0;
  button.addEventListener('click', () => {
    status.textContent = `Review count: ${++count}`;
  }, { signal: controller.signal });
  return () => controller.abort();
}

Provide a root containing the button and status element. Save the returned function and call it before replacing or remounting that instance. The local count makes repeated activation easy to observe; it is an illustrative interaction, not persistent review data.

Reference: MDN AbortController event listener cleanup.

Keep the controller’s lifetime aligned with the component

An aborted signal remains aborted. Create a new controller for a new mount instead of trying to reuse the disposed instance’s signal. A signal shared across unrelated components can remove listeners that should remain active, so choose the ownership boundary deliberately.

Removing a listener does not undo work it already started. A timer, observer or pending task created by the handler may need its own cleanup. Likewise, aborting listeners does not automatically remove the component’s DOM.

Test disposal and remounting explicitly

Activate the button twice, run cleanup, then activate it again and confirm the old listener no longer updates the status. Mount a fresh instance and check that one activation produces one response. Repeat this cycle several times.

Use a real action outcome or a diagnostic counter when looking for duplicates; an idempotent class toggle can hide multiple handler executions. Keep a separate policy for one-time listeners when once:true is the intended behavior instead of a component lifetime.

Scope event delegation to a component. Disconnect temporary DOM observers.
coverAlt: An event-listener lifecycle moves from mount to interaction to abort, with a new controller required for the next component instance.

title: Add Optional Break Points to a Long Label with wbr
description: Use wbr for chosen line-break opportunities, distinguish it from br and soft hyphens, and preserve the actual label text when readers copy it.
body:
Wbr marks a place where a line may break if needed. It does not force a new line like br and does not add a visible hyphen. Use it when a long machine-oriented label has meaningful boundaries that automatic wrapping does not express well.

Keep the label’s characters intact

<p class="asset-name">component<wbr>Preview<wbr>Desktop<wbr>2026.svg</p>
<style>
.asset-name { max-inline-size: 12rem; font-family: monospace; }
</style>

The source word can wrap between the chosen segments when the box becomes narrow. In a wide box, the optional opportunities need not produce breaks. There is no inserted space or hyphen between Preview and Desktop; wbr is a structural opportunity rather than an extra filename character.

Reference: MDN HTML wbr optional line breaks.

Choose the appropriate breaking mechanism

A br expresses an intentional line break, which is stronger than a responsive opportunity. A soft hyphen can show a hyphen when breaking a word. Overflow-wrap supplies a broader emergency policy for arbitrary content, while wbr lets an author identify preferred boundaries in a known string.

Do not insert hundreds of opportunities into ordinary prose to compensate for a poor text measure. For user-generated identifiers, decide which delimiters are meaningful and preserve the original value used for links, downloads and copying.

Review both wide and very narrow boxes

Resize the specimen until each boundary is exercised, then copy the rendered label into a plain-text editor and compare it with the real filename. Check screen-reader pronunciation if the label is an important control name; visual grouping is not a guaranteed spoken pause.

A segment can still be wider than the available box. Decide whether that case should allow emergency wrapping, local scrolling or a separately accessible full value. Optional breaks solve a placement question, not every overflow or truncation requirement.

Choose an emergency wrapping policy. Preserve access to truncated values.
coverAlt: A long asset label has optional break positions between component, Preview, Desktop and a file suffix, without adding filename characters.

title: Reuse SVG Geometry with symbol and use
description: Define an SVG symbol once, instantiate it with use, preserve viewBox and currentColor behavior, and give each surrounding control a clear name.
body:
Symbol defines reusable SVG geometry; use creates a rendered instance that refers to it. Keep the geometry separate from each instance’s meaning. A repeated decorative icon inside labeled buttons should not introduce a second competing accessible name.

Define one symbol and use it in a labeled action

<svg width="0" height="0" aria-hidden="true" style="position:absolute">
  <symbol id="review-check-icon" viewBox="0 0 24 24">
    <path d="M5 12l4 4L19 6" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2"/>
  </symbol>
</svg>
<button type="button">
  <svg width="24" height="24" aria-hidden="true" focusable="false">
    <use href="#review-check-icon"/>
  </svg>
  Mark reviewed
</button>

The symbol itself is not the visible instance. The use reference instantiates its geometry inside the button’s SVG. The visible text names the button, and the icon follows the inherited color through currentColor. This example does not implement the button’s review action.

Reference: MDN SVG symbol use icons.

Keep references and styling predictable

Use a document-unique symbol ID. A repeated component should reuse the definition rather than inject another conflicting definition with the same ID. Hard-coded fill or stroke values on the source geometry can prevent the instance from following the intended color.

Do not assume a normal descendant selector on use can style every internal referenced node like ordinary light-DOM markup. Set appropriate inherited values or design an explicit source styling contract. External sprite files add URL, origin and loading considerations beyond this same-document example.

Test the instance, not only the definition

Render the icon at two sizes and in two color contexts. Confirm the viewBox keeps the shape inside the expected area and that the button’s accessible name comes from its visible label. Check forced colors and a missing reference so the action remains understandable without the picture.

For an informative standalone graphic, provide an accessible name on the instance using a pattern tested with the supported browser and assistive technology. Reusing geometry does not automatically supply an appropriate name everywhere it appears.

Connect icon color to text. Name an informative SVG instance.
coverAlt: One checkmark symbol definition supplies two rendered icon instances while the surrounding controls keep their own visible labels.

title: Normalize SVG Stroke Dashes with pathLength
description: Use pathLength to express dash distances on a known scale, avoid percentage-unit surprises, and separate illustrative stroke geometry from progress semantics.
body:
PathLength lets an SVG shape calibrate distance calculations against an author-defined length. With pathLength="100", unitless dash lengths can use a convenient 0–100 scale even when the geometric path has another length. This calibration does not resize the shape itself.

Draw an illustrative sixty-unit segment

<svg viewBox="0 0 120 120" width="160" height="160"
     role="img" aria-label="Illustrative ring with sixty of one hundred units drawn">
  <circle cx="60" cy="60" r="45" fill="none" stroke="#dce1e9" stroke-width="8"/>
  <circle cx="60" cy="60" r="45" pathLength="100" fill="none"
          stroke="#1756a0" stroke-width="8" stroke-linecap="butt"
          stroke-dasharray="60 40" transform="rotate(-90 60 60)"/>
</svg>

The dash and gap sum to 100 author units, giving one cycle around this closed path. The rotation moves the starting position to the top. The image is an arithmetic specimen, not a measured task-completion result.

Reference: MDN SVG pathLength stroke dasharray.

Keep units and visible caps separate

Use unitless values for this normalized comparison. Percentage dash values have a different reference and should not be assumed to mean a percentage of the path’s length. Inspect the property’s unit rules before converting a number into a percent string.

Rounded line caps extend the visible ends of a dash beyond its centerline segment. A ring with round caps can therefore look slightly fuller than the same numerical dash with butt caps. Use the cap style that matches the visual requirement and explain it in a precise comparison.

Connect real values to appropriate semantics

Try values of zero, sixty and one hundred, then resize the SVG. Verify the shape remains stable and the intended segment changes. Check the start angle and any dash offset independently; both can change what the ring appears to represent.

If the graphic becomes a real progress indicator, expose the task’s label and actual value through suitable semantics and visible text. A colored arc with a normalized length alone does not tell assistive technology what is progressing or whether the task has completed.

Review the visible effect of line caps. Choose value or progress semantics.
coverAlt: An illustrative ring draws sixty of one hundred normalized units with butt caps; the diagram distinguishes normalized dash values from actual task progress.

title: Mark Product Names for Translation Without Freezing the Sentence
description: Use translate=no on stable names or identifiers, preserve translatable surrounding copy, and distinguish localization guidance from language metadata.
body:
The translate attribute tells localization tools whether text and translatable attributes should be translated. Use translate="no" for a stable product name or exact identifier when that matches the content policy. Keep the surrounding instruction available for translation.

Mark the smallest meaningful range

<p>Open <span translate="no">Penta AI</span> to inspect the page.</p>
<p>Keep the token name <code translate="no">--surface-panel</code> unchanged.</p>

The product name and token are protected ranges; the explanatory sentences are not. This expresses an editorial intention to translation tools. It does not run a translation service or guarantee identical behavior in every tool.

Reference: MDN HTML translate no product names.

Separate translation policy from language

Lang identifies a language for pronunciation and other language-sensitive behavior. Translate controls a localization decision. A name can need both a known language and a no-translation policy; one attribute is not a replacement for the other.

The translate value can be inherited. A broad no value on a wrapper may accidentally freeze help text, button instructions or error messages. Use yes on an appropriate descendant when it must remain translatable within a protected region, or narrow the original protected range.

Review the localized page as a whole

Test the page with the actual translation workflow the product supports. Check whether the protected spelling survives, the surrounding sentence is grammatical and the longer translated text still fits. Do not infer translation quality from the presence of the attribute alone.

Keep a short content policy listing which names, code tokens and identifiers remain stable. Some product terms may have official localized names, so a blanket rule that all branded words must stay unchanged can be wrong. Review titles and tooltips as well as visible body text where those attributes carry translatable content.

Declare content language separately. Review unknown-direction text.
coverAlt: Penta AI and a code token are marked as stable text within otherwise translatable instructions, with language metadata treated separately.

title: Give a Data Table Its Own Caption and Scope
description: Use a table caption to identify the dataset and its scope, keep header relationships intact, and verify the table’s accessible name after styling changes.
body:
A caption identifies the table it belongs to. It can make the dataset understandable when readers navigate directly to the table rather than reading the preceding paragraph. Write the caption around what the data represents, including the context needed to interpret it.

Identify an explicitly illustrative inventory

<table>
  <caption>Illustrative component inventory for a sample landing page</caption>
  <thead><tr><th scope="col">Component</th><th scope="col">Count</th></tr></thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr><th scope="row">Primary action</th><td>2</td></tr>
    <tr><th scope="row">Feature card</th><td>3</td></tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

The small dataset is invented for the example. The caption states its scope rather than implying a measured Penta AI result. Place the caption as the table’s first child; row and column headers still supply the relationships for individual values.

Reference: MDN HTML table caption context.

Keep a caption distinct from nearby headings

A section heading can introduce several tables or explain a broader subject. It is not automatically the caption of each table beneath it. Give each table enough context to be distinguished when encountered on its own, without repeating an entire preceding paragraph.

Caption-side can move the visible caption below a table without moving the element outside the table. Visual position and semantic association are separate. If the caption is hidden for a design reason, verify that the intended naming and visible context remain useful rather than assuming any hiding technique is harmless.

Check the name and the reading path

Inspect the table in the accessibility tree and confirm the expected caption contributes to its name or description under the chosen markup. Avoid adding competing ARIA labels without checking which text wins. Read a few cells with the supported assistive technology to verify headers as a separate concern.

Test a long caption on mobile and in print. Keep units, time period and any necessary data limitations available where readers need them. A good caption explains the dataset’s identity; it does not repair missing header associations or an unusable overflow layout.

Contain table overflow on small screens. Associate complex headers with cells.
coverAlt: A table caption identifies an illustrative landing-page inventory, followed by clear Component and Count column headers and two example rows.

title: Choose Cursor Feedback That Matches the Real Interaction
description: Use cursor keywords and custom-image fallbacks deliberately, inspect inherited cursor rules, and keep unavailable or draggable behavior in the interaction code.
body:
A cursor communicates a pointer interaction; it does not implement that interaction. Setting not-allowed does not disable a button, and grab does not make an element draggable. Review the cursor together with the control’s real behavior and visible state.

Keep a usable keyword fallback

.inspect-surface {
  cursor: url("/assets/inspect-cursor.png") 8 8, crosshair;
}
.inspect-surface.is-panning { cursor: grabbing; }
button:disabled { cursor: not-allowed; }

The image URL is a project placeholder that must be replaced with a real cursor asset before use. The 8 8 hotspot identifies the active point within that image. If the image cannot be used, the final crosshair keyword supplies a fallback. The is-panning class needs real interaction code to manage it.

Reference: MDN CSS cursor fallback interaction.

Check inherited and native cursor behavior

Cursor is inherited, so a broad rule on a wrapper can reach nested text or controls. A crosshair covering an editable field can communicate the wrong action. Inspect the actual hit-tested element and its computed cursor before changing a global style.

Browsers impose limits on custom cursor image sizes and supported formats. Keep the asset small and test the target platforms rather than assuming an arbitrary SVG or large bitmap will work everywhere. Touch interfaces may have no mouse cursor at all.

Test unavailable assets and interrupted interactions

Block the custom image and confirm the keyword fallback remains sensible. Move the pointer over nested controls and verify text selection, links and buttons still communicate their expected interactions. Test a panning cancellation so the grabbing state does not remain after the operation ends.

For an unavailable action, pair the appropriate native disabled state or deliberate accessible disabled behavior with an explanation where needed. Never rely on the cursor as the only indication: keyboard and touch users need the same underlying state and usable feedback.

Implement a discoverable unavailable action. Inspect the element receiving pointer hits.
coverAlt: A cursor image uses an explicit hotspot and falls back to a crosshair, while the diagram states that cursor styling does not implement the action.

title: Find Why a Web Component’s Slot Fallback Disappeared
description: Inspect assigned slot nodes when fallback content vanishes, distinguish named and default slots, and review whitespace without deleting meaningful user text.
body:
A slot displays its fallback when no content is assigned to it. Assigned content can exist without producing obvious visible text. Inspect the slot’s assigned nodes before assuming that a hidden fallback is a styling problem.

Compare a default slot with and without text nodes

<div id="slot-demo"></div>
<script>
const host = document.querySelector('#slot-demo');
const root = host.attachShadow({ mode: 'open' });
root.innerHTML = '<slot>Default review label</slot>';
const slot = root.querySelector('slot');
console.log(slot.assignedNodes().length); // 0
host.append(document.createTextNode(' '));
console.log(slot.assignedNodes().length); // 1
</script>

The fixed shadow markup is a trusted literal for this specimen. The whitespace text node is assigned to the default slot, suppressing its fallback even though it may look blank. This does not mean ordinary formatting whitespace should always be removed from production content.

Reference: MDN HTML slot fallback assigned nodes.

Inspect the assignment contract

A named slot receives matching slottable content through the slot attribute, while the unnamed default slot receives appropriate unassigned content. Check the attribute spelling and inspect assignedNodes rather than only assignedElements when text nodes may matter.

A populated light-DOM element can be assigned and then visually hidden by styling. Fallback does not automatically reappear just because that assigned element becomes display:none. The distinction is assignment, not the final pixel output.

Test empty, whitespace and named variants

Remove the text node and confirm the fallback returns. Add a visible span, then change it to a named assignment and inspect which slot receives it. Use a slotchange listener if the component needs to react to assignment changes, while remembering that arbitrary edits inside an already assigned node are a different observation problem.

Document whether a component requires explicit content or offers a meaningful default. Keep fallback labels understandable and check the final accessible name of controls using slotted text. A visually blank slot can also leave an action without a useful name.

Inspect shadow and light DOM separately. Observe relevant DOM changes deliberately.
coverAlt: An unassigned slot displays its fallback, while an assigned whitespace text node suppresses the fallback despite looking blank.
